News.title: UK plague of drugs to your door with slick menus & even ‘club card’ loyalty schemes shipped straight to your street
News.content:
SPECIAL DELIVERY UK plague of drugs to your door with slick menus & even ‘club card’ loyalty schemes shipped straight to your street







Next

BRAZEN drug dealers are selling illegal substances on glossy websites, offering discount codes, rewards schemes, and boasting tracked Royal Mail delivery straight to customers’ front doors.

A Sun investigation found a number of UK websites offering recreational drugs displayed with slick “menus”, reviews, newsletters, customer service chatbots and even club card style points systems.



Gone are the days of dark alleyway deals, users can now purchase illegal drugs from the comfort of their own sofa, just like doing an online food shop.

The Sun was able to purchase cannabis from one of these sites, which was delivered via the Royal Mail in discreet, airtight packaging.



Our reporter was instructed to pay into a UK bank account which used the name of a micro company registered at Companies House.

Its declared business activities include ‘Retail sale via mail order houses or via Internet’.

Insiders say these websites fall through the cracks between different authorities, with the National Crime Agency (NCA) directing The Sun to Ofcom, while the regulator insists standalone drug-dealing websites are a matter for the police.

And unlike the dark web, these sites are easily found on Google, with little to stop a child bypassing age verification checks by simply clicking a button claiming they are over 18.

Nearly all of those which The Sun investigated wanted to be paid in cryptocurrencies, but made exceptions for orders over £100.

But for those tempted to engage in this modern and illegal digital drug trade, the online Wild West is likely to be just as dangerous and untrustworthy.



A cyber-security expert told The Sun that some of the we investigated websites were “full of malware” which could be used to gain unauthorised access to buyers’ computers or data.



Our investigation also encountered two fraudulent gangs which attempted to con customers by taking payments but then sent users to a supposed delivery company which asked for an additional £150 issuance fee.

The courier website appeared to resemble a major logistics company, but most of its pages simply redirected users back to the homepage or displayed links which didn’t work.

These dealers, who likely also ran the supposed logistics site, would then direct potential users to a private Telegram channel, where they would send daily ‘menus’ to a group of around 250 users.

But a month later, the Telegram channel was no longer available after a notification showed users it had violated the messaging app’s terms of service.

When The Sun confronted these dealers and the sham delivery company, they both wanted fees to respond to our claims.



Carefree customers even leave reviews on these sites for other users to read, while others rate the service as a whole on Trustpilot.

The scale of the problem has been laid bare by police forces across the country, which in recent months have launched numerous operations to prevent drugs at the border from reaching their intended destinations.



Greater Manchester Police said it intercepted more than 2,800 parcels containing over 2.7 tonnes of cannabis from entering the region in 2025.

While Essex Police said it prevented over 400 packages containing cannabis at the border in the first three months of last year.

And Dorset’s Police and Crime Commissioner told MPs in July his force had intercepted 44 parcels containing £500,000 worth of drugs in the first three months of the year.

But it is unclear how many parcels containing illegal drugs — which are already in the country — are intercepted by law enforcement agencies within the postal network.



While authorities and technology companies crack down on individuals promoting and selling illegal drugs on social media, websites dedicated to dealing them remain accessible, raising questions about why they are allowed to continue operating.



Ofcom can fine websites that breach the Online Safety Act and seek court orders to block access to them in the UK, but its powers only cover services regulated under the Act and it cannot directly shut down websites.

An Ofcom spokesperson said: “Websites run by drug dealers to sell illegal drugs directly to people aren’t covered by the Online Safety Act and are a matter for the police.

“But social media sites and apps in scope of the Act must remove illegal drug-selling content posted by their users as soon as it’s reported to them, and take steps to stop people in the UK seeing it in the first place. Search services must also minimise the risk of people ending up on these websites.



“Where tech firms fail to comply with their duties under the Act, we’ve shown we’ll take action. We’ve already launched investigations into more than 100 websites and handed out more than £7million in fines.

“We’ll continue to play our part – acting within the scope of our powers – in support of action from police and other law enforcement agencies to tackle this illegal practice.”

A National Crime Agency spokesman said: “Many organised crime groups selling drugs use social media and communication platforms to promote and sell their illicit produce.

“The NCA is working with partners across law enforcement and government to tackle drug trafficking.



“Social media and technology companies also need to work to ensure that crime networks are stopped from being able to exploit their sites and platforms for criminal gain. Technology companies, including social media platforms, have a responsibility to create the safest possible environment for their customers by not enabling criminality such as drug trafficking.

“We continue to work with the technology industry to enable law enforcement to identify offenders who exploit the platforms for criminal gain, and to protect the public.”

A Royal Mail spokesperson said: “We work closely with police, Border Force and other law enforcement agencies to prevent criminal gangs from misusing the postal network. This includes sharing intelligence to support their investigations and assist in their interception of illegal items.

“Royal Mail is legally obligated not to open post. However, we routinely report suspicious items to the relevant authorities for further inspection.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Government spokesperson said: “Online platforms are required by law to clamp down on the sale of illegal drugs immediately and robustly. Those that fail to comply face significant enforcement action.

“The National Crime Agency is working in partnership with policing colleagues across the UK and internationally to help map and target key offenders operating online, including the darknet markets.”

News.title: Murder suspect ‘knew’ victim found ‘partially in wheelie bin’ in service lane near UK beauty spot – as man in 30s held
News.content:
'MURDER' PROBE Murder suspect ‘knew’ victim found ‘partially in wheelie bin’ in service lane near UK beauty spot – as man in 30s held







Next

A SUSPECT being held for murder after a man was found dead in a wheelie-bin is thought to have known the victim, cops said.

The victim was found “partially within a wheelie bin” with stab wounds on Wednesday morning in Plymouth.



The grim discovery was made around 6.40am in a service lane off Grand Parade in the West Hoe area of the city.

The victim, in his 50s, was pronounced dead at the scene, Devon and Cornwall police said.



A man in his 30s was subsequently arrested on suspicion of murder and remains in police custody.

Officers have now said they believe the suspect may have known the deceased.



The force were granted a warrant of further detention of the man for 36 hours, at Plymouth Magistrates Court on Friday, in order to continue their questioning.

Detective Inspector Chris Lithgow said: “A large-scale investigation is continuing at pace with a significant number of witness, CCTV, house-to-house and search enquiries taking place.



“We understand this is a concerning incident for the community, and every effort is being made to establish the circumstances surrounding this death.

“A suspect remains in police custody as our investigation continues.

“The suspect and victim are believed to be known to each other and we are keeping an open mind as to any motive.

“We are asking members of the public to help our investigation by avoiding speculation, and by not sharing any unconfirmed information online.”

The deceased man is yet to be formally identified.



Any relevant information, images or footage can be reported through Devon and Cornwall Police’s major incident public portal, or by telephone on 101, or on the force website quoting reference 50260282293.

News.title: Ukrainian troops sneaked into Russian lines through underground gas pipes in brazen op that left 100 Putin soldiers dead
News.content:
Next

UKRAINIAN soldiers have snuck nine miles through underground gas pipes to ambush and kill more than 100 Russian troops in an audacious “whack-a-mole” mission, Kyiv said.

Volodymyr Zelensky‘s fierce fighters crawled for miles through pitch-black disused tunnels to emerge behind enemy lines in an incredible subterranean assault in the Kupiansk, Kharkiv.



The operation, codenamed Veles after a Slavic god of the underworld, saw Ukraine‘s Khartiia National Guard corps kill 100 of Mad Vlad’s desperate lads and capture 30 more.

Troops secretly penetrated more than nine miles into Russian-held territory, advancing through dark disused tunnels without GPS or reliable radio communications.



They came within yards of enemy soldiers, sending mines to fight bitter battles in cramped close contact conditions.

The soldiers then emerged to launch coordinated attacks on the Russians, working with forces advancing above ground and combat drones.



Corps Commander Ihor Obolienskyi said: “The Russians believed that underground tunnels were a tool they alone could use to bypass our defences.

“We studied their experience, beat them at their own game and turned this threat into an advantage for our counteroffensive.”

The Ukrainians endured brutal conditions, crawling through four-foot wide pipes beneath the battlefield.

Troops from Ukraine’s 425th Separate Assault Regiment carried out a separate mission, Operation Impossible, to push Russian forces from another section of the maze-like gas pipeline network.



They spent days unable to stand up, crawling through filthy pipes, sleeping below ground and attacking enemy underground machine gun positions.

One Ukrainian soldier revealed he had crawled three miles to reach his position, spending three days in the tunnels.

He said: “You’re living inside this pipe – about ten guys, all packed in like a train.



“Just mud, mud, mud – everything is filthy. Just a mess. Pure mud. A grim brotherhood of arms.”

Another exhausted soldier said they suffered freezing conditions, had to drink filthy water and struggled to breathe underground.

He said: “For several days, we were constantly in a horizontal position, so the first thing we wanted to do after getting out was simply stand up.”

Ukrainians deployed battery-powered vehicles to carrying around ten men through the pipes.

The smell of gas and decomposing bodies was so overpowering that soldiers’ uniforms had to be washed in vinegar repeatedly.



The canny operation to use gas pipelines to bypass minefields turned a Russian tactic on its head.

Putin’s forces had lurked in the tunnels for months.

But whenever Ukrainian forces destroyed an exit, the Russians dug another.

Khartiia spokesman Volodymyr Dehtyarov said it was “like whack-a-mole”.

Eventually commanders opted to take the fight into the pipes and launched the incredible underground advance.



Commander of Ukraine’s Khartiia 2nd Corps Brigadier-General Ihor Obolenskyi said his men had turned Russia‘s own infiltration tactics against them.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said: “The Russians intended to use these gas pipelines to infiltrate our rear. So we went underground ourselves.”

News.title: Met Office issues new weather warning as Storm Boelo batters UK with 56mph gusts and lashing heavy rain
News.content:
BOEL-ED OVER Met Office issues new weather warning as Storm Boelo batters UK with 56mph gusts and lashing heavy rain







Next

THE Met Office has issued a fresh weather warning as Britain is battered by Storm Boelo.

Heavy rain will lash across the UK’s western and southern coasts until late tonight – as Brits have been warned to stay indoors this weekend amid forecasts of torrential downpours and 56mph winds.



The latest yellow warning, for rain, is in place for 12 hours until 11pm on Saturday – and could result in flooding with more than two inches expected to fall in parts.

The weather didn’t, however, stop those attending the Otley Run pub crawl in Leeds in full fancy dress.



Meanwhile, departure boards at Stansted Mountfitchet, Essex, show all trains between London and Stansted Airport are cancelled, after a tree fell on the railway.

The national weather agency’s warning states: “Heavy rain in association with Storm Boelo is expected to lead to surface water flooding in places.



“25-30mm is expected widely across the warning area during this time, with a few places such as upland areas seeing 50-60mm, and some of this perhaps falling within 6 hours.

“Rain will ease for a time through the evening, but this will be followed by another intense band of heavy rain following in from the west, before the whole system clears away eastward to bring a clear night with a few scattered showers following on.”

Brits have been warned to stay indoors this weekend during a second consecutive storm to sweep the nation after Storm Austen, the first of the season.



An amber warning for wind is also in place from 9pm tonight until 9pm tomorrow across Scotland and much of the north east of England, bringing 80mph winds.

Yellow weather warnings have been issued for the whole of mainland Scotland, the Western Isles, Orkney and the far north of England from 12pm on Saturday to 9pm on Sunday.

There will be “widespread gusts” of 55-65mph widely, with these reaching up to 70-80mph in more exposed coastal locations, the Met Office added.



A separate yellow warning for wind, covering Northern Ireland from 10am on Saturday to 12pm on Sunday, predicts gusts of 50-60mph, with up to 65-75mph in exposed regions.

Met Office Deputy Chief Forecaster Chris Bulmer, said: “Gusts of 70-80mph in exposed coastal areas and high ground are possible, with 50-60mph gusts more widely.

“The strong winds will be accompanied by heavy rain, making for an impactful weekend of weather.”

The disruption is expected to last through Sunday, bringing difficult travel conditions and potential building damage.

It comes after Storm Austin hit the UK on Friday with yellow weather warnings covering swathes of the country and bringing travel chaos ahead of the half-term holidays.



Austen battered England with gusts of up to 80mph, and “danger to life” warnings were issued by the Met Office.

Flights, ferries and train journeys were cancelled or delayed as the storm battered the UK on Friday.

Drivers in Devon and Cornwall were told to only travel if necessary amid reports of overturned vans, trees down, fallen power cables and debris blown across roads.

Cornwall Council said teams responded to around 250 highway incidents with most involving debris and flooding on the roads.

Nearly 18,000 homes and businesses were without power in England and Wales, according to the National Grid.



And more than 13,000 properties were without power in Cornwall alone, they said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Footage has emerged of the moment part of Brighton‘s West Pier collapses into the sea amid the turbulent conditions.

The historic pier was damaged after a huge wave hit just moments before parts of the famous landmark were seen collapsing into the water.

News.title: 12th century fairytale castle featured in iconic British kids TV show goes on sale for £5m – can you guess which one?
News.content:
KING OF THE CASTLE 12th century fairytale castle featured in iconic British kids TV show goes on sale for £5m – can you guess which one?







Next

A 724-YEAR-OLD castle which featured in a beloved kids TV show has hit the market for £5million.

The medieval pad includes 30 bedrooms, six towers and a moat – it even hosted Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn for dinner in its Great Hall.



Allington Castle, near Maidstone, Kent is a grade I listed property built in 1279 and mentioned in the Domesday Book of 1086.

The huge fortress is full of flash medieval features making it the perfect filming location for the CBBC classic Horrible Histories.



The historic gem was used in series eight and nine of the show as Samuel Pepys’ home, the Tower of London, the Palace of Versailles, and a Tudor castle.

Within the huge walls is a jousting yard, two inner courtyards, a great hall and a priest hole.



Its enchanting appearance also bagged it a place in the cult 1960s TV show The Avengers.

But now the castle is being flogged for £5million after its former owner died in 2025 leaving it in need of a new custodian.

The castle is over 24,000 sq ft in size and stands alongside seven cottages and a converted barn.

The massive property is so flash it takes three gardeners, a maintenance manager and two event coordinators to run.

The new owner will be treated to an indoor swimming pool, tennis court and a Victorian-style greenhouse.



Sir Robert Worcester lived inside the historic gem from the late 90s until his death last year.

It was turned into a luxury home by the Wyatt family in the 15th Century and Sir Robert Worcester continued the legacy by restoring it with original features.

Home hunters tempted by the property have been warned that viewings can take up to two hours due to the huge size of the grounds.

A spokesperson from estate agents Knight Frank said: “Allington Castle offers more than a home, it offers a legacy.

“The current owners have carefully maintained and enhanced the estate, preserving its medieval integrity whilst ensuring modern practicality, with certified electrical and heating systems throughout the castle and cottages.”

News.title: Driver, 18, & passenger, 16, injured after VW ‘on false plates’ crashes into parked cars & lorry in Birmingham
News.content:
Next

A 16-YEAR-OLD boy has been rushed to hospital with serious head injuries after a VW crashed into parked cars and a lorry.

The 18-year-old driver of the car, which cops say was “on false plates”, was also injured after the horror in Birmingham.



Emergency services rushed to Warwick Road, Birmingham at around 5AM this morning after a car crashed into several parked vehicles and a lorry.

The passenger was urgently taken to hospital with serious head injuries.



And the driver was also injured after the VW smashed into “several parked cars” before hitting the lorry.

The VW Passat was allegedly on false plates.

A spokesman for West Midlands Police said: “We were called following a collision involving a car and a lorry on Warwick Road, Birmingham, at just before 5AM today.

“The car, which was on false plates, is understood to have struck several parked cars beforehand.

“A 16-year-old boy from the car has been taken to hospital with serious head injuries.

“An 18-year-old man has sustained injuries which are not believed to be serious.



“We’re investigating the circumstances and anyone with information can contact us via Live Chat on our website, or by calling 101, and quote log 565 of 24/10/26.”

News.title: Riot cops fire tear gas and hundreds arrested as thousands take to streets across France and troops sent to Paris
News.content:
Next

RIOT cops have fired volleys of tear gas at protestors as thousands take to the streets across France in “Act Two” of last weekend’s disorder.

At least 135 arrests have been made so far as the military are ready to deploy troops to Paris after the worst riots the country has seen in years.



In a tense standoff on the streets of the French capital, feared riot police have deployed tear gas and fired water cannons, as angry protesters hurl projectiles towards them.

Molatov cocktails were chucked at riot police in Nantes.





And dramatic footage showed masked protestors in Lyon kick away fuming tear gas cans as they made their way towards the city centre.

In Pau, demonstrators were seen scrambling as cannisters were fired down a downtown shopping alley.

Water cannons, armoured vehicles and aerial surveillance are part of the government’s hugely scaled-up security strategy after fires, vandalism and looting ripped through the country.



Around 70,000 police backed by specialist units will be in the streets, which is said to be around a 20 per cent increase on last weekend.

Tensions between authorities and protesters heightened last night when the Paris police banned the previously-authorised march route that was set to start at Bastille, instead green-lighting one on the city’s outskirts.



The inter-union organisations behind the demo furiously rejected the ban and insisted they would show up at Bastille anyway.

Luxury boutique stores meanwhile boarded up their normally glitzy shop windows and added their own guards after losing trust in the police.



Shoppers often flock to the capital from overseas looking for high-end Chanel handbags and Hermes scarves, but shop owners have decided it is too risky to stay open.

A Rolex retailer and a De Beers store near the famous Place Vendome will remain closed today, and other stores will decide whether to close early as the protests develop.

Louis Vuitton, Dior and Bulgari have also boosted their own security.



Hermes finance chief Eric du Halgouet said the company had increased security measures at its French stores, adding it was too early to say how much impact recent events would have on business.

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu warned on Friday evening that “the threat remains high for the far left”.

He added: “Vigilance is also needed with regard to crime because it takes advantage of these disturbances to recreate more confusion and steal.”

He assured that the “lessons learned” from the October 17 riots meant bolstered up and renewed security arrangements, especially in “the way the force will be used”.



Other cities including Lyon, Marseilles, Toulon, Le Havre, Rouen and Grenoble have banned demonstrations altogether, citing “obvious reasons of security”.



Lyon, France‘s third biggest city, had up to 300 shops looted last weekend and a tourist office was torched in the hours of chaos.

The Yellow Vest movement, unions, university and high school students are all behind today’s demonstrations protesting against the government, cost of living, and education standards.

Police had already seized dangerous objects including fireworks that were set to be used in the rallies.

Hélène Denéchère, spokesperson for the Paris police, said: “Checks are being carried out throughout the Île-de-France region on all roads.

“Already, dangerous objects, intended to be used in particular against the police forces, have been seized, including fireworks mortars.”



Interior Minister Lauren Nunez told law enforcement this morning: “We know that we will probably have disparate groups that will try to create incidents, either by attacking businesses, or institutions and internal security forces.”

He added: “We need to be hyper-reactive. We will need to be extremely mobile. You have the support of the hierarchy, and of the minister as well.

“I know who you are, I know the violence you are facing. I know that you are acting within a legal framework and that everything you are doing is proportionate.

“I know that everything will go well. It will be a long day. Good luck to everyone.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Security chiefs are particularly concerned over potential clashes in Orleans, where protests are expected against Marine Le Pen‘s National Rally during the far-right party’s two day conference.



As many as 40,000 people have travelled to Orleans, 70 miles from Paris for the left wing protest.

News.title: Page 3 star Kray ‘sister’ reveals ALL on twins’ 93rd birthday from shock proposal to their mum’s devastating trial error
News.content:
Next

VIOLET Kray watched with bated breath as her sons Ronnie and Reggie were sentenced for the murders of George Cornell and Jack ‘The Hat’ McVitie.

Her hairdresser and friend Maureen Flanagan supported Violet in the public gallery of the Old Bailey as the twins were jailed with older brother Charlie and other gang members.





Justice Melford Stevenson famously told them at the March 1969 sentencing: “In my view, society has earned a rest from your activities.”

So Maureen was surprised when she heard Violet heave a sigh of RELIEF as the sentence was read out.

Painfully, Violet misheard the judge as he sentenced Reggie and Ronnie to a minimum of 30 years – thinking he had only jailed them for three years each.

Flanagan – a close friend of the Kray family – told The Sun: “When the judge sentenced them to life Mrs Kray misheard the tariff and thought they had been given a three-year minimum.

“She breathed a sigh of relief and said ‘that’s not too bad.’

“I had to tell her ‘no, it was 30 years.’





“She was in a state of shock after that.”

Today marks the 93rd anniversary of the day that the identical twins were born in Hagerston, East London, with Reggie arriving into the world 10 minutes before Ronnie.

Their father Charles was a heavy drinking rag-and-bone man who travelled all over southern England buying and selling junk.

Mum Violet was an East End matriarch who dominated the family home.

Oldest son Charlie was born six years before the twins and a sister, Violet, who would have been four years older than Ronnie and Reggie, died in infancy.

It was unusual for twins to survive birth in that era and Mrs Kray formed a close emotional bond with her twin sons, who both contracted diphtheria aged three.

Two years later, when the twins were aged five, the family moved to a terraced house at 178 Vallance Road, Bethnal Green, later to become known as ‘Fort Vallance’.

Ronnie said of their childhood: “We had our mother, and we had each other, so we needed no one else.”



Maternal grandfather, Jimmy ‘Cannonball’ Lee, of Romany heritage, encouraged the twins to take up boxing and they became useful fighters, utilising their skills on the streets.

However, their promising boxing careers ended due to criminal convictions and dishonourable discharges from the Army with Ronnnie and Reggie among the last prisoners to be held at the Tower of London.

Inevitably, they drifted into crime, setting up nightclubs and running protection rackets.

Their specialty was threatening other criminals for a cut in their ill-gotten gains.

The twins assembled a gang nicknamed ‘The Firm,’ who wore sharp suits and overcoats, drove black limos and modelled themselves on the American Mafia.

Ronnie styled himself as ‘The Colonel’ and loved to rub shoulders with celebrities, leaving the more business-minded Reggie to run the clubs and rackets.

Society photographer David Bailey captured the dark, brooding looks of Ronnie and Reggie in a series of iconic black and white photographs taken in April 1965.

The twins socialised with showbiz stars including Judy Garland, Frank Sinatra, Peter Sellars and Diana Dors.



They were also close to former Hollywood actor George Raft, who became a key link between the Krays and the US mafia.

Ronnie and Reggie also knew Cockney actress Barbara Windsor well, though their relationship got off to a bad start.

They became upset when Babs filmed ‘Sparrows Can’t Sing’ on their home turf without their permission.

Ronnie and Reggie turned up on the film set and demanded protection money and that two of The Firm were used as extras.

The Krays later hosted the 1963 reception party for the film premiere at their club, The Kentucky.

Ronnie is said to have been gay, and Reggie rumoured to be bisexual. It has even been claimed they had sex with each other during their youth, fuelling their narcissistic tendencies.

Reggie disastrously married Frances Shea, who killed herself as their relationship was never consummated and referred to her husband as ‘bacon bonce’ – cockney rhyming slang for ‘nonce.’

Meanwhile, Ronnie became embroiled in a scandal with Lord Boothby, whom he supplied with boys along with Labour MP Tom Driberg.

Flanagan ended up being “one of the family” after becoming Violet Kray’s hairdresser and stylist in the mid-1960’s.

Islington girl Flanagan’s introduction to the family came when she met the twins’ older brother Charlie at a club on City Road.



Flan, now 84, says: “He was handsome and charming and complimented me on my hair.

“When I told him I had been a hairdresser he asked me to do his mum’s hair.

“I had a little white Mini and had no idea who the Krays were at the time.

“I turned up at Vallance Road and met Violet.

“She was warm, friendly and had baked a cake.

“We hit it off immediately.

“The mantlepiece was covered with boxing trophies and she told me they had been won by the twins and they lived there at the time.

“The other thing that I noticed was all the shirts hanging up.



“I thought she must be taking in laundry.

“But she was washing and ironing 12 shirts a day for the twins as they always wanted to look immaculate.”

Flan met Reggie that day and found him to be “cold and suspicious.”

She met Ronnie a fortnight later on her regular Thursday afternoon appointment with Violet.

Flan said: “Ronnie was a completely different person to Reggie and had a presence and a stare which was really frightening to begin with.

“Tom Hardy captured him perfectly in the film Legend.

“But Ronnie and I got talking and I soon relaxed.

“He was a gentleman.

“He told me I should be on the telly and when I expressed an interest he got me an Equity card through one of his contacts.”



Flanagan later had bit-part appearances as a Benny Hill girl, as well as roles on Monty Python, The Two Ronnies and the Frankie Howerd show.

She was also one of the original Page 3 models in The Sun during the 1970s.

Flanagan said: “My television career was all thanks to Ronnie.

“He was as good as his word.”

However, Ronnie was also a mentally deranged homicidal maniac who believed he was beyond the law.

On 9 March 1966 he walked into the Blind Beggar pub in Whitechapel and shot rival Richardson gang associate George Cornell in the head in full public view.

Cornell’s offence was to call Ronnie a “fat poof” and the Kray gang boss later wrote of the killing : “I felt f***ing marvellous.

“I have never felt so good, so bloody alive, before or since.”

Ronnie’s lieutenant, Ian Barrie, fired five shots into the air as a warning to people not to talk to police.



In December that year, Ronnie organised the escape of an old prison pal, ‘Frank ‘The Mad Axeman’ Mitchell, from Dartmoor jail.

After housing him in a flat in the East End, Mitchell became threatening.

The Krays called on hitmen Freddie Foreman and Alf Gerrard to kill and dispose of him.

Ronnie began taunting his twin brother to kill someone and in October 1967 – four months after the suicide of Reggie’s 23-year-old wife – the pair murdered Jack ‘The Hat’ McVitie.

The Trilby-wearing criminal had been paid £500 upfront by the twins to kill the Krays’ accountant Leslie Payne, with the same amount to follow afterwards.

However, drug user McVitie failed to carry out the hit, signing his own death warrant by threatening the twins and causing trouble at one of their clubs.

He was lured to a party in Stoke Newington where Reggie initially tried to shoot him in the head but the gun didn’t work.

Reggie then repeatedly stabbed McVitie with a carving knife as Ronnie yelled ‘Do him, Reg.’



The American Mafia withdrew from the Krays over concerns about their risky lust for violence.

Meanwhile, a secret Scotland Yard squad led by Leonard ‘Nipper’ Read was cracking open the wall of silence surrounding the Krays.

They swooped on the Kray gang on 8 May 1968, catching Ronnie in bed with a young man and Reggie with a woman.

With the Krays locked away on remand, further key witnesses came forward.

Flanagan said: “I went with Mrs Kray to see her boys at Brixton prison while they were on remand and she took them roast dinners, fresh socks and underpants.

“I was at the Old Bailey when the barmaid at the Blind Beggar gave her evidence against Ronnie.

“She was a very good witness and everyone felt it was over after that.”

Flanagan went on: “After the convictions I used to accompany Violet to see the twins in prison.

“Before she died (in 1982) she asked me to keep going to see them after she was gone.

“All three Kray brothers were separated after they were sentenced and the twins never saw each other again apart from at Violet’s funeral.”



Flan became a conduit to the outside world for twins Reggie and Ronnie while they were serving their life sentences.

She made hundreds of visits to 12 different prisons to see the pair and helped Ronnie live in style and comfort at Broadmoor, where he died in 1995.

Flanagan was responsible for keeping Ronnie in silk shirts, ties and underwear, monogrammed handkerchiefs and Italian shoes.

She also helped supply Ronnie with his daily 100 Players cigarettes and a weekly pork pie from Harrods, which he shared with fellow inmates at Friday night suppers in his room at the secure hospital.

Flan says: “Ronnie was always The Colonel wherever he was.

“He was always charming and would never tolerate any swearing in front of women.

“It is hard for me to compare the kind and charming Ronnie Kray I knew with the one who would shoot a man dead in cold blood.”

Flanagan said both twins could be demanding at times, Ronnie especially so.

She said: “Reggie wanted the latest Reebok trainers and things like that.

“But Ronnie had a great list of things, shirts, ties, silk underwear.”



Fees from films, TV programmes, books and newspaper deals helped keep Ronnie in a life of relative luxury.

Homosexual Ronnie married twice behind bars to different women and exclusive pictures were duly sold.

Reggie asked Flanagan to marry him on three occasions.

She politely refused but says: “At least I would have known where he was every night.”

Ronnie’s most famous visitors were movie stars Jame Fox and Richard Burton.

Fox saw Ronnie at HMP Brixton while researching his gangster role in the film 1970 Performance.

Burton visited the crime boss in Broadmoor – under an assumed name – while researching his part in the 1971 film Villain.

Kray was only being held at Broadmoor temporarily at the time and Flanagan says: “Ronnie wasn’t impressed by Burton at all.

“He hated the loafers Burton was wearing and said he was scruffy, had pock-marked skin and greasy hair.”

Ronnie held strong views about crime – if not his own.



Flanagan recalls: “One day he came into the visitors room carrying a newspaper under his arm and pointed to a story about an old lady being battered.

“He told me to find out from the paper where the old lady was and send her £10.

“He said “They call us bad – what’s happened to England?”

Ronnie sent out bouquets of flowers “all the time” and ran up a £7,000 canteen bill in Broadmoor buying coffees and teas for his cronies, leaving older brother Charlie to foot the bill.

Flanagan has used her association with the Krays to give talks at young offenders’ institutions.

She says: “I tell the boys what a knife did for Reggie and what a gun did for Ronnie.

“They took lives with weapons and destroyed their own lives in the process.”

The twins were 35 when they were jailed for life.

Ronnie died aged 61 while Reggie followed five years later in October 2000 from cancer, 35 days after being released on compassionate grounds.

Charlie died six months before Reggie aged 72.



Flanagan was involved in planning the funerals of Ronnie and Reggie, with the old East End turning out in huge numbers to remember them and their lost “manor.”

She says: “The Krays are now a myth and have gone into folklore.

“They were men of their time and high profile enjoying the company of politicians and film stars.

“I have never glamorised crime and would not defend what the Krays did.

“But they were very kind to me, especially Ronnie.”

Flanagan was given the MBE last year for her charity work.

She will mark today’s anniversary of the twins’ birth by holding a charity auction at the Blind Beggar pub with Kray memorabilia going under the hammer.

Flanagan says: “I’m sure they would both have been thrilled to know I have been honoured at Buckingham Palace.

“They would also be delighted their reputation is being used for a good cause.”

News.title: Manhunt launched for prisoner who escaped south London medical facility
News.content:
Manhunt launched for prisoner who escaped south London medical facility

Anthony Lloyd, 38, was last seen at around 4.10pm on Friday, October 23, after forcing his way out of a medical facility in Lewisham

View 2 Images (Image: Metropolitan Police )

Police have issued an urgent warning as a manhunt is launched for a prisoner who escaped from a medical facility in south London.

‌



‌



Met officers have warned he could pose a risk to himself and the public.

‌



Anthony Lloyd, 38, was last seen at around 4.10pm on Friday, October 23, after forcing his way out of the unit in Lewisham.

‌



He was spotted heading in the direction of Catford, but officers believe he could now be anywhere in London.

Detective Superintendent Melanie Pressley, who is leading the search, said police were carrying out "various significant enquiries" to locate Lloyd and return him to custody.

She said: "We are concerned he poses a risk both to himself and the public, and would urge anyone who sees him to call 999 immediately. Do not approach him."

‌



View 2 Images (Image: Metropolitan Police )

Lloyd is described as white, around 5ft 8in tall and of medium build, with short dark hair.

‌



He was last seen wearing a grey-blue T-shirt, black tracksuit bottoms and white trainers.

Police have said Lloyd also has links to Surrey, Sussex, Thames Valley, Hampshire, Nottinghamshire, Derbyshire and Merseyside.

‌



Det Supt Pressley added: "If you have any information, however small, that could help us locate Lloyd, please get in touch with police as a matter of urgency."

Anyone who sees Lloyd is urged to call 999 immediately and not approach him.

Article continues below

Anyone with information that could help officers trace him should contact police, quoting CAD4739/23Oct.

News.title: UK weather live: 28 areas on flood alert as Storm Boelo set to bring 80mph winds
News.content:
The Met Office has issued 'danger to life' amber weather warnings for Storm Boelo, which arrives just after Storm Austen caused serious damage in the South West

Storm Boelo is set to bring 80mph winds and 'widespread travel disruption' to the UK this weekend, with forecasters warning of potential flooding, power cuts and problems on the roads.

One amber warning for wind, two yellow warnings for wind and a yellow warning for rain will cover different areas across the UK this weekend.

It comes after Storm Austen led to airports being closed, flights cancelled and even Brighton's iconic West Pier partially collapsing.

Meanwhile, Prime Minister Andy Burnham warned on Friday that the UK could face “a winter of greater flooding” and said we are living in a world where “unexpected events” are “more and more common”.

An amber weather warning is in place across Scotland today, along with the north of England down to Carlisle and the north-east of Northern Ireland.

It comes just a day after Storm Austen battered the South West of England, with schools closed and 31,000 homes at one point left without power yesterday.

Tom Morgan, a Met Office meteorologist, said: “Yesterday’s Storm Austen affected the far south of the UK and northern France and the Channel Islands, whereas today’s Storm Boelo will be affecting the north of the UK."

News.title: Fire ravages Adolf Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat leaving it so damaged it 'likely cannot be saved'
News.content:
Fire ravages Adolf Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat leaving it so damaged it 'likely cannot be saved'

Police in Bavaria, Germany, have made an arrest following a fire at Adolf Hitler's Alpine mountain retreat the Kehlsteinhaus - also known as the Eagle's Nest

View 3 Images Adolf Hitler's mountain retreat caught fire on Friday night (Image: Berchtesgaden/AFP via Getty Images)

A fire swept through the mountaintop retreat built for Adolf Hitler and known as the Eagle's Nest as emergency services struggled to tackle the blaze in snow and wind.

‌



‌



The fire at the building, located in the Berchtesgaden district in south east Germany, started just before 10pm on Friday night, police said in a statement. More than 200 Firefighters battled the flames at the difficult-to-access site on a cliff 1,834 meters above sea level.

‌



The structure, preserved after World War Two as a historical site from the Nazi era, had been so badly damaged that it “could probably not be saved,” the force said. Efforts continued to put out the flames at the Eagle's Nest on Saturday afternoon.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images The firefighters found no one inside the building (Image: APA/AFP via Getty Images)

Hitler’s closest friends expose chilling truth of how monster charmed them before unleashing evil READ MORE :

Police said a person was arrested, but officers have yet to be determined whether they had anything to do with the fire. Rain that turned into the year's first snow, accompanied by strong wind, complicated the already difficult task of tackling the blaze and firefighters had to pull out overnight after several hours, officials said.

‌



No one was injured in the fire, and firefighters hoped to finish their work on Saturday though they weren't able to enter the building because of a danger of falling material. The building, known in German as the Kehlsteinhaus, is located on a cliff 1,834 meters (6,017 feet) above sea level.

It is reachable by an elevator built inside the rock from the end of the mountain road, which is closed to public traffic but used during the day by buses for visitors. It has been operated as a cafe and restaurant since 1952 and contains an exhibition on its history. The Nazi dictator himself rarely used the Kehlsteinhaus - unlike the Berghof residence, also in the Berchtesgaden area, the ruins of which were blown up in 1952.

‌



The Obersalzberg Documentation Center, further down the mountain, is home to the area's main historical exhibition and was unaffected by the fire. Officials indicated that the Eagle's Nest would be restored, though they were vague so soon after the blaze about how exactly that would be done.

View 3 Images The building remembers Adolf Hitler's life (Image: THE NATIONAL ARCHIVES/AFP via Ge)

‌



"We're not going to leave a ruin there," Bavaria's interior minister, Joachim Herrmann, told reporters in Berchtesgaden. But what the site will look like in the future will be a matter for discussions with local officials, historians, preservationists and others.

‌



"I think we will be able to find a sensible solution," Herrmann added. Bavaria's state government owns the building. The minister stressed that "it is important that we continue to do the work of remembrance."

The fire comes months after controversial plan to redevelop the house where the dictator was born has been slammed by concentration camp survivors. The £17 million conversion of the 17th-century house where Hitler was born on 20 April 1889 into a police station is nearing completion, with officers even expected to move in the coming months - during the second quarter of 2026.

Article continues below

Ministers insist the bold project in Braunau am Inn, Austria will finally “neutralise” one of Europe’s most toxic and notorious addresses. But critics warn the symbolism is both twisted and sinister. For Ludwig Laher, writer and member of the Mauthausen Committee Austria, which represents survivors of Nazi concentration camps, the decision carries serious weight for society.

News.title: France protests live: Tear gas and water cannons deployed as thousands join marches
News.content:
The Louvre, the Orsay and Picasso museums are closed, with a partial night curfew also in place across different parts of Paris

More protests are planned across France today following a weekend of significant disorder that ravaged the country.

Around 70,000 officers have been sent out across France to prevent large-scale disorder similar to last weekend. So far, today's protests seem less severe compared to last weekend, with a turnout of about 35,000 protesters so far, compared to 60,000 this time last week.

More than 2,700 arrests were carried out following the looting last week, with curfews now imposed across Paris. The widespread disorder was caused by demonstrators furious at the cost of living crisis and poor school conditions.

Scenes of looting, burned-out cars and attacks on public buildings stunned the world as groups of masked vandals targeted businesses in Paris and other city centres. Besides the 70,000 law enforcement officers, helicopters, armoured vehicles and water cannons will also be deployed today.

A partial night curfew in Paris, covering parts of the city including the historic Place de la République, is in place until Monday. Meanwhile, the Culture Ministry said the Louvre, the Orsay and Picasso museums as well as the Grand Palais would be closed.

News.title: Budget must ending housing benefit freeze to give families 'breathing space'
News.content:
Budget must ending housing benefit freeze to give families 'breathing space'

EXCLUSIVE: In a letter seen by The Mirror, over a dozen major charities, including Shelter and Crisis, call on Chancellor John Healey to bring the benefit back in line with private rents

View 2 Images Andy Burnham with his Chancellor John Healey at last month's Labour conference (Image: Michael Bowles/Shutterstock)

Chancellor John Healey has been urged to use next week's Budget to end the housing benefit freeze blamed for straining families' budgets.

‌



‌



In a letter seen by The Mirror, over a dozen major charities, including Shelter, Crisis, and food bank organisation Trussell, call on Mr Healey to bring the benefit back in line with private rents.

‌



As Greater Manchester Mayor last year Andy Burnham had called for an end to the freeze to Local Housing Allowance (LHA) and said it would make a real difference in preventing homelessness.

‌



In their letter to the Chancellor, the charities says: "Unfreezing LHA would also give millions of low-income private renters some much needed breathing space."

LHA rates set the amount of housing benefit private renters can receive but freezes over the last decade have meant the support has failed to keep up with the cost of soaring local rents.

The charities pointed to Resolution Foundation estimates showing a typical two-bedroom home at the lower end of the private rented market now costs £158 a month more than the LHA rate.

‌



They said: "This shortfall in housing support is straining household budgets overall, leaving many households struggling to afford other essentials."

Andy Burnham defends emergency kit list and gives verdict on stockpiling wine READ MORE :

View 2 Images Charities called for action in helping prevent homelessness (Image: PA)

‌



The charities, which also includes Generation Rent, Homeless Link, and St Mungo's, added: "At present, there are 135,000 households (including 177,000 children) experiencing homelessness living in temporary accommodation in England, many for months and years, because there are not enough social homes available and private rents are increasingly unaffordable.

"This system is not working for people trapped in often poor-quality accommodation and homelessness for long periods."

‌



They conclude: "This Budget therefore presents a major opportunity to strengthen the UK Government’s wider efforts to prevent and end homelessness. We urge you to unfreeze Local Housing Allowance and uprate rates so that they once again cover at least the cheapest 30% of homes in a local area."

The call comes ahead of a pre-Budget summit on homelessness in Downing Street with some of the charities involved in the letter seen by The Mirror set to attend.

‌



Crisis chief executive, Matt Downie, who is expected to join the meeting this week, told The Mirror: "With the Prime Minister clearly prioritising ending homelessness, including a 'first instruction' to eradicate rough sleeping, the Westminster government must seize the opportunity of the Autumn Budget to ensure that everyone can access the foundation of a safe and stable home."

He added: "This starts with bringing housing benefit back in line with the cheapest third of private rents.Currently, fewer than 2% of homes available to rent privately are affordable for someone in receipt of housing benefit.

Article continues below

"The gap between the support people receive and the actual cost of private rents is trapping people in a cycle of debt, poverty and homelessness. More families than ever are living in temporary accommodation - it's an injustice that must be stopped."

A Government spokesperson said: “We're determined to turn the tide on poverty, and our recent statistics show that effort is making a difference - household incomes have risen 5% in real terms, food bank usage has fallen, and food insecurity is down. “We have also launched a £1 billion Crisis and Resilience Fund, invested more than £1 billion in homelessness services, and committed a record £39 billion to affordable and social housing. “Local Housing Allowance rates were increased to the 30th percentile of local market rents in April 2024, at a cost of approximately £7bn over five years across Great Britain.”

News.title: Greggs has major update for customers as new menu item 'biggest ever'
News.content:
Greggs has major update for customers as new menu item 'biggest ever'

It brought the launch forward by two weeks

View 3 Images It seems to have gone down a treat (Image: James Gill - Danehouse, Getty Images)

Greggs has given an update to customers today as it confirmed some record-breaking news.

‌



‌



It said that its much-loved Festive Bake had achieved its all-time single-day sales record, on the very first day it was available this year. Launched nationwide on Thursday, it returned on the earliest date in its 17-year history and fans wasted no time getting into the festive spirit, snapping up more Festive Bakes in a single day than on any other day since it first launched, Greggs said.

‌



Greggs brought the launch forward by two weeks, believing "Brits were ready to get their Christmas food fix earlier than ever" and, judging by the record-breaking opening, it seems it was right. Greggs said it now believed the strong start put it on course to sell more Festive Bakes than ever before.

‌



View 3 Images The Greggs Festive Bake

Zoe Harris, customer director at Greggs, said: “We know the Festive Bake has a huge following, but this launch has been something else. We brought it back two weeks earlier than ever before because we know people are ready to start feeling festive sooner and in just 24 hours, they proved us right.

‌



“To see the biggest day of Festive Bake sales ever is incredible. This record-breaking start means it could be our biggest Festive Bake season yet. Christmas has definitely come early for Greggs fans.”

Greggs Festive Bake ingredients

Fine-tuned for 2026, the Festive Bake brings together chicken, smoked ham hock, sweetcure bacon, creamy soft cheese and spiced pork stuffing in a rich sage and cranberry sauce. It’s wrapped in golden-glazed puff pastry and finished with a crisp crumb topping, which Greggs said "flakes all down your top".

‌



View 3 Images Greggs said it had broken a record (Image: Finnbarr Webster, Getty Images)

The festive line-up also features the Pigs Under Blankets Toastie, Pepperoni Pizza with Hot Honey, Festive Feast Baguette, Festive Flatbread and Sweet Mince Pie Roll, plus three new sweet treats and a range of seasonal drinks.

Article continues below

All items on the new festive menu are now available in shops nationwide, Greggs confirmed. Customers can secure their seasonal fix on the go via Click + Collect using the Greggs App, or have the entire feast delivered to their door through Just Eat and Uber Eats.

News.title: Two people injured after police dogs escape handler's home
News.content:
Two people injured after police dogs escape handler's home

Two members of the public were injured when police dogs broke free from the property of their handler in Leicestershire as the force confirmed an investigation is underway

View 2 Images The dogs were brought under control and the police force has apologised (Image: Supplied/ Samuel Kalantzis)

An investigation has been launched after two people were left injured after police dogs escaped from their handler's home.

‌



‌



The animals, a current operational police dog and one now retired from service, escaped from the garden of their handler’s home address in Sileby, Leicestershire.

‌



Two members of the public sustained minor injuries in the incident. The force said it was an isolated incident but confirmed they are to hold an enquiry.

‌



The two dogs, which appear to be German shepherds, began barking in the street before approaching a woman, footage shows. A man, who was driving through the area, then pulled over in a bid to help before appearing to be bitten by one of the dogs.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 2 Images Footage of the aftermath has been shared on social media (Image: Supplied/ Samuel Kalantzis)

‌



Man and dog killed after being hit by bus in Bristol as police launch appeal READ MORE :

XL Bully 'exemption' change update as Defra issues statement READ MORE :

The man, who did not wish to be named, said: "I came across the incident while driving through the area and noticed someone apparently having difficulty with one of the dogs.

"As a professional dog handler myself, I stopped to offer assistance. Within moments of exiting my vehicle, the operational police dog bit my ankle, breaking the skin on both sides.

‌



"Fortunately, my protective work boots prevented what could have been a much more serious injury."

He told LeicestershireLive that he does not blame the dogs for the incident on Tuesday, or wish for them to be put down, but highlighted concerns for the public's safety.

‌



"Had a child, an elderly person or someone unable to retreat quickly encountered these dogs, the consequences could potentially have been much worse," the man said. The dogs were then brought under control by the officers living at the address and taken back to the house.

Leicestershire Police confirmed that an investigation into the incident is underway and those injured were spoken to and did not require medical attention.

‌



A spokesperson said: "This incident will understandably cause some concern and during the last few days the force has carried out a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding what happened.

"The force has deemed that the correct security arrangements are usually in place, and this was an isolated incident. The dog handler has been spoken to regarding the importance of ensuring the gate of the property is always secure.

Article continues below

"The dog handler and police dog will also be undergoing a safety assessment to ensure operational standards continue to be met. All other dog handlers in the team have also been spoken to regarding the importance of ensuring the dogs are kept in a secure premises when not on duty. The two members of the public have been updated and the force has apologised to them."

News.title: Plan for Northern Olympics to get £7m in Healey's Budget
News.content:
The report will look in closer detail at how hosting the games could work.

It will consider the kinds of venues and transport links required, how different cities could share the games, how communities could benefit.

Crucially it will also examine how much it could cost as well as assess the chances of a bid succeeding. The Conservative-Lib Dem coalition government said in 2013 it estimated hosting in London had cost Â£8.9bn.

A report in 2013 by the UK Trade and Investment, which has since been replaced by the Department for International Trade, said it had sparked a Â£9.9bn boost to the economy through new contracts, sales and foreign investments.

But the estimated amount was queried by some, including the Federation of Small Businesses and the National Institute of Economic and Social Research (NIESR).

The new feasability study for the Northern Games will be done by government, UK Sport, the Northern Mayors and include the British Olympic and Paralympic associations.

Healey said: "Olympic legacy lasts way beyond the celebration of sport over the summer. The North hosting an event as big as this would be truly unforgettable.

"Britain's experience of London 2012 is proof we can host the world. I'm picking up the pace on our work to potentially bid for these prestigious games. It will lift communities, create opportunities and give the UK a huge boost."

News of the funding for the study was welcomed by the British Olympic Association, ParalympicsGB and UK Sport.

"We welcome the government's continued support for exploring the potential of a future bid for the Olympic and Paralympic Games in the UK in the 2040s," they said in a joint statement.

"Building on the success and legacy of London 2012, we look forward to working in partnership to explore this exciting opportunity and the benefits it could deliver for the nation, and for the global Olympic and Paralympic movements."

News.title: Between quick wins and big dreams lies Burnham's biggest test
News.content:
But the widespread suggestion that you'll be able to blink and miss the Budget has got some hackles up in the Treasury. A budget, by its very nature, can never be a small event - it sets billions upon billions of taxes and spending decisions.

And there are likely to be extra taxes on banks, vows to sweep away some business regulation, particularly for small business, more powers passing to local leaders under the guise of devolution and more action on energy bills which are heading back up again.

John Healey has made it clear publicly and to staff, that he wants to encourage people with the guts and drive to start a business. One source said: "If you are taking on John's mantra about talking up Britain then you can't say, 'Nothing to see here'."

Whatever else the chancellor brings to Parliament in his red box, do not expect him to arrive with all the solutions to the country's very well-documented problems, whether that's getting the economy growing more convincingly, sorting out gaps in defence cash, welfare, social care, or new ways to pay off the country's groaning debts more quickly.

One former minister suggests even if Healey and Burnham had stumbled upon all the answers in a few months, it's just not possible to fix everything at the same time because of the constraints on the economy.

They wondered: "Is he going to invest in growth? Is he going to put everything he has into the challenges people will face this winter? Is he going to throw it at defence? There is just not enough to tackle all these problems simultaneously - ministers are going to be exposed to the cold light of day."

Burnham and Healey have to find a way of maintaining the balance in an unusually happy Labour Party.

MPs talk of ministers and Burnham himself being more visible and approachable in Parliament, knocking around with colleagues in the evening, fewer "golden slips" doled out when ministers were excused from voting alongside colleagues so they could get on with their important jobs.

One minister told me they'd had to tell their private office not to arrange for them to be "slipped" , from going to the Commons in the evening to see backbenchers.

It's paying off in the mood among MPs. One told me: "You're not feeling like the only way you can ever have a chat with a minister is by arranging an appointment for three months down the line â the soft touches really matter."

News.title: Infantino tells BBC Sport he is backed by 'vast majority' of world football
News.content:
During the interview he reflected on having been "fully endorsed" by the Asian Football Confederation - following a U-turn by its president Sheikh Salman - and having the backing of "all African countries".

But only last week, he apologised to the Fifa Council over the "communication and consultation" regarding FFE.

He was told by Council members in that meeting that he was not "fit to be Fifa president" if he did not give them the documents they have asked for, including the rationale for FFE.

Yet, when pressed on when he would be providing the requested papers, he did not give a clear answer, saying they had to follow a "legal process" and that they were "working on it".

"We'll answer of course all the questions that are asked as far as the process allows, as far as we can," he said.

Speaking from the first Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan, he said he and the Fifa administration were doing "as best we can" but admitted they have done "some things which are maybe less good".

He also said that they need to have dialogue "more often" with Uefa, in an effort to repair their strained relationship.

Asked by the BBC if he was fit to be Fifa president, and whether he had considered standing down, he laughed, before saying: "Well you know I was elected by 211 member associations from all over the world.

"I think what is important is that in an organisation like Fifa, there can be different views, different points of view.

"But if we are serious about democracy, about the democratic process, about believing that everyone has the same vote and the same voice all over the world, that football belongs to everyone, if we are serious about that, then we need, to respect as well the views of the vast, vast majority.

"I'm just coming back off Tokyo where the Asian Football Confederation has fully endorsed me. I was in Cape Verde where all [Confederation of] African [Football] countries have endorsed me. I'm speaking to all associations everywhere in the world."

He continued: "There are different points of view it's not always easy to bring them all under one roof but we need to respect and I do respect all opinions all views and then it will be up to the Fifa member associations to decide who they want as a president and how they want Fifa to be run."

The deadline for candidates to confirm they are standing against Infantino for the election in March is 18 November - although none have yet filed and he could stand unopposed.

News.title: Strictly's new presenters - after mixed reviews have they found their feet?
News.content:
Strictly Come Dancing's new hosting trio received a very mixed reception when the latest series began a month ago. Ratings have dipped and the jury's still out, but critics say they are slowly getting into the groove.

Changing the hosting team on the BBC's flagship Saturday night entertainment show was never likely to be a waltz in the park.

And going from two presenters to three, and giving them slightly different roles, upset the show's rhythm even more.

Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman were always going to be a hard act to follow.

Into their sparkly shoes have stepped the safe and smooth Emma Willis; the flamboyant former professional dancer Johannes Radebe; and cheeky comedian Josh Widdicombe, a wildcard who was not hitherto associated with either the dance world or prime-time TV.

Willis and Widdicombe have been paired on the live shows, where he is tasked with injecting humour into the moments before and after each dance - with mixed results, say critics.

Radebe, meanwhile, has taken over from Winkleman upstairs on the mezzanine, bringing his warmth and dance expertise to the celebrity interviews following each routine.

News.title: Are California voters about to impose 'world's first' tax on billionaires?
News.content:
But the vote is also offering regular residents a voice on an issue that has roiled politics for decades.

"I believe this is the first billionaire tax - meaning a wealth tax that is targeting a very extreme percentile of the wealth distribution," says Francesco Trebbi, a public policy professor at the University of California, Berkeley. He noted the measure's historic nature and how it could help even out California's wealth gap.

The state has the largest economy in the country and boasts the fourth largest global economy, bigger than India and the UK. And it is home to one of the highest concentrations of billionaires in the world. But it also has the largest share of homeless people in the nation and one of the highest wealth gaps.

Those who back the measure have argued it helps ensure that the ultra-wealthy are contributing their fair share and will help backfill gaps in the state's budget. The move aims to raise $100bn (Â£75bn) to make up for federal funding cuts to the state's health-care system.

Suzanne Jimenez, chief of staff for Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West, which helped lead the charge for the initiative, says the measure is a "short-term solution" for massive federal funding cuts coming to California as a result of US President Donald Trump's sweeping tax and spending bill.

"If we do nothing, we're going to see a collapse of our healthcare system, while we figure out a longer-term solution to fund our healthcare," she tells the BBC.

News.title: Before you crank up the thermostat, try these tips to keep you and your home warmer for longer
News.content:
With the clocks going back this weekend, the nights will be drawing in.

So if you have a thicker duvet, now is the time to bring it out. Some supermarkets sell winter duvets for under Â£20 - look for 10.5 tog or higher.

But there's something to be said for a craftily placed blanket, too. When it gets cold, Rebecca, 44, from Hertfordshire, sleeps with a blanket underneath her mattress, which she says stops draughts. "This was passed to me by my nan, she swore by it," she says. Others swear by placing a blanket above the mattress but under the bedsheet.

You can heat your bed before getting in with a hot water bottle, but make sure you check the expiry date. A guide by NHS Scotland, external says to let the water from the kettle cool for a few minutes before filling, only fill it two-thirds full, squeeze air out of the top before putting the stopper on, and don't hold it directly against your skin.

Using an electric blanket - to heat your bed before you get in or to wrap around yourself on the sofa - is "one of the cheapest ways" to stay warm, says Emily Seymour, energy editor at consumer organisation Which?. Testing by Which?, external shows it typically costs between 2p and 8p an hour to run an electric blanket at its highest setting. The London Fire Brigade, external says to unplug your blanket before you get into bed unless it has a thermostat control, not to use a hot water bottle at the same time, and replace it every 10 years.

News.title: The artist dropping her debut album after a billion streams
News.content:
Jazzy is rooted in the Dublin club scene, starting her career as part of a group called Powerful Creative Minds in the city.

But as more and more clubs close, the DJ says there are fewer opportunities for artists to cut their teeth offline.

"When I first started going out, there was a lot more going on," she says.

"There was a lot more nightclubs to go to and it's very different when we look at it now, which is sad.

"There's definitely a home for dance music on the internet of course but club culture is very important and I think that's something that we need to keep going for sure."

Latest figures from the Night Time Industries Association, external suggest about 12 venues are closing across the UK every month, with almost 30% of the night time economy lost since the coronavirus pandemic.

"I hope to God that it doesn't disappear, the club scene altogether," says Jazzy, who describes a similar issue in Ireland.

"We all need to try and put a hand in to keep it going."

Jazzy's taking her new album on tour across the UK from next month, but first she has her biggest gig yet: Dublin's 3Arena in front of a home crowd.

Even after a Coachella set and supporting Calvin Harris, she describes this as the "biggest milestone of my career to date".

While she says fans can mostly expect her brand of uplifting records on the album, she says it's also more personal than her usual work.

She highlights one track in particular, Invisible, as a change from her more upbeat releases. It deals with a bad experience she had in the music industry, describing it as "like my first ever diss track".

"I hope [fans] learn a little bit more about me, because that was one of my goals with the album - to open up a little bit about experiences in life as well.

"So there's a little message from me in each song."

News.title: UK to invest £100m in 'world first' AI Biosecurity Lab
News.content:
The UK says it will establish a national AI Biosecurity Lab (AIBL) to help strengthen its defences against emerging biological threats.

As part of Wednesday's Budget, the government will commit Â£100m to establishing the new, "world first" institute with the support of leading AI firms.

The chancellor will also pledge millions of pounds in spending across a range of initiatives aimed at shoring up the UK's ability to respond to evolving cyber, biological and AI-enabled threats.

"AI will transform daily life: every firm, community, hospital, school, and every aspect of our economy can benefit," John Healey said.

"I understand and share the concerns of working people, so I am setting out a distinctively British approach to AI.

"One that doesn't leave workers behind and defends our national interest, while ensuring the benefits of AI-enabled growth are felt right across the country."

The full details about the role and remit of the new lab are yet to emerge.

But the AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said it would be a "major new global institution" that brings together "world-leading scientific expertise" to ensure the UK can safeguard its citizens and goals as AI develops.

"That means staying ahead of emerging threats, from cyber attacks to biological risks, while building more of the critical technology our security depends on," he said.

"By backing British science, advanced chips and our own AI companies, we can strengthen our national security, rebuild Britain's industrial strength and create good, skilled jobs across the country."

The AI Biosecurity Lab's creation will also be supported by leading AI developers, with OpenAI and Anthropic providing Â£200m worth of AI model credits that can be spent on the use of their models.

News.title: Tory activist in 'contract killing broker' claim had worked for party HQ
News.content:
A former Tory activist who appeared to offer to "broker" the hiring of contract killers in an undercover film report previously worked for Conservative headquarters.

Jack Ross was contracted to do social media work for the party until earlier this year, the BBC has been told.

It comes after Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch referred to them as "shocking allegations", adding that she did not "believe that person is a member anymore".

A Conservative spokesman said Ross's party membership had "been suspended with immediate effect pending an investigation". It has reported that Ross said his words were not meant to be taken seriously.

Ross was paid to provide social media advice to the party for a brief period, the BBC has been told. He was never an employee or Conservative Campaign Headquarters pass holder.

However, he met Badenoch on several occasions as part of his role as chief executive of Turning Point UK, an offshoot of a right-wing American organisation.

Ross has also met several other right-wing politicians including the former Prime Minister Boris Johnson and Nigel Farage, the Reform UK leader.

In undercover filming broadcast this week by Al Jazeera, Ross appears to offer to "broker" the services of contract killers.

The Al Jazeera report said its undercover journalist approached Ross in 2022 with a fictitious situation of a family business at risk of being taken over by a criminal gang.

Ross is alleged to have asked the undercover reporter what was needed from him, and listed violent options that could be bought including stabbing, shooting and killing.

Al Jazeera said Ross denied the finding "completely" and claimed everything he said to the reporter was not meant seriously.

Turning Point UK has been approached for comment.

News.title: Sam Fender calls out ticket prices ahead of tour
News.content:
Sam Fender has called out the price of gig tickets ahead of his next tour, promising to lower the cost.

The 32-year-old announced his Proper Massive Stadium Tour earlier this week, which will visit Newcastle, Cardiff, London, Edinburgh, Dublin and Manchester in summer 2027.

While tickets are yet to go on sale, Fender responded to a post on social media which claimed to outline the expected ticket prices.

The Geordie musician also said standing would not be split into a front and back tier and he had "no idea how this was normalised at gigs".

Tickets are due to go on general sale at 09:30 GMT on Friday, with a pre-sale at the same time on Wednesday.

But Fender said he was "not happy" with the reported prices.

"They're getting changed," he said on Instagram.

"It got inflated well more than I'd had in mind, it should only be inflated in relation to the cost of putting the show on."

The North Shields singer also said he did not want there to be an option for fans to pay more money to be closer to the front.

"The standing will not be split as well, I had no idea about it," Fender said.

"I have no idea how this was normalised in gigs... it won't be happening on this tour."

He is not the first musician to raise concerns over ticket pricing.

Zara Larsson agreed with fans earlier this year that her tickets were too expensive.

The Swedish singer said while she did not have control over the prices, she hoped she would in the future.
