News.title: Bournemouth thrash Milan to seal greatest win in club’s history
News.content:
Milan could not even point to being down to 10 men for the last hour as mitigation; long before, Bournemouth had treated the Rossoneri with contempt. When Ruben Amorim’s side trudged off, soaked and silenced, they had not mustered a single shot on target.

Few nights have better encapsulated the Premier League’s power. Bournemouth have never finished higher than last season’s sixth in the top flight of English football; AC Milan have won seven European Cups. But the Premier League’s financial clout is such that, each season, the bottom club earns more than the champions of Serie A.

The Premier League’s shared riches, allied to years of astute recruitment and management, have underpinned the Bournemouth’s ascent. Even Andoni Iraola’s departure has not stalled the progress at the Vitality Stadium; Marco Rose has relished the new European adventure.

Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz had already been toppled in Bournemouth’s first two European games. Now, Bournemouth have won their first three matches in Europe. Despite middling Premier League form, Rose’s ambitions will extend far beyond securing a berth in the knockout stages of the Europa League. On this evidence, Bournemouth are legitimate contenders to win the competition, and earn a berth in next season’s Champions League.

“It’s a special night for the club,” Ryan Christie, Bournemouth captain, said. “It’s mega – in terms of the story of the club, it’s ridiculous.”

Evanilson, perhaps, was Bournemouth’s standout player against AC Milan, combining intricate linkup play with a constant threat in front of goal. Centre-back Antonio Silva, controlling play from deep while marauding forward, also possessed a calmness that any of Milan’s beleaguered team lacked.

His side’s fate swiftly sealed, Amorim did not bother to summon Luka Modric or Christian Pulisic. Bournemouth’s own bench showed the depth that the club now possesses. Rayan showed off his trickery and directness; Adli – a substitute for substitute Alex Toth, who suffered a hamstring injury – then ensured that Bournemouth secured the margin of victory that their dominance deserved.

Sports.title: Why are Arsenal wearing black armbands vs Everton?
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL are taking on Everton at the Emirates in a huge Premier League clash.

Declan Rice and Co are wearing black armbands in tribute to Gunners legend Ken Friar.



ARSENAL VS EVERTON LIVE COVERAGE

Why are Arsenal wearing black armbands vs Everton?

Arsenal are wearing black armbands in memory of club icon Ken Friar, who died aged 92 earlier this month.



Players also wore the armbands in memory of Friar when the Gunners beat Lille 3-0 in the Champions League last week, with further commemorations to follow today.

Ahead of kick-off against Everton, a stadium tribute is planned to honour the Arsenal legend with a moment of applause.



Today’s matchday programme is also dedicated to Friar.

Friar worked for the club for 70 years and became their life president in 2020 after retiring from his executive responsibilities.

His first role was with the club’s box office in 1950, before he was appointed Arsenal’s secretary in 1973.

Friar’s greatest legacy is the part he played in the Gunners’ move from Highbury to Emirates Stadium at the turn of the century.



After 23 years as Arsenal’s managing director, Friar changed roles in 2000 to oversee the stadium project.

He worked alongside his friend and fellow director, Danny Fiszman, and the club moved into the Emirates six years later.

Friar was awarded an OBE in 2000 for his services to association football and also received the Freedom of the Borough of Islington.

Despite stepping down from the board in 2020, Friar would still attend Arsenal games and the club remained close to his heart.

Affectionately known by those at Arsenal as ‘Mr Friar’, he was a part-time box office runner four years prior to officially starting work with the club in 1950.



Born in Islington, Friar used to play football outside of the old Highbury stadium as a youngster.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta dedicated the win against Lille to the late Friar.

Speaking after his side’s Champions League triumph, he said: “I am sure he would be very happy with how the boys played and the way he won.

“That victory is for him. I know how proud he feels about what we built, and especially the group of players that we have.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He added: “The legacy that Ken is going to leave to all of us, to our football club and to everyone that has been close to him is going to live forever.



“I want to pass on all our love to his relatives and family, so they know that the way we feel about him is nothing but extraordinary.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta issues Bukayo Saka injury update with Arsenal star facing lengthy spell on sidelines
Sports.content:
Next

MIKEL ARTETA has delivered a worrying injury update on Bukayo Saka amid fears the Arsenal star could be sidelined for TWO MONTHS.

The England winger, 25, was forced off just ten minutes into Wednesday’s 2-2 Champions League draw against Bayern Munich.



Saka suffered a quad injury after attempting a pass and immediately required medical attention.

Early examinations suggest the Gunners ace could miss a minimum of six weeks, with fears his absence could stretch to eight.



But Arteta has now revealed the England international will require further scans before the full extent of the damage can be determined.

Speaking ahead of today’s Premier League clash with Everton, Arteta said: “I think it will be weeks, the extent of the injury.

“I think we’re going to have to repeat the scans in a week, ten days to see the extent of that.”

Fluid around the affected muscle has made it difficult for Arsenal’s medical team to assess the severity of the injury.

And should the worst fears be realised, the winger could also miss several crucial fixtures in Arsenal’s pursuit of silverware.

The latest setback adds to Saka’s injury frustrations after he previously endured lengthy spells on the sidelines with hamstring and achilles problems.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Arteta could now turn to Noni Madueke or Eberechi Eze to fill the void, while teenage sensation Max Dowman may also be handed more opportunities.

The Gunners will be keen to capitalise on Manchester City‘s slip-up at Aston Villa today.

Three points over Everton would move Arteta’s side level on points with the Premier League leaders, after Enzo Maresca’s men fell to a 2-1 defeat earlier in the afternoon.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo shows his class with incredible gesture to Al-Nassr team-mate after winning match
Sports.content:
Next

CRISTIANO RONALDO showed his class after handing his man of the match award to a team-mate.

The Portuguese superstar, 41, was named the standout performer following Al-Nassr’s 3-1 victory over Al-Faisaly in the Saudi Pro League.



But Ronaldo decided that fellow striker Abdullah Al-Hamdan was more deserving of the individual honour.

And footage showed the five-time Ballon d’Or winner personally presenting Al-Hamdan with the trophy before the pair posed for photos alongside a mascot.



Al-Hamdan had enjoyed an impressive evening, opening the scoring after just four minutes to give Al-Nassr an early advantage.

Ronaldo then doubled his side’s lead in the 49th minute, heading home a free-kick delivery from fellow Portuguese star Joao Felix.



But Al-Hamdan turned provider in the closing stages, setting up Brazilian winger Angelo to restore Al-Nassr’s two-goal cushion and seal the victory.

Former Manchester United and Real Madrid icon Ronaldo struck the 982nd goal of his remarkable career.

CR7 is just 18 strikes short of a historic 1,000 career goals.

Ronaldo thought he had added another shortly afterwards, but his effort was ruled out for offside after being set up by Al-Hamdan.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Speaking to Saudi broadcaster Thmanyah after the game, Al-Hamdan said: “It is a great honour for me to be alongside a legend of the legends of football.”

He added that the recognition would motivate him to offer more.

The Saudi striker also praised Ronaldo’s influence on and off the pitch, saying “we learn a lot from him” and revealing how the football legend takes time to help younger players develop.

Sports.title: Aston Villa 2 Man City 1: Enzo Maresca’s 100% record comes to an end as Nicolas Jackson continues red hot form
Sports.content:
Next

UNAI EMERY celebrated his fourth anniversary of becoming Aston Villa boss with another Premier League tactical masterclass.

The Spanish super-coach has now won all FOUR of his contests with Manchester City at Villa Park – while this latest result represented the FIRST league game Enzo Maresca’s side has failed to win this season.



A magnificent brace from Nicolas Jackson proved to be the difference as Villa won at home for the first time this campaign.

It was on October 24, 2022, when Emery arrived in Birmingham, and though his ill-fated Arsenal tenure has impacted his managerial reputation in the eyes of some English fans, nobody thinks badly of him now.



There is arguably nobody more shrewd within English football when it comes to tactics, formations and ideas.

This was a huge test of City’s Championship credentials but Villa, to a man, pressed and harried them to great effect, drilled to perfection by their meticulous manager.



Of course, whatever instructions Villa may have had pre-match, their cause was helped massively when their opponents practically gifted them a goal – as was the case in the sixth minute.

Marc Guehi – the only man on the field at kick-off not to drop down to one knee to acknowledge an anti-racism initiative – has not had the best of seasons and the England man was at fault for the opener.

His first touch of the ball was heavy and Villa captain John McGinn, always alert and ready to pounce on any mistake, managed to nick possession off the City centre-back.

This fed Jackson, and though he had defenders beside him, the Senegal striker showed great skill to beat City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma with pace and precision.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

As Emery punched the air in jubilation on his special day, Jackson, 25, ran off towards the fans to celebrate.

There was a thumbs-down motion as if he were a Roman Emperor in the Colosseum and then he used the same hand to perform a throat-slitting gesture.

It was a ruthless and clinical finish – Donnarumma, a man of his stature and size, should have done better there.



And it meant City have only kept FIVE clean sheets in their 13 matches this campaign.

“That’s why you’re going down,” they chortled in the Holte End, but that only tells half the story of what is to come from the legal ramifications of City’s guilty verdict.

Emery is clearly a good judge of character and player and even though he had the world’s best goalkeeper in Emiliano Martínez, he was not fazed that he left for Chelsea – because Zion Suzuki was waiting in reserve.

The Japanese international, with his back to the building site of the North Stand, made two decent saves in the first half.

First, he managed to palm to safety a strong strike by Iliman Ndiaye, which sailed through a crowd of players.



The next, he was more than able to blank out a good move by City, which resulted in the attempt by Rayan Cherki from ten yards.

The one time in the first half Suzuki, 24, was beaten, he was grateful for the post to save his skin as a fizzing left-footed drive by the dangerous Ndiaye on 29 minutes bounced off the frame of the goal.

Once the half-hour mark came, referee Peter Bankes had three big calls to make, all within the space of a few minutes.

Claims of a penalty for Villa and then City were both waved away.

And then he brandished a yellow card to Guehi when Jackson was brought down outside of the box.



The ref felt there was enough cover that it was not a last-man situation.

Officials can never please everyone.

But regardless of what the one-eyed fans might have screamed, the three decisions were correct.



It had been an entertaining first half, but Maresca had lost faith in Guehi, hooking him off at half-time to avoid another caution.

Erling Haaland had been anonymous in the first half but he only needs one chance to prove why he is the best striker in English football.

Even without his long locks, the Norwegian giant has lost none of his powers and it was no contest really when he outjumped Villa defender Victor Lindelof in the air for the equaliser.

Ndiaye provided the cross from the right, having received a short pass from a free-kick, and it was a peach of a delivery – while inflated bananas were raised by City supporters in the away end.

For Haaland, it was his 13th goal in 11 appearances, nine matches in a row in which he has scored – the man is relentless.



It could have been the start of an amazing City comeback but Jackson had other ideas.

The thumbs-down motion was back when he swept home from 12 yards from newly-introduced sub Ibrahim Mbaye’s cutback on 60 minutes.

It was Jackson’s seventh goal this season and further emphasised why Emery was so keen to nab him for £65million while also willing to let go of Ollie Watkins.



Again Donnarumma should have done better, with Jackson’s shot hit straight at him but squirming under his 6ft 5in frame.

City huffed and puffed without much success in the latter stages though Ian Maatsen headed a Haaland header off the line on 89 minutes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

You would hope Emery will permit himself a glass or two this evening for this latest masterstroke.

Another Arsenal manager, Arsene Wenger, could also enjoy this day – all of the top-flight clubs have been beaten at least once, so there won’t be any repeat of the Gunners’ 2003-24 Invincibles season.

Sports.title: Norwich ease pressure on boss Clement with win at Charlton
Sports.content:
Norwich halted a six-match losing streak with a 3-1 comeback win at Charlton to ease pressure on head coach Philippe Clement.

Charlie Kelman fired Charlton into an early lead but Paris Maghoma equalised for the Canaries, who then went ahead through Mathias Kvistgaarden and wrapped up victory via an Ivan Mesik own goal.

Charlton had a chance inside the opening 20 seconds but Tyreece Campbell was unable to beat City goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw.

Norwich had the ball in the net in the fifth minute, Jack Stacey tucked away a reverse pass by captain Pelle Mattsson, but it was flagged for offside.

The Addicks started with real intensity, their press unsettling the Canaries, and it led to the opening goal on 10 minutes.

Image: Mathias Kvistgaarden of Norwich City celebrates scoring his team's second goal

Kayne Ramsay nipped in to intercept Harry Darling's pass and Kelman, one of four changes made by Charlton boss Nathan Jones, took a touch on Joe Rankin-Costello's pass to go around Grimshaw and finish from a tight angle.

Billy Koumetio made a perfectly-timed tackle to dispossess Kvistgaarden in the penalty box in the 22nd minute.

Norwich finished the first period stronger as the hosts began to sit deeper.

A driving run from Maghoma, leaving Rankin-Costello trailing, saw the City attacker produce a low cross which narrowly evaded Kvistgaarden on the edge of the six-yard box.

Ramsay was at fault for the Norwich equaliser on 35 minutes. The Charlton right-back attempted a flick which was pounced on by Kvistgaarden and his threaded pass was dispatched impressively past Arthur Okonkwo by Maghoma as he opened his goal account for the campaign.

City finished the half controlling the ball and that continued after the action resumed.

Andre Brooks shot wide from a clear-cut opportunity before Kvistgaarden collected his third goal of the campaign, heading in from six yards out from Ruairi McConville's cross.

Charlton believed they had levelled in the 57th minute when McConville headed into his own net from Campbell's cross but it was struck off for offside.

Okonkwo came out quickly to smother a chance for Oscar Schwartau and then Grimshaw was equally quick to close the angle to frustrate Kelman shortly after the hour mark.

Norwich moved further ahead in the 75th minute as Mesik scored an own goal. Substitute Anthony Musaba's cross sliced off the Slovakian international and past Okonwko.

Charlton's keeper made two more saves to keep the margin of defeat down, tipping away Jacob Wright's shot and then saving from his legs as livewire Musaba tried to add a fourth.

It was the Addicks' first defeat at The Valley this season and they are now without a victory in nine Championship matches.

Sports.title: Bamford strikes to hold 10-man Derby
Sports.content:
Patrick Bamford was injured in the act of scoring Sheffield United's equaliser in a 1-1 draw with struggling 10-man Derby.

Bobby Clark gave the visitors a first-half lead with Bamford levelling the scores late in the game, only to limp off amid the celebrations.

After a quiet start, the game burst into life around the half-hour mark with efforts on goal at either end.

Derby threatened when the ball fell to Clark following a cross from Joe Ward and his firm drive was well saved by Michael Cooper down to his right.

Carlton Morris then found himself through on goal and fired in a shot on target which was saved by Cooper with his legs.

Image: Kalvin Phillips of Sheffield United battles for possession with Carlton Morris of Derby County

United's first effort of note came from Kalvin Phillips, whose long-range strike forced a save from Jacob Widell Zetterstrom.

Derby took the lead in the 37th minute when Ryan Hedges, on the left-hand side of the area, saw his low shot come back off the near post and the ball fell to Clark, who fired into the net from inside the D.

Blades boss Chris Wilder made a double substitution shortly before the hour-mark, sending on Sydie Peck and Femi Sereki.

Ben Brereton Diaz put an effort off target for the hosts while Derby's Sammie Szmodics chested the ball down before volleying over.

The visitors were reduced to 10 men in the 66th minute when Dion Sanderson received a second booking following a clumsy challenge on Sereki.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Derby's Dion Sanderson is sent off with a second yellow card against Sheffield United in the Championship.

After Romelle Donovan had an effort saved by Zetterstrom, the substitute played a key role in the equaliser.

The goal came in the 79th minute when Donovan delivered a probing cross to the far post and Bamford was on hand to bundle the ball over the line from close range. Bamford was injured in the process, however, after falling awkwardly and he had to be replaced.

Peck fired in a shot on target but it was straight at Zetterstrom who made a comfortable save.

Tyrese Campbell and fellow substitute Peck had chances to win it for the hosts in time added on.

Campbell saw his shot on the turn force a fine save from Zetterstrom, who turned the ball onto the bar and away, then Peck fired in a shot which the keeper was again equal to.

Donovan saw his shot comfortably saved and in the dying seconds of the game United skipper Japhet Tanganga put an effort straight at Zetterstrom.

The result means that Derby have won just once in their opening 12 games of the season.

Sports.title: Portsmouth hit back to beat Millwall
Sports.content:
Thomas Waddingham's fortuitous winner earned in-form Portsmouth a come-from-behind 2-1 victory over Millwall at Fratton Park.

Millwall captain Jake Cooper's attempted clearance ricocheted off Waddingham and into the back of the net in the 82nd minute to settle an error-strewn Championship contest.

Jenson Metcalfe had put the visitors ahead early on after a mistake from Pompey goalkeeper Nicolas Schmid but it was quickly cancelled out by Lyndon Dykes' own goal.

And Waddingham's late winner saw John Mousinho's side record a third win in four matches.

Image: Lyndon Dykes of Millwall fails to stop a shot from Marlon Pack of Portsmouth

Pompey made four changes to the side that started their midweek draw at Wolves, with Zak Swanson, Marlon Pack, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen and Marko Milovanovic replacing Jayden Meghoma, Rocco Shein, Tyrese Shade and Ebou Adams.

Alex Neil made only the two changes for Millwall as Max Crocombe replaced the injured Filip Marschall in goal and Luke Cundle came in for Mark Sykes, while fit-again striker Mihailo Ivanovic made his first appearance of the campaign off the bench.

Millwall made the brighter start with Metcalfe scoring the game's opening goal just six minutes in, capitalising on a calamitous pass forward from Pompey goalkeeper Schmid.

A response came just 10 minutes later when Adrian Segecic's scuffed free-kick deceived Dykes at the near post, forcing the Millwall forward to get the final touch as it nestled into the back of his own net.

An end-to-end first half ended level, but the intensity continued into the second period with both sides desperately trying to battle the wet and windy conditions and each other to take the lead.

Millwall would have reclaimed their lead on the hour mark if not for the heroics of Madiodio Dia, who threw his body on the line on two separate occasions in quick succession to block shots.

Pompey came close to taking the lead in the final 20 minutes when Swanson's right-footed corner caused chaos in the Millwall box, but nobody in blue was able to poke the ball home.

Soon after Waddingham, in his first appearance since August due to injury, almost made an instant impact off the bench when he got close to getting on the end of Adams' cross.

The persistence of the striker was rewarded with eight minutes left when Cooper tried to clear from inside his penalty area but the ball hit Waddingham and flew past Crocombe.

Millwall seemed to run out of ideas and were unable to find their way back in the contest as their winless run extended to three games.

Sports.title: England crush France to remain in hunt for World Cup semi-final spot
Sports.content:
Herbie Farnworth scored a first-half hat-trick as England demolished France

England kept alive their faint hopes of reaching the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals with an 82-0 trouncing of France.

Herbie Farnworth and Dom Young scored hat-tricks as England overcame a nervy start in Perth to boost their scoring difference and remain in the hunt for a last-four spot heading into the final round of pool matches.

England entered the game staring at a 150-point deficit following Samoa's landslide win in Papua New Guinea earlier on Saturday. They took a sizeable chunk out of that with a 14-try victory but require another big win when they face the Kumuls in Wollongong on Friday, and will also need a favour from Tonga against Samoa on November 1.

Mikey Lewis came off the bench to score twice with Matty Ashton, George Williams, Victor Radley, Jez Litten, Jack Welsby and AJ Brimson also crossing for England while Hugo Savala kicked 26 points.

Brimson was the architect for many of those tries, the full-back shredding France in an awesome attacking display, with Junior Nsemba and Kai Pearce-Paul producing a number of eye-catching carries and offloads in contact.

Dom Young also bagged a hat-trick

England were met with stiff resistance during the opening quarter as some superb France defending kept them scoreless, but the dam burst on 23 minutes and those early efforts took its toll as they faded badly towards the end of the first half.

Brian McDermott's side scored six tries in the final 17 minutes of the first period, Farnworth grabbing three of those to help England into a 36-0 half-time lead.

The rout continued in the second half and France's persistence with going short from kick-offs led to a hat-trick try for Young on 62 minutes, while Brimson bagged the try his performance deserved with three minutes remaining.

Brimson shines for England

AJ Brimson starred at full-back

England full-back Brimson was deservedly named man of the match after a brilliant display that included a try, three assists and five line breaks.

He told Premier Sports: "It's my first win for England. Disappointing last week [against Tonga]. We had a tough assignment today, we needed a good performance to give ourselves a chance. It's not always easy having that mindset.

"The first 20 was a grind but credit to our spine and halves, keeping us calm and we knew we'd get them in the end."

McDermott hails 'enormous' effort

England head coach Brian McDermott:

"What we've done today, given the context, is just enormous. We had to win big but, as any coach will tell you, nobody thinks like that. You think, 'we've got to win'.

"We had some real good, candid conversations this week about what that actually means and we've been able to do that without getting distracted in chasing points.

"Everything was measured, everything was inside the game model, everything was what we planned to do - well, most of it at least.

"Whatever the results are next week, we want to finish strong against PNG [Papua New Guinea] as well, and if that means we're going home next Sunday night, that will be a big disappointment to us.

"But I'm not sure what more we could have done."

What's next?

England need another big win when they face Papua New Guinea in their final pool match in Wollongong on Friday (9.05am). Attention will then turn to Tonga vs Samoa on Sunday (9.05am), where they require a favour from the former.

Sports.title: England suffer 15-try defeat against rampant Australia
Sports.content:
Jocelyn Kelleher scored two tries and kicked nine goals against England

England were outclassed in a 78-0 defeat to defending champions Australia but remain in with a chance of reaching the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals.

Stuart Barrow's side shipped 15 tries on a unforgiving evening in Perth and must quickly regroup ahead of Friday's final pool match against Samoa, where the winner will advance to the last four.

England had no answer to a rampant Jillaroos, who dominated from the first whistle and kept a clean sheet for the second successive game. But they will be frustrated by the manner in which they gifted Australia territory and scoring opportunities during an error-strewn and ill-disciplined first half.

England's start was disastrous. They were caught offside from the kick-off and duly punished as Jaime Chapman opened the scoring, and another botched restart followed as Jenna Foubister kicked the ball straight into touch.

Australia aren't a side who require such easy access into the opposition half and they cut loose, scoring seven tries in a one-sided first half where their one negative was a suspected broken wrist suffered by Julia Robinson.

England also lost Eva Hunter to injury - the second rower could only watch on with ankle on ice as her team-mates fell to a heavy loss.

Jaime Chapman celebrates scoring the first of Australia's 15 tries

After conceding two early Chapman tries, England thought they had hit back when Anna Davies crossed in the corner. However, replays showed her knee was in touch before she grounded the ball.

That was as good as it got. With the excellent Tamika Upton returning kicks with interest and Jocelyn Kelleher combining with half-back partner Tarryn Aiken to devastating effect, Australia kept the scoreboard ticking over with regularity.

Kelleher scored twice with Isabelle Kelly and Abbi Church also dotting down to make it 36-0 at half-time.

The onslaught continued with Aiken, Olivia Kernick, Quincy Dodd all scoring within 10 minutes of the restart, before Church scored one of the tries of the game after Kelleher regathered her own grubber and combined with Upton to put the winger over.

Makenzie Weale, Tiani Penitani Gray, Kelly and Shayley Bent added further tries as Australia threatened to better the 90-4 victory over England in Las Vegas last year, but England refused to throw in the towel and popped up with some big defensive moments despite being under constant pressure.

Focus must quickly shift to Samoa but Barrow faces a challenge to lift his players.

Barrow shifts focus to 'elimination football'

England rush out after a goal-line drop-out

England head coach Stuart Barrow:

"It's really disappointing when you see a score like that. You can't be happy with it in any way, shape or form, but it felt different. It felt like we competed a lot more on plays.

"We didn't give up, we just kept trying, but once they get a roll on like that I don't think any team in the world can compete with them. They're just too quick, too skilful and they're too fast for our girls at that stage.

"When you're defending back-to-back-to-back sets, then suddenly fatigue comes in, and that accelerates the momentum that they've got on you."

On facing Samoa: "It's elimination football. A lot of our girls have played a lot of elimination football over the last couple of years. It makes it do or die and that's exciting. We've just got to recover from this, first and foremost.

"We've got an early flight tomorrow [Sunday] to Sydney and then a trip on to Wollongong. We've just talked about how we handle the recovery from now because we've got a five-day turnaround until we play next and we'll be focused on that."

What's next?

England play Samoa in their final pool fixture on Friday (6.45am), where victory in Wollongong will secure a semi-final place.

Sports.title: Aston Villa and Jackson end Manchester City’s perfect run with stunning win
Sports.content:
Manchester City have added a loss in the Premier League to the one to the Premier League, as their perfect on-pitch record vanished at Aston Villa. The two most in-form strikers in England did battle and it was Nicolas Jackson’s double that meant his side come out on top against Erling Haaland.

City are certainly fallible, losing for the fourth time in a row here, and it was a reminder that life will not always be as simple as their first seven games. Mistakes cost them as Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma played their part in Jackson’s goals, which will give him greater pleasure as they ended Enzo Maresca’s perfect start.

Aston Villa started at lightning pace while City cowered. City were so ponderous in the opening stages they gave away a corner after being penalised for taking too long over a goal-kick. After two mistakes last weekend against Ipswich gave away goals, Guéhi would have hoped for a more reassured performance, but he was once again punished for the opener, miscontrolling a Rúben Dias pass to allow Jackson in, with the striker rifling home in the sixth minute.

City did not look like a side who had won every Premier League game thus far. The hosts, on the other hand, had forgotten their mid-table tag and were more reflective of the team sitting second in the Champions League standings with three wins out of three.

Quick Guide Aston Villa 2-1 Manchester City key facts Show • Aston Villa are the first side to win three successive Premier League games against Manchester City since Liverpool in December 2016 (run of four). • Three of Manchester City’s last five Premier League defeats have come against Aston Villa, while they have lost four successive away league games to a side for the first time since February 2023 against Tottenham Hotspur. • Erling Haaland (pictured) has scored in each of his last seven Premier League appearances; it’s his joint-longest run in the competition along with between August and October 2022. • After conceding eight goals in their opening nine matches of the 2026-27 season in all competitions, Manchester City have since conceded nine times across their last four games. Opta Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The inflatable fruit enthusiasts got to witness an improving situation on the pitch as City enjoyed plenty of possession in and around the Villa area, but Iliman Ndiaye, who had a penalty claim waved away, and Rayan Cherki, were thwarted by Zion Suzuki’s reactions. Villa defended with commitment and discipline to limit the space available with great success.

While City constantly threatened and Ndiaye struck the post, there was always a nagging doubt that Villa could cause problems on the counterattack. Jackson against the unfortunate Guéhi was starting to look like a mismatch, as the defender was unable to cope with the speed and physicality of the striker. Guéhi was booked for pulling down Jackson on the edge of the area to leave him in a precarious position on every level, forcing him to be replaced at the break.

View image in fullscreen Erling Haaland rises the highest to equalise for Manchester City. Photograph: Ed Sykes/Getty Images/Sportsphoto/Allstar

The entertainment and exhilaration of the first half was always going to be difficult to sustain, but there was no backing down from either side. City’s endeavour was rewarded in the 53rd minute when Ndiaye got the better of Ian Maatsen and found Haaland finally able to connect with a cross, heading home from close distance for his 13th of the season. It is hard to keep that man quiet.

There was a sense City could take control of the match and went close through Josko Gvardiol and Doku, but once again lapsed. Villa did not need an invitation to burst into life and were unable to contain them as the ball moved quickly from back to front, with Jackson sending the ball out to Ibrahim Mbaye before getting on the end of the cross for his second. Donnarumma should have done better, letting the shot slip under him.

The academy trio Phil Foden, Rico Lewis and Ryan McAidoo were sent on to change things for the visitors and they provided energy, but when chasing the game there was a loss of focus. Passes and crosses were misdirected and needless bookings were collected. If City could point to perfection before this, the label was rapidly fading as the seconds ticked by.

Jackson went off with eight minutes left to a standing ovation. Haaland had a very late chance to level, but Maatsen cleared off the line, to ensure Jackson and Villa claimed the glory.

Sports.title: Relief for Slegers as Russo rescues Arsenal against Tottenham in WSL
Sports.content:
Alessia Russo’s second-half penalty delivered relief, a reprieve and a chance for a reset as Arsenal came from a goal down to earn a precious second win of the WSL season in the north London derby.

At a rain-lashed Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Gunners were again their own worst enemy, forced to come from behind after Cathinka Tandberg’s headed opener, before Georgia Stanway levelled and Russo powered in the penalty that gave them the lead they protected defiantly.

With the pressure building on Renée Slegers and her Arsenal players after five games without a win, at times it felt like they were trying to disprove the phrase “you can’t dig yourself out of a hole”.

Arsenal had looked a little shaky in the opening few minutes but they settled, built possession and started to pose a threat. A failure to carve out clear-cut chances and capitalise on any period of dominance has been the running theme of their season. They lacked fight and there was sloppiness too, with too many overhit passes putting the ball out of play or gifting possession to their opponents.

That the opener came from a Tottenham corner was unsurprising then. Victoria Pelova swung the ball in and Tandberg rose above her two markers, Stanway and Emily Fox, who failed to even to rise and challenge, and headed home.

Spurs’ joy was short lived, however, as Stanway made up for her marking error four minutes later by arriving to meet Russo’s cut back and powered the ball in off the crossbar. Arsenal continued to keep the ball and probe, but failed to find another opening in the first half.

After the break there was concern for Tottenham when Alice Sombath’s leg seemed to twist awkwardly as she stretched for the ball and the club’s record signing left on a stretcher to be replaced by Ella Morris, who made her return from an anterior cruciate ligament injury towards the end of last season.

After the lengthy stoppage, Russo forced a huge save from Lize Kop as she attempted to turn in Caitlin Foord’s cross from close range, and the forward put her hands to her head and screamed in frustration at the missed opportunity.

View image in fullscreen Georgia Stanway equalises for Arsenal in the 17th minute. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

It didn’t take long for that frustration to transform into elation, though. The resulting corner from Kyra Cooney-Cross was headed on by Leah Williamson at the near post and Lisa Baum’s effort came back off the post. Spurs’ clearance bounced off the raised arm of Morris and the referee pointed to the spot.

After sending Kop the wrong way and driving the ball low into the corner, Russo raced to the large corner of Arsenal fans and leapt into the air in an empathic celebration.

Now Slegers and her players need a run of form and luck in their games against Benfica, Aston Villa and Liverpool before the trickier trio of Barcelona, London City Lionesses and OL Lyonnes.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: Portsmouth ride luck to beat Millwall; Norwich back to winning ways
Sports.content:
Thomas Waddingham earned in-form Portsmouth a come-from-behind 2-1 victory against Millwall at Fratton Park. Jake Cooper’s attempted clearance ricocheted off Waddingham and into the net in the 82nd minute to settle an error-strewn contest.

Jenson Metcalfe had put the visitors ahead early on after a mistake from the Portsmouth goalkeeper, Nicolas Schmid, but it was quickly cancelled out by Lyndon Dykes’s own goal.

Waddingham’s fortunate winner means Portsmouth have won three of their last four matches while Millwall have taken just six points from their last seven games.

Patrick Bamford was injured in the act of scoring Sheffield United’s equaliser in a 1-1 draw with 10-man Derby at Bramall Lane. Bobby Clark gave the visitors a first-half lead with Bamford levelling the scores in the 79th minute, only to go off after falling awkwardly.

Norwich halted a six-match losing streak with a 3-1 comeback win at Charlton to ease pressure on their head coach, Philippe Clement. Charlie Kelman fired Charlton into an early lead, but Paris Maghoma equalised for the visitors, who then went ahead through Mathias Kvistgaarden and wrapped up victory via an Ivan Mesik own goal.

It was Chalton’s first defeat at The Valley this season and they are now without a victory in nine Championship matches.

Quick Guide League One roundup: Marshall sinks Foxes Show League One roundup: Marshall sinks Foxes Callum Marshall scored a dramatic stoppage-time winner as Luton heaped more pressure on Leicester's manager, Russell Martin, with a 2-1 victory. The 10-man Foxes appeared to have earned a point when Liam Cullen struck a brilliant equaliser five minutes after John Lundstram had seen red. But Marshall struck in the fourth minute of added time as Martin’s side suffered a fourth league defeat in 11 games. Luton had led after 39 minutes when Jordan Clark dispossessed Caleb Okoli and teed up Nakhi Wells to sweep home. The Foxes were reduced to 10 men with five minutes left when Lundstram received his second yellow card for a lunging tackle on Isaiah Jones. Huddersfield maintained their promotion push with a 2-1 victory over rock-bottom Wigan. Ilias Bronkhorst and Derensili Sanches Fernandes were on target for the Terriers, before Christian Saydee replied late on. Huddersfield went top, ahead of Stockport, who play Notts County on Saturday afternoon. PA This story will be updated after later matches Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

On Friday, Will Lankshear scored twice as a Middlesbrough battered Bolton 5-1. Aidan Morris, in-form Lankshear and a Lewis Brunt own goal before half-time set the Teessiders on the way to a 10th successive win over their hosts in a run stretching back to 2014.

Thelonius Bair gave Steven Schumacher’s side hope in the second minute of first half stoppage-time but the former Bolton loanee Amario Cozier-Duberry, who contributed nine goals and 10 assists for the Trotters in League One last season, made the points safe after 73 minutes. Lankshear added a fifth five minutes later with his 11th league goal.

Sports.title: Vincent Kompany to miss ‘weeks, not days’ with virus treatment, say Bayern Munich
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich expect Vincent Kompany to miss an extended period as their head coach continues his hospital treatment for a virus after collapsing on the training pitch on Friday. Speaking at a press conference on Saturday, Bayern’s sporting director, Max Eberl, confirmed Kompany was still in hospital in a stable condition.

Kompany’s English assistant coach, Aaron Danks, will replace the 40-year-old for Sunday’s Bundesliga match at Freiburg. Eberl said examinations were continuing to determine the nature of the former Manchester City and Belgium captain’s condition, with a recovery timeframe yet to be determined.

“Vinnie will be given all the time he needs. We’re not starting to put together any timeframes. We need to firstly figure out what it is and then we’ll discuss calmly what recovery time is to be. We won’t be talking about days, but weeks. We need to all be clear on that.”

Taking Saturday’s press conference in Kompany’s absence, Danks said he had spoken with the former centre-back briefly on Friday but only to wish him well. “I explained to him that we wouldn’t be having no football conversations. It was just checking in on his health and making sure he’s OK.”

Danks added: “All the football operations are in our hands and we’ll work together as a team to keep the club moving forward.”

Bayern’s second team’s game was postponed on Friday after Kompany’s collapse but Eberl said the club did not consider trying to postpone Sunday’s Bundesliga game. “I think the greatest joy for Vinnie would be for us to play well tomorrow and, ideally, get a positive result,” Eberl said. “That would probably be one of the best things we could do to help him recover.”

Danks confirmed the Germany captain, Joshua Kimmich, who has been on bereavement leave since Tuesday, would also miss Sunday’s game.

Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday’s home Champions League 2-2 draw with Arsenal despite missing the pre-match press conference due to the virus. Speaking after the Arsenal game, Kompany said his body reacted after he tried to push through the illness. “I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn’t listen to my body – and then at some point my body just said: ‘Enough is enough!’”

Sports.title: Older, calmer, but still playing the hits: Mourinho and Madrid primed for clásico
Sports.content:
José Mourinho has done the por que?, the printout and the press conference no-show, and he’s been here only three months. The Real Madrid manager has played the classics without even playing a clásico. Not yet anyway, but it’s time: on Sunday night he returns to the stadium he first arrived at 30 transformative years ago as Bobby Robson’s talented young translator, and last visited in 2013 as the most famous manager in football.

The coach who once declared “today, tomorrow and always, Barcelona in my heart,” and claimed he would only ever go to Real Madrid to destroy them, has been entrusted with attempting to bring about the destruction of Barcelona. It is not the first time: if his return is about nostalgia, which it is, that’s wrapped up in their rivals too.

“The clásico is just another game in the championship but to say it’s a game like any other would be to lie, totally unreal,” Mourinho said on Wednesday, and he knows. As for Barcelona’s latest star, he’s looking forward to seeing Mourinho again. “I love the needle,” Lamine Yamal says. “The Mourinho-Guardiola era, I loved all that. That’s football. Sport is serious but I want a show and we have more fun.”

There are bigger things, sure; life beyond Barcelona. Madrid’s astonishing Champions League record since Mourinho was last here – following up the elusive decima, the 10th title which had evaded them for 12 years, with the 11th, 12th, 13th, 14th and 15th in 10 years – played out without Barcelona. There has not been a European clásico since the 2011 Champions League semi-final when the man Pep Guardiola had just called the puto amo, the fucking master, produced his por que speech, asking why Barcelona were favoured by the continent’s referees and accusing Uefa of fixing it for them.

Yet right now it doesn’t feel as if anything is bigger, this week’s Champions League matches framed around what they meant for the game that really matters, even with Barcelona going to Paris. The rivalry is always there; in Mourinho’s case it is at the heart of it. The day he got the Madrid job in 2010 was the day he won the Champions League with Inter but its genesis lay in the semi-final, when he had sprinted across the Camp Nou pitch, finger raised, celebrating. Madrid were relieved and grateful, spared the sight of Barcelona lifting the European Cup in their stadium and shown how to stop a team that appeared unbeatable. Mourinho, leaving the Santiago Bernabéu in Florentino Pérez’s car while his joyful players returned to Milan, was asked to repeat that with Madrid.

Pérez, who had presided over the galácticos’ failure and walked away, had returned in 2009 but won nothing. Instead, Barcelona dominated. They had the core of Spain’s World Cup 2010 winners: six starters in the final. Madrid needed a culture shift, to go to war, a manager to rule over the dressing room. “This year’s galáctico is José Mourinho,” the president said.

View image in fullscreen José Mourinho (left) with Bobby Robson and Ronaldo after Barcelona defeated Paris Saint-Germain in the Cup Winners’ Cup final in 1997. Photograph: Colorsport/Shutterstock

By the time Mourinho left, it had turned nasty, his enemies internal too. They had been, Mourinho later said, “three intense, almost violent years”. Yet Pérez had always felt drawn towards the only manager he has truly liked. Including when Mourinho was belligerent; especially when he was belligerent. Mourinho had, Pérez said, returned Madrid to their rightful place. After every subsequent success the president called to tell him he started this. And if Mourinho’s first clásico brought a 5-0 defeat, Barcelona going on to win the league and Champions League; if his final season had ended trophyless; and if Guardiola had won twice as many trophies, it was also true that of the four competitions Guardiola failed to win at Barcelona, three were taken from him by Mourinho.

Time has passed, things have changed, but the parallels are clear. Madrid have gone two years without a trophy. In the first of those, Barcelona won the league with two weeks to spare, completing a domestic treble. They had defeated Madrid four times, scoring 16 goals. Last season they wrapped it up with three weeks to spare via a clásico victory as incontestable as their superiority throughout a season when Madrid’s splits played out in public. Then Spain won the World Cup with eight Barcelona players in the squad. Madrid’s only representative, Marc Cucurella, joined the club after the tournament started.

If this was a crisis, it was time for Mourinho. A man whose flaws had been forgotten over time, nostalgia eclipsing all else. A man with the authority – a man afforded the authority – to impose on the dressing room. One with the personality to fight, go to war again. With just about everyone, and Barcelona especially. When you listened to Pérez’s extraordinary rant in May, the quiet part said out loud, all campaigning and conspiracy, politics and paranoia, it made sense.

When it comes to the still unresolved Negreira case, in which Barcelona paid the vice-president of the referees’ committee, José María Enríquez Negreira, more than €7m between 2001 and 2018, there is substance to Madrid’s complaints. Barcelona have denied corruption, saying Negreira worked as an adviser, but that case has become the centrepiece of Madrid’s discourse, unlike when the two clubs were still holding out in the Super League. It doesn’t help when the league president likens your TV channel to Joseph Goebbels’ propaganda.

Whether those complaints have validity now is a different question; whether the discourse of conspiracy does is another step again, even when decisions go against you. Every mistake – and decisions that are not even mistakes – is framed as a machiavellian plan, the insinuations constant – when they are not said outright.

When Mourinho arrived he said he was older, calmer, but here he is. In defeat, perhaps he was always likely to be. After losing to Betis, he asked por que? (Why? Because that’s the rule, the decision correct.) After losing to Atlético, he turned up with a printout. And then he didn’t turn up to the press conference after he had run on to the pitch to embrace Vinícius Júnior after the Brazilian scored against Villarreal only for the goal to be ruled out and Vinícius sent off for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair. That led to a four-game suspension, the forward ruled out of the clásico.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The reason for the no-show was that Mourinho didn’t want to risk saying something that would earn him a suspension for the clásico, the game. And he is happier now, if only for a little while, something shifting. When last Saturday Barcelona made it 11 wins from 11, averaging more than four goals a game, most agreed they would win the clásico and the title would be done: they were flying, led by Lamine Yamal, while Madrid, beaten twice, hadn’t taken off. Mourinho’s team had not been very good, familiar problems still there. In short, there was not much football.

The previous Wednesday Madrid had delivered another of their seemingly inexplicable comebacks, from 3-1 down at Roma, to win 4-3 in the final seven minutes, but was there really anything to build on? It turned out there was something of an explanation. In those minutes Arda Güler played, Yan Diomande played, Fede Valverde played at right-back, and Vinícius didn’t play.

It seemed so obvious to everyone, including the manager. So he did it again, and Madrid scored four against Sevilla – three of them glorious – last Sunday and four more against Leipzig on Wednesday, Diomande belting in a wonderful volley once Vinícius had gone off. The night before, Barcelona conceded four at the Parc des Princes.

Hansi Flick admitted he prioritised the clásico over PSG, leaving out Rodri and withdrawing Pedri and Raphinha early to keep them fresh for a game that could be decisive and tends to shape a season. But he has injury concerns at the back and warned his players that 15 goals conceded is too many. Mourinho couldn’t resist complaining that Madrid have a day less rest for the clásico – something perhaps mitigated, much like any analysis, by playing at home against Leipzig rather than away at Paris Saint-Germain – which got the excuse in early, more evidence of how “they” have it in for his side.

“We need to cut the gap and we can only do that by winning,” said the Real Madrid goalkeeper, Thibaut Courtois, of the six-point deficit. “We’re going with confidence.” Yet things do feel a little better now, defeat for Madrid not inevitable, a title still there to played for and something like a team taking shape. “I had to get to know them,” Mourinho said on Wednesday night. “I’ve only been here 105 days; it’s not long.”

Sports.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
Sports.content:
Take captaincy from Fernandes, then try to sell him and Martínez

The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor.

Ensure the players connect with the fans

Seven hundred United supporters made the trip to Lombardy and witnessed a horror show in incessant rain as their team folded against Cesc Fàbregas’s side. Yet, as always, the faithful will be there on Sunday desperate to cheer their men on against Bournemouth and beyond. Carrick constantly talks of how fans are the club’s lifeblood but do all of the players feel this? Performances such as that at Como will surely be averted if a base creed citing how fundamental supporters are to United is laid down to the squad by the manager.

Play with joy again

Sir Alex Ferguson’s flying wingers, Sir Matt Busby’s holy trinity of Best, Law, Charlton, the “attack, attack, attack” mentality: none of this is evident currently on the field; part of what Carrick admitted on Friday had been “lost”. What is needed is a return to this tradition, and this team are capable as was evident in the spirit of Carrick’s first game of his second tenure. Then, on 17 January 2026 at Old Trafford, he sent out an XI that went at Manchester City from the opening whistle, gave Pep Guardiola’s men zero time to breathe, and a rousing 2-0 victory sent all of a United stripe home jubilant. This, basically, was Carrick’s side last season, a proposition that played with a bounce that landed in third place. This term the smile has vanished and a prevailing sense of doom has settled over the club – precisely what Carrick had vanquished after the gloom of Ruben Amorim’s final days. Time to restore the cavalier edge.

United have suffered, in part, this term owing to Carrick’s drive to move to a more possession-based proposition. The problem is one of the key midfielders recruited to execute this, Youri Tielemans, does not have the legs for a central role, and so has been fielded at 10, while Kobbie Mainoo, who can run an engine room, is injured, and Fernandes’ penchant for running about, out of position, means gaps appear where a ball receiver should be.

Give the young players more of a chance

In Fernandes, Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire, Diogo Dalot, Marcus Rashford, Amad Diallo and Martínez there is a core of long-serving senior players who are not performing. To wake this cadre and freshen the mood from what feels a pervasive staleness, why not blood, more regularly, the younger players? The “play the kids instead” trope can be a cliche but it is a truism for a reason: youth has zero to lose, should run around with a smile and can brighten the darkest of times. Shea Lacey, a nippy wide man, Harry Amass, a promising left-back, and the Fletcher twins, Jack, a clever No 10, and Tyler, a defensive midfielder, are 19 and have 22 appearances between them. None could do worse than those senior players ahead of them.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Get the attack firing

In seven of their 11 games this season United have scored either a solitary goal or none, a shocking statistic that shows up how dysfunctional the attack is and, as part of the creative collective, the midfield too. United have only 10 goals in seven league outings and in three Champions League games have managed five – four of these against the minnows Sabah. At Como there was, again, zero pattern of play, control and a paucity of chances that has to be a serious concern. This has to change or a relegation fight could be United’s. A more off-the-cuff style, allied to an attacking outlook, would suit Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and others and start menacing teams again as United did when beating City, Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool last year.

Sports.title: Premier League news: Spurs’ nine injuries ‘normal’, says De Zerbi; ‘emotional control’ keeps Blues red-free
Sports.content:
1. ‘Big confidence’ in Tottenham’s injury team Roberto De Zerbi has insisted Tottenham’s medical staff bears no responsibility for the numerous selection issues he faces against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday where his club will attempt to win for only the second time in 42 matches in all competitions. The head coach has been boosted by the return of Pedro Porro from injury while he reported that Andy Robertson, Omar Marmoush and Dominic Solanke were “good” in light of fitness concerns. De Zerbi had bad news elsewhere, however, saying Destiny Udogie was still out and Tosin Adarabioyo was a doubt. James Maddison did not train for three days after the home win over Coventry on Monday and may not be ready, while caution will remain the watchword with Dejan Kulusevski, who played his first minutes since May 2025 against Frank Lampard’s side. De Zerbi could be without nine players due to injury when the longer-term absentees are factored in, including Lucas Bergvall and Savio. Rodrigo Bentancur is suspended. Spurs appointed a new performance director last season in Dan Lewindon and he oversaw a clutch of new hires in the performance department in July. De Zerbi made the point that the club would make a “total report” on injuries at the end of the season but “so far we can’t say anything bad about the medical staff”. “I am convinced our medical staff this season is high level. I have big confidence because I know how they are working and they are good enough to believe in. We are suffering a normal situation in football.” De Zerbi went into detail on the cases of Porro, Bergvall and Robertson to reinforce his argument. “Pedro won the World Cup with Spain,” he said. “Maybe with the head or body he didn’t recover enough to start this season without a pre-season. He already suffered in the World Cup the muscular problem of the hamstring. He felt it in training and played anyway against Aston Villa [on 29 September] because he pushed to come back before the right time and he suffered another injury. What is the responsibility of the medical staff? “Bergvall turned his knee and felt pain in the first minute against Manchester United [on 10 October]. He finished the game and the day after he felt pain. What is the responsibility of the medical staff? Nothing. Robertson played four games in a row for Scotland [during the recent international window] and after that felt a small problem and did not play in Manchester. He played 65 minutes against Coventry and was fatigued. It’s normal fatigue for a player who played [so much].” On Spurs’s terrible record at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi said: “What is the problem? We didn’t play in the past for Tottenham and I was not the Tottenham coach in the last seasons. We have already many problems and this is not a problem.” David Hytner

2. Alonso: ‘We keep calm, don’t lose our heads’ Xabi Alonso has said greater emotional control is behind the improvement of Chelsea’s disciplinary record, one that saw them picked up 11 red cards last season. Alonso focused on the problem after becoming manager last summer and has been rewarded with better behaviour from his new side. Chelsea, who can expect a feisty encounter when hosting Tottenham on Saturday evening, have not had a red card this season and showed intelligence when they won 2-0 at Everton last weekend. “For me it comes a lot with emotional control, with the control of the game,” Alonso said. “If you are focused on what you have to do, you are prepared for what’s going on. Normally you don’t make that many mistakes and don’t overreact to certain situations. “This is a fundamental part of the game, to have that emotional control. The momentum is coming – we keep calm, I don’t lose my head and I don’t get stupid yellow cards, make stupid penalties.” Alonso pointed to Chelsea signing more experienced players last summer. “I think it helps,” he said. “Absolutely. It helps for that composure that you need in certain moments. You have players that sometimes, even during the game, they take a step back to see this is happening and now we need to keep focused and calm.” Stamford Bridge is usually at its loudest when Spurs turn up at a ground where they have not won since 2018. Alonso expects an “electric” atmosphere but admitted that playing with control in the Premier League can be tough when crowds feed off duels and end-to-end football. “It is really difficult,” he said. View image in fullscreen Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has played down the impact of his influence from the touchline: ‘I have from the touchline some kind of input but the real one is from the players.’ Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters “To find a total dominance in a game when you are in full control and you have few problems like in other leagues, it’s difficult to find it in the Premier League unless you have become a top, top, top team. That’s why you can’t rest on your laurels when you are 2-0 up.” Alonso played down the impact of his influence from the touchline. “It is people on the pitch,” the Spaniard said. “I can say many things but sometimes I don’t reach [the players], I don’t control. I can do it in advance. I have from the touchline some kind of input but the real one is from the players. Normally the most experienced ones. It’s the ones that feel it.” Chelsea are without Emiliano Martínez after the goalkeeper broke his jaw against Everton. Mike Penders will start and Alonso sees similarities between the young Belgian and his compatriot Thibaut Courtois. “I spoke with Thibaut as well when he was in the World Cup, asking about Mike, and he even said that he could see resemblances with Mike,” Alonso said. Jacob Steinberg

3. Go easy on Ngumoha, says Iraola Andoni Iraola has insisted Rio Ngumoha must be allowed to make mistakes and not have his development stifled by “impossible” demands. The 18-year-old sparkled for Liverpool in their Champions League comeback against Villarreal on Tuesday while still adapting to playing on the right wing. It was only a fifth start under Iraola for Ngumoha, who last month became the third-youngest player to make his competitive debut for England, after Wayne Rooney and Jude Bellingham. The Liverpool head coach has described it is a “privilege” to coach the teenager but is wary of too many expectations being heaped on such a young talent. “I feel very lucky to have him but this is a moment when, because he has played well, we cannot straight away put expectations on him super high because it is not fair for him,” Iraola said. “He will still have to make mistakes, he will still have his moments where it is up and down, because this is a natural process that every player goes through. “We cannot straight away put demands on Rio that are impossible to beat. No, we have to help him in this process knowing that he will have good games and probably some games when it is not so good.” Iraola believes Ngumoha’s personality offers reassurance that he will not be unduly affected by the growing attention. The winger has two years remaining on the contract he signed on turning 17 but is expected to be rewarded with a new deal. “I haven’t felt that he’s very affected, positively or negatively, by all the things that are said about him,” Iraola added. “He’s very focused on the football side, on improving his performances and trying to get the things that we need from him. It’s not easy when you are 18 and everyone is talking about you but he knows that what matters is what is happening today in training and the things that he can add to his game. He’s very focused on that.” Liverpool will again be without the injured Dominik Szoboszlai when hosting in-form Brighton on Sunday and Victor Muñoz is doubtful with a knock sustained in last weekend’s win at Brentford. Andy Hunter View image in fullscreen The 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha sparkled for Liverpool in their Champions League comeback against Villarreal on Tuesday. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

4. Farke faces triple injury blow Daniel Farke has been dealt a blow before Sunday’s Premier League game at Sunderland after revealing Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Anton Stach and Noah Okafor are all injury doubts. Calvert-Lewin, whose fourth league goal of the season earned Leeds a 1-1 home draw against Manchester United last week, and midfielder Stach both sustained foot injuries in that match. Winger Okafor is struggling with a thigh strain and all three players are rated “major doubts” after missing out on team training this week. Farke confirmed Daniel James is in restraint after recovering from his recent injury, while Lukas Nmecha, Harry Wilson and Jean-Mattéo Bahoya will also be hoping to feature. Nmecha has made six league appearances off the bench this season and Farke added: “Overall you have to say for a back-up striker, Lukas has scored I think seven goals last season,” said Farke. “Of course, if he doesn’t play each and every minute due to the fact that Dominic was so outstanding, I think this is a really good record and I would have to say in the last game he looked sharp.” Press Association

5. Nothing has changed for us, says Arbeloa Alvaro Arbeloa maintains “nothing has changed” as his Fulham side look to build on a first Premier League win. The Spaniard – who took over as head coach at Craven Cottage in the summer – has come under scrutiny following a testing start to the campaign before easing some of the pressure with a 1-0 victory over Hull at Craven Cottage. Fulham come up against another promoted side at Coventry on Saturday and Arbeloa wants his players to continue to show the same focused mindset. “Nothing has changed for us,” Arbeloa said. “When we were not winning games, we believed that we were doing so many things well, and now we have the same targets, so we should come in and try to win a tough game. “Yes, now we have the reward that we were looking for, and now it is another week, another game, so we need to fight again for the win.” Arbeloa added: “When you are working and you are not winning, it is not easy, so everything is easier when you play well, in the way that you want and you win matches. That is the most important thing, and it is very important for your confidence, and I think we deserve it.” Press Association
