Sports.title: Christian Mbilli May Not Need His Best Against Canelo
Sports.content:
Christian Mbilli could walk away with a victory over Canelo Alvarez without needing the fight of his life next Saturday, October 31, in Saudi Arabia. His relentless pace and trademark volume might easily suffice against a 36-year-old fighter whose offensive engine visibly sputters when pressed to maintain high-gear work.

Canelo clearly talks like the WBC super middleweight champion needs a miracle.

“He’s going to come 100% because he’s going to need it,” Canelo insisted to DAZN Boxing.

That mindset clings to the idea that defeating him demands career-best perfection. His one-sided loss to Terence Crawford last September completely shattered that myth. Crawford used nothing more than crisp footwork, sharp feints, and an active jab to leave Canelo completely flat-footed, snatching the undisputed 168-pound crown with tactical clarity.

Crawford never looked pushed to the brink. He dictated terms using distance, precision combinations, and smart angles, while Canelo simply followed him around the ring unable to pull the trigger with any consistency.

Mbilli presents a very different stylistic problem. He will naturally offer Canelo cleaner counterpunching lanes, yet he will relentlessly drag the Mexican star into deep water by forcing an uncomfortable pace.

Whenever Canelo turtles behind his high guard, Mbilli will let his hands go. Even if those punches crash into elbows and gloves, judges reward activity, and Canelo will have to respond. Landing an occasional explosive counter cannot bail out long stretches of ring hibernation.

Naturally, Canelo still carries dynamite timing and wicked rib-cracking hooks. Careless, head-down rushes could give the decorated veteran the exact highlight-reel openings he craves. Blind aggression rarely secures a victory against elite counterpunchers.

Nevertheless, Mbilli has no obligation to pitch a flawless twelve-round masterpiece. He simply needs to keep the pressure going, deny Canelo the rest breaks he desperately seeks, and make the aging star sweat for every single exchange.

Canelo might be living on past reputation if he thinks Mbilli must deliver a superhuman performance to win. The real question is whether Canelo can muster enough gas in the tank to survive Mbilli on a routine, rock-solid night.

Sports.title: Andy Ruiz vs Dave Allen Targeted For Spring
Sports.content:
Andy Ruiz Jr. and Dave Allen could meet in Sheffield in March or April 2027, with Allen revealing that Matchroom’s Frank Smith has told him the company is targeting that window for the heavyweight fight.

The Fight Wire reports Allen also indicated that he would likely retire afterward. The fight has not been officially announced, and the proposed dates remain a target.

Ruiz (35-3-1, 22 KOs) would enter the bout coming off a defeat against Damian Knyba in September. His last victory came against Luis Ortiz in September 2022, with a draw against Jarrell Miller and another lengthy absence between that win and the Knyba loss.

That represents a dismal drop for a man who battered Anthony Joshua to win the unified heavyweight crown in 2019. Ruiz held all the gold, dominated global sports headlines, and blew the chance to become a generational heavyweight star. He surrendered the titles in the rematch and spent the next seven years fighting just four times.

Allen keeps fighting to stay relevant and earn a living, but nobody expected him to rule the division. He has spent much of his career taking punishment from better heavyweights. Ruiz reached the top, won three world titles, and then wasted the opportunity.

A win over Allen gets Ruiz back in the win column, but beating a domestic trialhorse proves nothing about his ability to mix with elite heavyweights. An upset loss drops him off the boxing map entirely.

Take Allen’s retirement talk with a grain of salt. Sharing the ring with Ruiz hands him a big-name scalp to target along with a solid payday. Even in defeat, a decent showing will keep promoters dialing his number.

Expect Allen to stick around if matchmakers keep waving checks in his face. Giving a former unified champion a real scrap will open doors for future paydays, not push him into retirement.

Right now, the story is Matchroom penciling in that spring date in Sheffield. Calling it a farewell bout looks like wishful thinking, especially since another decent payday will easily tempt him back into the ring.

Sports.title: WBO Set To Strip Denzel Bentley Of Title
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley is set to lose his WBO middleweight title after allowing the deadline to commit to mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernández to pass, leaving his November 7 fight against Shane Mosley Jr. as his next bout.

WBO president Gustavo Olivieri told EverythingBoxing’s Darshan Desai that the organization received no formal communication from Bentley’s team confirming he would go ahead with the Hernández defense within the allotted 24 hours. According to Desai, the WBO will now strip him.

Bentley has already signed to face Mosley Jr. in his Zuffa Boxing debut. That looks like a more winnable fight than defending against Hernández, although Bentley would enter it without the championship he had hoped to keep.

Hernández (11-0, 9 KOs) would be a dangerous fight for Bentley, with the power to knock him out. A loss like that would be a rough way to begin his time with Zuffa.

Bentley would have a chance against Hernández, but this would be a dangerous defense against a challenger who has been finishing most of his opponents. From a career standpoint, accepting the loss of his belt and going ahead with Mosley Jr. is understandable. He keeps his scheduled fight and avoids the immediate possibility of a punishing defeat.

The WBO cannot justify letting him keep the belt while pursuing a side attraction. Hernandez did the work to earn his mandatory ranking, and he shouldn’t be put on hold just because Bentley decided to take a different path.

Vito Mielnicki Jr. could step into the opposite corner against Hernandez for the vacant belt. Mielnicki holds the number two spot in the WBO ratings just behind the Cuban, positioning the American contender as the frontrunner if he accepts an invitation to fight for the strap. Sanctioning body officials have not made an official announcement regarding the pairing.

Bentley can still get off to a good start with Zuffa by beating Mosley, but he’ll be giving up his world title to take the easier fight.

Hernández would then get his shot at the vacant belt against someone prepared to face him.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Talks DAZN Benefits As Inactivity Continues
Sports.content:
Devin Haney credits DAZN with offering the opponents he needs to build his legacy. After 11 months outside the ring, however, he still needs a fight date to turn that explanation into something fans can judge.

Haney has not fought since beating Brian Norman Jr. last November. His DAZN agreement gives him a broadcasting home, but the next opponent and an official event announcement remain the real test of its value.

“All the opponents are on DAZN. Zuffa Boxing, they offered me a ton of money. I’m thankful for that,” Haney told Chris Mannix on DAZN. “I’m thankful for them to reach out to my team, but all the opponents are on DAZN. It’s not just about money for me. It’s about me being the best and me putting on the best fights.”

That is a reasonable explanation for choosing a platform. It is also a promise that requires action. Having potential opponents under the same broadcasting umbrella does not put their names on Haney’s record.

“I’m a legacy fighter. I love the money. The money is massive at DAZN as well. It’s great, but I need to have the opponents too to showcase my skills.”

Haney is getting paid well by his own account. The missing part is the opportunity to showcase those skills. Interviews can explain his intentions, but they cannot replace rounds, title defenses, or victories.

A unification with Liam Paro has reportedly been agreed, although an official announcement is still pending. Getting that fight scheduled would give Haney something concrete to support his comments. Until then, it remains another proposed contest following a lengthy absence.

The inactivity does not establish that Haney alone caused the delays. Negotiations require cooperation. Still, the time comes out of his career regardless of who holds up an agreement.

Prime years pass quickly. Haney can prefer DAZN and have sound reasons for doing so, but his legacy benefits when he fights. Right now, he is explaining what the platform can offer while fans wait to see it delivered.

Sports.title: Rocky Marciano vs Mike Tyson: Speed Against Stamina
Sports.content:
Rocky Marciano against Mike Tyson would match relentless pressure against explosive speed. Both heavyweight champions could end a fight with one punch, but the deciding factor might be whether Marciano could survive Tyson’s early attacks and force him into a longer fight.

The comparison should involve both men at their best. Tyson’s late-career defeats tell us little about how the fighter who demolished Michael Spinks would have handled Marciano.

Tyson would have the advantages in hand speed and weight. Although similar in height, he generally fought substantially heavier than Marciano. His quick combinations to the body and head would present an immediate threat to a fighter who needed to get close to do his best work.

Marciano retired at 49-0 with 43 knockouts and six successful heavyweight title defenses. His unbeaten record did not mean he avoided trouble. Jersey Joe Walcott dropped him in the opening round and led on the scorecards before Marciano knocked him out in the 13th.

Against Ezzard Charles in their rematch, Marciano fought through a severe nose injury to secure an eighth-round knockout. Those victories demonstrated his ability to remain dangerous when a fight was going against him.

Tyson’s first championship reign showed how quickly he could take control. He stopped Trevor Berbick in two rounds to win the WBC title and later knocked out Pinklon Thomas, Tyrell Biggs, Larry Holmes, Tony Tubbs and Spinks. James “Bonecrusher” Smith and Tony Tucker took him the distance, with Tyson winning both fights on points.

Against Marciano, Tyson’s uppercuts would be particularly dangerous. Rocky often advanced from a low crouch, bringing him into range of short punches as he worked his way inside. Tyson could also attack the body before bringing his hooks upstairs.

Marciano’s answer would be to keep punching and deny Tyson comfortable breaks. He attacked the chest, shoulders, and arms when an opponent’s head was protected. Those punches could contribute to wearing Tyson down, although they would leave Marciano close enough to be countered.

Tyson’s peek-a-boo style was more than a stationary high guard. At his best, he used head movement and quick changes of angle to create openings. Marciano would have to deal with that movement before he could establish his own attack.

A longer fight would give Marciano more opportunities. His conditioning and sustained output were major strengths, particularly over 15 rounds. If he could survive the early combinations and continue forcing Tyson to work, his chances would improve.

That does not make an early Tyson knockout inevitable or a late Marciano victory automatic. Marciano could be dropped, while Tyson could win over the distance, as his victories over Smith and Tucker demonstrated.

Tyson would have the stronger chance of an early stoppage because of his speed, combinations, and greater size. Marciano’s best route would be to withstand that opening assault and turn the contest into a prolonged, punishing fight.

Would Tyson’s speed settle it early, or could Marciano survive and wear him down?

Sports.title: WBC World Title Bout Smith vs Puello
Sports.content:
In what will be his first title defense, the WBC super-lightweight world champion Dalton Smith will defend his title against the number one-ranked contender Alberto Puello.

Smith plans on having a successful homecoming while Puello wants to play the role of spoiler, as he looks to become a two-time world champion. The action is set to take place at Utilita Arena in Sheffield, England, live on DAZN.

The most notable victory on Alberto Puello’s record occurred in June 2024 when he outboxed Gary Antuanne Russell and won the vacant WBC Interim title. A short time later, Puello was elevated from Interim to full world champion.

Puello had one successful title defense, and then he lost his title to Subriel Matias. Now the Dominican boxer Alberto “La Avispa” Puello (25-1,11KOs) is ready to reclaim his WBC belt.

Back in January 2026, the British boxer Dalton Smith experienced his crowning moment.

During the course of four rounds, Smith stood inside the pocket and went toe-to-toe with Subriel Matias.

With 55 seconds left to go in the 5th round, Smith landed a hard overhand right that wobbled Matias. Seconds later, Smith connected with another overhand right that sent Matias down to the canvas.

A dazed Matias was able to stand up, but after witnessing him stumble, the referee stepped in and put a halt to the contest. With the victory, Smith won his first world title.

Now Dalton “Thunder” Smith (19-0, 14 KOs) plans to entertain his home fans while successfully defending his WBC belt. He faces a difficult task as the challenger is a very proficient opponent.

The southpaw Alberto Puello is a skilled technical counterpuncher who has a solid jab, he routinely utilizes lateral movement, he has good ring generalship, and a sharp straight left hand.

Dalton Smith is an aggressive boxer-puncher who has a high boxing IQ, good footwork, is an expert at controlling distance, is accurate, has good timing, and punching power.

Alberto Puello believes he’s well prepared for this fight, and on Saturday night he’s going to take back what belongs to him. Dalton Smith also feels he’s ready, and he’s going into this title bout in a particular mindset.

“I have prepared for this like I’m the challenger, and on Saturday night I will prove to the boxing world why I am No.1. I am cool, calm, collected, and I will do it again on Saturday,” Smith stated.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson’s Team Opens Talks With DAZN
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson is looking for a way back into the ring early next year, and manager Jay Prince is actively exploring options with DAZN. Prince insists that chasing a showdown with Devin Haney wasted valuable time, stalling Stevenson after promised fights failed to materialize.

While Prince confirmed dialogue with the streaming giant, nothing is locked down yet.

“We’re having conversations with quite a few people, and DAZN definitely is one of them,” Prince said to Fight Hub TV.

Prince explained that the split from Zuffa Boxing came down to fight delivery rather than money. Financial terms were settled, yet getting viable rivals into the ring proved impossible.

“We had a contract so the purses and different things were pretty much agreed upon. It’s just getting opponent,” Prince said.

According to Prince, several names were listed in the paperwork, but everything ground to a halt around Haney. Once those talks collapsed, Stevenson chose to cut his losses instead of idling.

“We no longer want to go down the road of focusing on this one guy, Devin, when there’s other things to do.”

Prince also shut down talk that Stevenson turned down a $7 million payday to face Rayo Valenzuela.

“Never was discussed with me. And if it was discussed, I would be the first to know,” Prince said.

That rebuttal dismisses rumors of an easy purse left on the table. Still, Prince gave little detail on why none of the other contracted names crossed the finish line.

He took aim at Haney over weight demands too, denying that a rehydration limit derailed the matchup.

“No dehydration clause. We agreed at 45, and Shakur was training for the fight.”

Prince claimed Bill Haney killed the deal by attempting to drag the contest up to 147 pounds, offering his side of an affair both camps view quite differently.

For now, the DAZN talks remain exploratory. Stevenson has a targeted window, but until an opponent signs on the dotted line, the layoff continues.

Sports.title: Richardson Hitchins Declares Keyshawn Davis Fight Off
Sports.content:
Richardson Hitchins says his proposed fight with Keyshawn Davis is off, claiming Davis demanded $6 million for a bout Hitchins had already agreed to nearly two months ago.

If that account is accurate, Davis has put a high price on an opportunity that could help him earn bigger purses. Beating Hitchins would give him something he cannot produce through callouts alone: a quality victory to strengthen his position in future negotiations.

“He was asking for 6ms to fight me,” Hitchins said on social media. “I been agreed to the fight going on 2 months. I was wondering what was the hold up.”

Hitchins also claimed Davis had never earned more than $1 million in boxing. That assertion and the alleged $6 million demand remain his account of the negotiations. The statement does not establish what Davis was offered, how the proposed purse was structured, or his side of the dispute.

Still, Hitchins has put an uncomfortable figure into public discussion. Davis now faces criticism over whether his asking price reflects what this particular fight can generate.

Davis is entitled to negotiate for the biggest purse available. Facing Hitchins is a serious undertaking, and neither fighter should be expected to accept whatever number gets placed in front of him. But the money has to come from someone willing to fund the event.

A competitive matchup does not automatically produce enough ticket sales or broadcast revenue to support every purse request. If Davis wanted $6 million, the people financing the fight would need a reason to believe that investment made sense.

That is where losing this opportunity could hurt him. Hitchins would offer Davis a chance to prove himself against a skilled opponent whose jab and boxing ability could force him to solve difficult rounds. A strong performance would give Davis more to sell the next time he asks for a major payday.

Instead, Hitchins is now telling fans he accepted while Davis priced himself out. That version gives Hitchins the better public argument until Davis provides his own explanation.

The immediate cost is a worthwhile fight slipping away. The longer Davis waits for a purse that satisfies him, the longer he goes without the victory that could make his next demand easier to justify.

Ghana News.title: 22 NYPD officers to visit Ghana for humanitarian outreach and police engagement
Ghana News.content:
Twenty-two officers of the New York City Police Department (NYPD) are expected to visit Ghana from November 10 to 18, 2026, for a humanitarian outreach mission targeting underprivileged children and vulnerable communities.

The mission, organised by the African Law Enforcement Organization (ALEO) under the theme “To Serve and to Protect Beyond Borders,” will combine community support activities with engagements aimed at strengthening professional ties between law enforcement personnel in Ghana and the United States.

ALEO is a non-profit organisation based in Jamaica, New York, comprising active and retired law enforcement and security professionals. It is led by its President, Detective Chibuzo C. Amadi.

The organisation says the mission reflects its commitment to public service beyond policing and geographical boundaries, with a focus on supporting communities in need.

The delegation is scheduled to visit the Ghana Police Service Headquarters on November 10, the day of its expected arrival, for a professional exchange with Ghanaian law enforcement officials.

The officers are also expected to pay a courtesy call at Jubilee House, the seat of Ghana’s Presidency.

The engagements are intended to promote goodwill and strengthen professional relationships between law enforcement personnel in both countries.

Foundations support outreach

The mission has received support from the Magho Foundation, Afro Pop and Exotical Sponges.

The Magho Foundation was instrumental in connecting ALEO with schools and an orphanage in Ghana that it had previously supported.

The connection was facilitated by William Apau, an NYPD officer and ALEO member popularly known as Ministerapau, who founded the Magho Foundation.

The organisers say the outreach will focus on bringing practical support and encouragement to children and vulnerable people in selected Ghanaian communities.

Service beyond borders

The visit reflects the role diaspora-led organisations can play in humanitarian assistance and professional exchange between Ghana and the United States.

For the organisers, the mission is intended to demonstrate how values associated with public service, including protection, unity and community responsibility, can extend beyond the traditional duties of law enforcement.

The delegation is expected to spend eight days in Ghana, undertaking humanitarian activities and professional engagements before concluding its visit on November 18.

Details of the specific communities to be visited and the items or services to be provided have not been outlined in the information released by the organisers.

Ghana News.title: Bawumia meets Ghana Association of Medical Laboratory Scientists to discuss healthcare reforms
Ghana News.content:
New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has held consultations with the leadership of the Ghana Association of Medical Laboratory Scientists (GAMLS) on policy proposals to strengthen Ghana’s healthcare system.

The discussions covered the proposed establishment of a dedicated regulatory council for medical laboratory science, financial clearance for the recruitment of health professionals, local production of laboratory reagents, stronger disease surveillance systems and strategic partnerships with the private sector.

Dr Bawumia said the engagement provided an opportunity to exchange ideas on challenges facing the health sector and explore practical measures to improve healthcare delivery.

Medical laboratory services play a central role in disease diagnosis, treatment decisions and the detection of public health threats. Improving staffing, access to laboratory supplies and professional regulation could therefore affect the quality and reliability of services across the country.

The proposed local production of laboratory reagents also featured among the issues discussed, amid the broader need to strengthen domestic manufacturing capacity and reduce reliance on imported diagnostic supplies.

Dr Bawumia expressed gratitude to GAMLS leadership and members for sharing their perspectives, reiterating his commitment to developing policies informed by stakeholder engagement and the experiences of Ghanaians.

The consultation forms part of his engagements with professional groups on priorities for the country’s healthcare sector.

The proposals would require further policy development, including details on the proposed regulatory council, recruitment arrangements and measures to support local reagent production.

For medical laboratory scientists, the issues extend beyond professional regulation and working conditions to the wider capacity of Ghana’s health system to deliver accurate diagnoses, monitor disease outbreaks and respond to emerging public health threats.

Ghana News.title: Road infrastructure encroachment fuels pedestrian knockdowns
Ghana News.content:
The increasing encroachment on road pavements and other infrastructure by petty traders and hawkers within the Greater Accra Metropolitan Area and other large cities continues to raise road safety concerns, prompting the National Road Safety Authority (NRSA) to start a stakeholder engagement to address the menace.

While malfunctioning traffic lights, broken road signs, faded road markings and bad driver behaviour are driving road crashes and deaths, the situation has been worsened by petty traders who obstruct pedestrian walkways by displaying their merchandise.

For over a year now, the Daily Graphic has observed that some traders display their wares on pavements designated as pedestrian walkways, while others pitch camps at bus stops, forcing drivers to park their vehicles on the shoulders of roads.

In some cases, the drivers park their vehicles on both sides of roads, a development that impedes vehicular movement, creates human traffic and puts pedestrians in danger.

The Central Business District of Accra is bursting with such encroachments; the Mallam Market area and the Kaneshie enclave on the Dr Busia Highway, areas around the Kwame Nkrumah Interchange, as well as Kwabenya to the Achimota Mall are among the areas where the encroachments are rife, leaving city guards and police personnel overwhelmed.

Some of the other areas in Accra that have gained notoriety for the encroachment on road infrastructure by petty traders include Odorkor Tipper to the main traffic light, Madina, Nima-Mamobi, and Agbogbloshie.

The Graphic Road, which stretches from the intersection at the Farisco Traffic Light on the Kwame Nkrumah Avenue to the Obistebi Lamptey Interchange, is also notorious for the encroachment on road pavements, with a new entrant emerging every day.

Between the Graphic Road overpass, near the Graphic Head Office, up to the Farisco Traffic Light is the epicentre for the illegal trading activities on that street.

Traders display their wares on the pavements and portions of the road leading from the Accra Brewery to the Graphic Press House with impunity, and the activity starts

from about 8 p.m. and continues to the wee hours of the following day.

The encroachments, which started from one end of the dual carriageway, have not only become widespread with many traders joining the fray, but both sides of the road pavements are under siege.

To facilitate traffic flow, the police have had to station their men to direct traffic, as commercial vehicles are also cashing in on the presence of traders and shoppers right on the road.

The joint activities of traders, buyers and commercial vehicles have created chaotic situations, as drivers stop in the middle of the road to load, while illegal and wanton U-turns have also emerged with impunity.

Commercial drivers park their vehicles on both sides of the road beyond the Graphic Press House to the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) area as they wait for passengers to board them.

Pedestrians are left vulnerable as they have to weave their way through a sea of vehicles that run bumper to bumper, while personnel from the Motor Traffic and Transport Division (MTTD) of the Ghana Police direct traffic.

Experiences

A driver of a minibus that plies Accra-Kaneshie, Daniel Obeng, explained to the Daily Graphic that he parked his vehicle on the shoulders of the road around the Graphic House because the bus stop had been encroached upon by traders.

“Drivers are supposed to stop at bus stops to load our cars, but the bus stops are now used by traders for commercial activities and that is why we also park on the shoulders of the road to get passengers,” he said.

A 39-year-old cassava dough seller, Yaa Ntreh, complained that she and other traders displayed their wares on the pavements at the Graphic Press House because the CBD was choked.

“We cannot find space at the CBD to sell our wares, so we decided to sell here.

Also, where we are now is strategic; people can easily locate us and buy our goods,” she said.

In the wake of the lawlessness of the traders and drivers, pedestrians remain vulnerable to road crashes.

“If you are walking from Accra Brewery side towards the COCOBOD road and you are not very careful, drivers can just knock you down. You cannot walk on the pavement because it has been taken over by traders,” 27-year-old Adamu Rufai, a shopper, said.

The Daily Graphic observed that at Agbogbloshie, Nima-Mamobi and the Odorkor Tipper, petty traders have taken over pavements leading to the main traffic lights with yams, furniture, wood products and other merchandise.

At the same time, articulated trucks have been parked on both sides of the major road at these places, making the spaces narrow for vehicles to move freely.

Pedestrian knockdowns

Encroachment on the road infrastructure is problematic because it results in pedestrian knockdowns, which account for 33 per cent of deaths from reported road crashes, according to the National Road Safety Authority (NRSA).

The Daily Graphic’s analysis of road traffic statistics from the NRSA revealed that over the past 35 years (1991 to 2025), 63,599 persons died from reported road crashes across the country, with about 20,988 of those deaths resulting from pedestrian knockdowns.

Law on trading on pavements

The new Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2519) and Road Traffic (Amendment) Act, 2025 (Act 1153) outline several prohibitions designed to keep pavements and vehicular roadways clear of informal commercial activities, hawking and unauthorised vending.

Regulation 142 (Selling Goods on Roads and Pedestrian Walkways) declares it an explicit offence to “sell, display, offer for sale or deliver goods on or alongside a road, on a pedestrian walkway, near a railway crossing, under a blind-corner sign or within an intersection.”

For hawking or selling on roads and walkways, Regulation 142 states that offenders caught displaying, selling or delivering goods on roadsides or pedestrian pathways face “a fine of up to 50 penalty units (approximately GH¢600), imprisonment for as long as three months, or both.”

When the Daily Graphic spoke to the Director-General of the NRSA, Abraham Amaliba, on how to deal with the encroachment on roads, he said the authority had started engaging key stakeholders to tackle the menace.

For instance, he said the NRSA had held a meeting with the Ghana Highway Authority (GHA), the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) of the Ghana Police Service and actors in the road sector to help stem the tide.

Again, he said the NRSA had held a meeting with all 29 Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) in the Greater Accra Region to devise a comprehensive strategy to clear encroachers off the streets.

“Then also, when you trade on the pavement, it moves the pedestrian back onto the road to compete with vehicles and that leads to pedestrian knockdowns and deaths,” he said.

Police action

The Director of Education, Research and Training at the police MTTD, Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Alexander Kwaku Obeng, said road safety was about enforcement and the police needed the support of other stakeholders to succeed in enforcing road safety regulations.

"If road markings are faded, it will be difficult for the police to enforce the law in that regard; this is why we are happy that there are plans to upgrade roads and incorporate more road markings," he said.

ACP Obeng also said MMDAs needed to rise to their responsibility of decongesting the roads by taking traders off the pavements.

He stressed that while the police were willing to enforce the law on traders on the pedestrian walkways, political interference made it difficult.

"Enforcement of road traffic regulations had been the weakest link over the years because of human involvement.

The use of technology is what is doing the magic and that is what we should do more," he said.

ACP Obeng also said police enforcement of road traffic regulations through digital means was also focused on tackling speeding by drivers since that was the foundation of many crashes.

Ghana News.title: Minority demands Sammy Gyamfi’s resignation as GoldBod CEO over comments on small-scale mining licences
Ghana News.content:
The Minority Caucus in Parliament has called for the resignation or dismissal of Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi over comments it says suggest that small-scale miners can operate without the requisite licences and permits.

The Caucus has also demanded an unqualified apology from Mr Gyamfi, government sanctions against him and a clear roadmap from President John Mahama to end illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey.

"⁠Mr. Sammy Gyamfi should resign immediately as CEO of GOLDBOD; failing that, he should be dismissed to restore the institution's credibility," part of the statement read.

"A clear roadmap from President Mahama and his government to end galamsey as promised to Ghanaian prior to the 2024 general elections."

In a statement issued by the Ranking Member of Parliament’s Lands and Natural Resources Committee, Kwaku Ampratwum-Sarpong, the Minority Caucus condemned Mr Gyamfi’s reported position on small-scale mining operations outside restricted areas.

The statement questioned the basis for allowing mining without the necessary licences and permits, asking whether such operations could also be permitted in schools, churches, mosques, marketplaces, hospitals, Jubilee House, Parliament and the law courts.

“The New Patriotic Party (NPP) calls on Civil Society Organisations (CSOs), Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs), other political parties, the Clergy, Traditional Authorities, media houses, the Media Coalition Against Galamsey, the Ghana Chamber of Mines, the Trade Unions, Youth Organisations, Market Women, Professional Bodies, Development Partners, the Diplomatic Community, Concerned Citizens and other well-meaning Ghanaians to condemn Mr Sammy Gyamfi’s reckless comments and the NDC government’s approach to solving galamsey issues contrary to what was promised, and to demand accountability for their stewardship to Ghanaians,” the statement said.

The Caucus argued that the position attributed to Mr Gyamfi contradicts the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), particularly Sections 9(1) and 82(1), which provide for licensing requirements for mining activities.

It also referred to Section 89 of the Act, which provides for the designation of areas for small-scale mining, insisting that any such arrangement must comply with the law.

The Minority Caucus outlined a series of demands, including an apology from Mr Gyamfi and a public condemnation of his remarks by the government, together with appropriate sanctions.

The statement further called for a thorough audit of GoldBod’s documentation to establish whether gold purchases can be traced from the mine to the market and whether the purchases comply with responsible-sourcing requirements.

"A thorough audit of the Ghana Gold Board's documentation to verify traceability of all gold purchases, from mine to market to establish responsible sourcing practices."

The Caucus urged President Mahama to present a clear roadmap for ending galamsey and declare a state of emergency in areas it describes as “red flag galamsey hot spots”.

It also called for the formalisation of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) through a Legislative Instrument (L.I.).

"To declare a state of emergency in all the red flag galamsey hotspots and to formalise the establishment and operations of NAIMOS through an L.I. to give meaning and structure to it."

The Minority Caucus said the demands were necessary to ensure accountability and strengthen efforts to tackle illegal mining.

Ghana News.title: NDC elections underway across the country as over 15,000 delegates vote for new executives
Ghana News.content:
The National Democratic Congress (NDC) is holding its internal elections across the country today, Saturday, October 24, with over 15,000 delegates casting their ballots to elect new constituency executives.

The exercise, taking place at designated polling centres, has so far been generally smooth in some constituencies, although delays have been reported at certain voting centres.

In the Central Region, voting is underway in several constituencies, with delegates participating in the exercise to elect executives who will oversee the party's activities at the grassroots level.

At the Cape Coast North polling centre, located at the New Examination Centre of the University of Cape Coast, the Central Regional Police Commander, DCOP Bossman Ohene Boadi, assured delegates and aspirants of adequate security to ensure a peaceful electoral process.

Addressing police personnel during a last-minute engagement ahead of voting, DCOP Boadi warned that the police would not tolerate hooliganism or violence during the exercise.

He emphasised the need for officers to remain vigilant and maintain law and order throughout the voting process.

About 1,350 delegates are expected to vote in the Cape Coast North Constituency, while another 1,050 delegates are expected to participate in the Cape Coast South Constituency.

In the Komenda-Edina-Eguafo-Abrem (KEEA) Constituency, approximately 1,728 delegates are expected to elect new constituency executives from a field of 53 aspirants.

Reports from the constituency indicate that the voting process has been smooth so far, with delegates participating in the exercise.

Meanwhile, in the Volta Region, about 2,300 delegates are expected to participate in the elections in the Ho Central Constituency.

At the OLA Senior High School polling centre, the electoral process has been proceeding smoothly despite a delayed start.

The elections form part of the NDC's internal democratic processes aimed at selecting constituency leaders to manage party affairs and strengthen its organisational structures.

Security personnel have been deployed to maintain order at voting centres, while party officials and election supervisors oversee the process.

Ghana News.title: GTA CEO responds to Abeiku Santana’s concerns over access to her office
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA), Maame Efua Houadjeto, has responded to concerns raised by her one of deputies, Gilbert Abeiku Aggrey Santana, over difficulties accessing her for urgent official consultations.

In a letter written to the Board Chairperson of the Authority, Mrs Houadjeto said she operates an open-door policy, particularly for executive and senior management officers, and questioned the suggestion that her availability had been a challenge.

“In as much as I am surprised and disappointed that the letter does not reflect the true state of my availability to you as my deputy Chief Executive Officer, I propose that we strengthen our internal consultation and communication arrangements through the following measures,” she stated.

Her response follows a letter dated 22nd October 2026 in which Mr Aggrey, the Deputy Chief Executive Officer responsible for Marketing and Special Duties, appealed to the Minister of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Abla Dzifa Gomashie, to intervene in what he described as recurring difficulties in accessing the CEO for consultations on urgent operational matters.

In his letter, Mr Aggrey said he had, on several occasions, requested meetings through the CEO’s secretary or personal assistant, only to be informed that she was unavailable.

He said the situation had made it difficult for him to obtain timely guidance, approvals and decisions needed to carry out his responsibilities, particularly in domestic tourism, special events and marketing.

“This situation sometimes causes delays in operations, stakeholder engagements, and the implementation of key assignments,” Mr Aggrey wrote.

He stressed that his concerns were not intended as a personal complaint but were aimed at addressing what he considered a communication gap within the institution.

“My intention is not to make a personal complaint, but to highlight a communication gap that needs to be addressed in the interest of effective management and institutional efficiency,” he said.

Maame Efua proposes measures to improve communication

In her response, Mrs Houadjeto acknowledged the need for timely consultations and decisions, particularly on matters with operational, financial, strategic or stakeholder implications.

She proposed five measures to improve coordination between the two offices and the Authority’s executive management team.

These include scheduled executive consultations to review departmental priorities and operational challenges, as well as a clear procedure for flagging urgent matters and escalating issues when scheduled meetings are not possible.

She also proposed that requests for meetings be properly communicated, acknowledged and scheduled by the relevant officers, taking into account the urgency and importance of each matter.

Other measures include clarifying delegated responsibilities and approval processes, and encouraging regular engagement among members of the executive management team to minimise delays and ensure the consistent implementation of decisions.

Mrs Houadjeto said the measures were intended to improve the Authority’s overall management processes rather than address individual concerns alone.

“I wish to emphasize that the objective of these measures is not merely to address individual concerns, but to strengthen the overall effectiveness of our management processes and promote a more responsive, coordinated, and results-oriented institution,” she said.

CEO calls for collaborative working relationship

The GTA chief executive said management remained committed to professionalism, institutional discipline and harmonious working relationships within the executive management team.

She also expressed confidence that the two offices could continue to work together despite differences in schedules, operational demands or administrative processes.

“I value the contribution of the Deputy Chief Executive Officer to the Authority and expect that we will continue to work collaboratively, with mutual respect and a shared commitment to achieving our mandate,” she stated.

“Differences in schedules, operational demands, or administrative processes should not become impediments to the effective performance of our collective responsibilities.”

Mrs Houadjeto proposed a meeting at the earliest mutually convenient opportunity to agree on practical arrangements for implementing the measures outlined in her response.

Ghana News.title: Africa launches West Africa research programme to speed up outbreak response
Ghana News.content:
A new regional initiative is seeking to strengthen West Africa’s preparedness for public health emergencies by connecting research institutions and enabling faster, more coordinated responses to disease outbreaks.

The Africa Research Preparedness Programme for West Africa is designed to address gaps in research coordination that experts say could delay critical interventions during outbreaks of diseases such as Ebola, Mpox, Lassa fever and COVID-19.

Despite the presence of skilled scientists and established research institutions across the continent, preparedness remains uneven, with some clinical trial sites facing challenges transitioning from routine research to emergency response.

Head of Africa Strategy and Engagement at the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), Shingai Machingaidze, said the programme would adopt a hub-and-spoke model to connect existing research capabilities and support coordinated action during outbreaks.

She said the approach would allow countries to work together on research protocols and evidence generation, with the goal of activating clinical research responses within 10 to 15 days of an outbreak.

“We have the capacity. What we’re trying to make sure we do better is how we all work together to respond to the same outbreak,” she said.

“We are putting together what we call a hub and spoke model to build a coordinated capability to respond. We need speed to respond to outbreak and we cannot do that if we have not prepared enough.”

The programme is expected to provide a common platform for institutions across West Africa to align priorities, share expertise and strengthen emergency research systems.

Regional institutions join effort

The initiative brings together several organisations involved in public health research, regulation and outbreak preparedness.

They include the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), the African Medicines Agency, the World Health Organization’s Regional Office for Africa, the Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research, the Medical Research Council Unit The Gambia, the International Vaccine Institute (IVI) and CEPI.

The collaboration is intended to improve the ability of research institutions to mobilise their expertise and resources when outbreaks occur, rather than work in isolation.

Associate Director-General of the International Vaccine Institute in South Korea, Birkneh Tadesse, said operational research and clinical trials were also important to efforts to develop vaccines and support responses to outbreaks, including Ebola.

“IVI is trying to work on operational research and clinical trials on drugs on vaccines. There is the east and central Africa preparedness programs in the response to the Ebola outbreak also,” he said.

Turning research capacity into rapid action

The programme comes amid continued concerns about Africa’s ability to respond quickly to emerging and recurring infectious diseases.

Experts have warned that the presence of research facilities and scientific expertise does not automatically translate into an effective emergency response without coordination, advance planning and systems that can be activated quickly.

The initiative seeks to address that challenge by strengthening links between institutions before outbreaks occur, allowing researchers to coordinate protocols and prepare for clinical studies when emergencies arise.

Its effectiveness will depend on sustained investment, clear coordination arrangements and the ability to translate research findings into timely public health interventions.

The target of activating clinical research responses within 10 to 15 days will be a key measure of whether the programme can help close the gap between existing research capacity and the urgent demands of an outbreak.

Ghana News.title: Protect children from sexual abuse, Raissa Child Protection Initiative urges
Ghana News.content:
The Raissa Child Protection Initiative over the weekend held a community durbar at Agbeve, Sowutuom, in Accra to educate residents on child sexual abuse prevention and the need to protect children from all forms of sexual exploitation.

The programme forms part of efforts by the non-governmental organisation (NGO) to raise awareness of child protection, educate parents and caregivers on their responsibilities, and encourage community members to report suspected cases of abuse to the appropriate authorities.

Founder of the NGO, Ms Raissa Sambou, said protecting children from sexual abuse required the collective responsibility of parents, caregivers, traditional authorities and other members of society.

She said children needed safe environments where they could speak about uncomfortable experiences without fear of blame or punishment.

Madam Sambou stressed that children who experienced sexual abuse were never responsible for what happened to them and urged adults to listen to them, take their concerns seriously and seek appropriate assistance when necessary.

She noted that both boys and girls could be victims of sexual abuse and called for equal protection and support for all children, regardless of their sex.

She also urged parents and caregivers to educate children on body boundaries, inappropriate touching and how to seek help from trusted adults.

Ms Sambou cautioned that perpetrators could be people known to or trusted by children, adding that parents needed to remain vigilant and establish safeguards to protect their children.

She further called on community members not to conceal abuse to protect family relationships or reputations, stressing that the safety and welfare of children must take priority.

A legal practitioner and member of the Raissa Child Protection Initiative project team, Alhaji Yussif Baba Suleman, said the 1992 Constitution of Ghana contained provisions to safeguard children's rights, making it important for people to understand those rights and ensure they were respected.

He urged the public not to shield perpetrators of sexual abuse because they were relatives, friends or people close to their families.

Alhaji Suleman said offenders must face the full rigours of the law to ensure justice for victims and deter others from committing similar offences

He also called on residents to report suspected cases to the appropriate authorities rather than resort to secrecy or informal settlements.

The durbar highlighted the importance of community participation in preventing child sexual abuse and ensuring that affected children received the necessary protection and support.

Beneficiaries of the forum thanked the organising team for the valuable information shared and hoped such programmes would be held frequently in communities across the country.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
