World.title: Ukraine says Starlink restored as attacks continue in Russia and Ukraine
World.content:
Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US are expected to meet in Abu Dhabi next month.

Share Ukraine says Starlink restored as attacks continue in Russia and Ukraine on social media

Ukraine says restrictions on its military’s Starlink satellite connections have been lifted after more than a week of disruption that hampered drone operations against Russian forces.

Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said on Saturday that Starlink and Starshield connections were stable on equipment travelling above 400 kilometres per hour (250 miles per hour). He credited talks with Washington and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s diplomacy.

Ukraine relies heavily on Elon Musk’s SpaceX satellite services for communications and drone missions. However, who ordered the restrictions remains unclear, with US President Donald Trump denying responsibility while defending Elon Musk.

The disruption further strained relations between Kyiv and Washington, already under pressure over Trump’s agreement to temporarily lift sanctions on Russian diesel and allow US imports.

Trump also called earlier this month for Ukraine to have a new president, then suggested on Monday that someone other than Zelenskyy should negotiate for Kyiv. The exchanges follow their public confrontation at the White House in February 2025.

Talks planned in Abu Dhabi

The lifting of the Starlink restrictions comes as the United States seeks to revive peace negotiations between Moscow and Kyiv. Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US are expected to meet in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November, more than four years after Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed the planned negotiations on Friday, while Zelenskyy also announced agreement on technical-level meetings.



It comes as Trump credited his wife, Melania Trump, with securing a local ceasefire in Oleshky, in southern Ukraine’s Kherson region, which Russian forces have occupied since 2022.

Subsequent Ukrainian and Russian statements putting the ceasefire’s start on October 27, with the humanitarian operation planned for October 29.

Deadly attacks continue

A Russian missile strike on Lozova, in Ukraine’s northeastern Kharkiv region, killed a man and wounded two others on Saturday, regional Governor Oleh Syniehubov said, while in northern Ukraine, a Russian attack on Chernihiv on Friday killed a man and wounded at least 25 people, local authorities said.

Shelling in Kramatorsk killed one person and wounded six, including three children, according to Donetsk officials. In nearby Sloviansk, attacks on Friday killed a 62-year-old woman and wounded four people, Mayor Vadym Lyakh said.

Ukraine reported strikes inside Russia on Friday and overnight into Saturday, including on Togliatti’s Togliattikauchuk petrochemical plant, a major synthetic rubber producer. Mayor Ilya Sukhikh confirmed industrial damage but reported no casualties.

Ukraine also said it struck Oryol’s Proton electronics plant, which it says makes missile components. Regional Governor Andrei Klychkov reported three deaths in an attack on an unidentified facility.

Authorities in Russian-occupied Crimea reported power cuts after overnight Ukrainian attacks.

Russia’s Defence Ministry said air defences intercepted a SCALP cruise missile, four Neptune missiles and 1,297 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones over 24 hours, TASS reported. The figures could not be independently verified.

World.title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Can Kylian Mbappe’s Real Madrid and France record win it?
World.content:
Despite not winning silverware last season, Mbappe has been public about his goal to clinch the Ballon d’Or.

Share Will Mbappe succeed in his relentless media push to win the Ballon d’Or? on social media

He may not be the bookmakers’ favourite or last season’s top goalscorer, but Kylian Mbappe has left no stone unturned in his media push to win the upcoming Ballon d’Or.

The 2025-26 season, on which the award is judged, left the Real Madrid talisman without a trophy for club or country.

On an individual note, however, the France captain set records, which he hopes will finally land him the coveted award that carries no cash prize but, alongside the accolade, increases a player’s worth and status.

“Being the all-time top scorer in World Cup history, overtaking all the great legends in the history of the sport in the most important tournament there is, is something that really stands out,” Mbappe said last month.

“Who am I voting for? Myself.”

In an award voted for entirely by journalists, Mbappe believes he is the most deserving contender in the run-up to Monday’s ceremony in London.

But how does his performance compare with other shortlisted nominees? Al Jazeera breaks it down:

World Cup exploits with France headline Mbappe’s bid

The 2026 FIFA World Cup in North America marked another spectacular individual campaign for Mbappe, who not only won the Golden Boot for the top scorer for the second successive campaign but also became the all-time top scorer in World Cup history.

His 22 World Cup goals in as many matches keep him at the top of a star-studded list that includes Argentina’s legend Lionel Messi in second place on 21 and German ex-international Miroslav Klose third on 16.

Madrid see a Real return from Mbappe

Beyond international duty, Mbappe also enjoyed an excellent individual campaign with his club, Real. His tally of 25 goals earned him the honour of La Liga’s top scorer, while he was also the Champions League’s leading marksman with 15 goals.



Those numbers have made Mbappe confident he will win the prestigious Ballon d’Or for the first time.

“I was top scorer in all the biggest competitions, and I think that this could be a good year for me, and I really feel it,” the ex-PSG star said.

No silverware weakens Mbappe’s case

Despite Mbappe’s solo brilliance, there is nothing in his trophy cabinet from last season to put forth a strong case.

Amid a turbulent campaign first under Xabi Alonso and then Alvaro Arbeloa, Real finished second in La Liga and were bundled out of the Champions League by Bayern Munich in the quarterfinals, leaving Mbappe and Los Blancos ending a second straight season without major trophies.

To make things worse, France came fourth at the World Cup after losing to Spain in the semifinals and England in the third-place playoff.

Even though Mbappe was often the lone hero in many of Real or France’s games, he failed to win a trophy, unlike his close contenders Lamine Yamal, who won the World Cup with Spain and La Liga with Barcelona, and Bayern’s Harry Kane, whose three trophies last term include a Bundesliga title.

Mbappe shrugs off trophyless season for France and Real Madrid

Those differences do not seem to bother Mbappe, though.

“They won’t announce a team in the envelope; they will announce a player,” Mbappe told RFI radio station, referring to the Ballon d’Or ceremony.

“The ability to perform individually and produce eye-catching moments – that’s what stands out to people for an award like this.”

While Mbappe’s self-promotion has been rampant in recent months, his club manager, Jose Mourinho, has also backed the 2018 World Cup winner.

“We know who has made history this summer, and he’s not from PSG or the Spanish national team,” Mourinho said.

History suggests trophies matter in Ballon d’Or triumph

Over the last decade, every Ballon d’Or winner won at least one trophy during the years they were crowned the best player.

Ousmane Dembele, the 2025 winner, enjoyed a trophy haul that included leading PSG to their first-ever Champions League title, while Spain’s midfield maestro Rodri won the Euro 2024 with Spain and the Premier League with Manchester City among his accolades when he was named the Ballon d’Or winner two years ago.

The last time a player won the Ballon d’Or without a major trophy in his cabinet was in 2013 and coincidentally featured another Real player: Cristiano Ronaldo.



At that time, Ronaldo lifted his second Ballon d’Or, also ending Messi’s four-year winning streak.

The forward earned the award purely for his individual brilliance, scoring 66 goals for club and country, in a season when Portugal failed to progress beyond the 2012 World Cup playoffs and Real were the league’s runners-up.

Ronaldo’s 2013 triumph proves that while odds are not in Mbappe’s favour, he still has a slim chance.

After nine nominations and a third-place finish in 2023, many would argue that Mbappe’s moment to kiss the coveted Ballon d’Or trophy is long overdue.

World.title: Man City beaten at Aston Villa as perfect Premier League start ends
World.content:
Nicolas Jackson scores twice – either side of an Erling Haaland header – as Aston Villa beat Man City 2-1 at Villa Park.

Manchester City’s perfect Premier League start came to a crashing halt in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa as Nicolas Jackson’s double extended an upturn in form for Unai Emery’s new-look side.

Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club, but failed to find a solution to City’s struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost in each of the past four seasons.

After Jackson blasted home the opener after just six minutes, Villa relied on a brilliant goalkeeping display from Zion Suzuki to keep City at bay.

Erling Haaland briefly levelled early in the second half only for Villa to respond on the hour mark when Jackson drilled home Ibrahim Mbaye’s cross.

Four years on from Emery’s arrival, which has transformed the club from a sleeping giant into a Champions League club, the Spaniard is working more magic despite seeing the spine of his squad in recent seasons decimated.

Six players from the side that started Villa’s victory in last season’s Europa League left during the transfer window.

But the recruitment of the likes of Jackson, Suzuki, Mbaye and Johan Manzambi is already paying dividends after a slow start to the campaign.

Until now, City have managed to shrug off the cloud hanging over the club’s Premier League future to keep winning on the field.

The 10-time English champions are appealing a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking financial rules between 2009 and 2018 that could lead to swingeing sanctions, including relegation.



There was little sign of that distraction affecting Maresca’s men, but they were made to pay for two sloppy defensive errors.

A heavy touch by Marc Guehi presented Jackson with possession for the opening goal as he cut inside Elliott Anderson and blasted high past Gianluigi Donnarumma.

City largely dominated the remainder of the first half, but could not find a way past Suzuki.

Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov were all denied before Ndiaye struck the post.

City’s pressure finally told on 52 minutes when Haaland powered in a header from Ndiaye’s cross for his 13th goal in 10 appearances this season.

Josko Gvardiol nearly completed the comeback when Suzuki turned his blistering drive onto the crossbar moments later.

Instead, it was Villa who got the decisive third goal.

Mbaye was played in behind the City defence and from his cross, Jackson’s low effort should have been saved by Donnarumma.

The visitors pressed in vain for another equaliser to allow Arsenal the chance to move level on points at the top of the table when they host Everton later on Saturday.

A sixth win in seven games in all competitions for Villa lifts them up to sixth.

World.title: Do abstaining voters hold the key to Brazil’s 2026 presidential election?
World.content:
Sao Paulo, Brazil – The first time she voted in a Brazilian presidential election, in 2014, Larissa Campelo voted for centre-right Senator Aecio Neves. Four years later, in the next presidential race, she supported a centre-left candidate, former Sao Paulo Mayor Fernando Haddad.

But ahead of what is expected to be one of Brazil’s tightest presidential run-offs ever, the 30-year-old mother of one has decided she has had enough with politics.

She is abstaining from the vote on Sunday, just as she did during the first round of the election on October 4.

Voting is compulsory for most Brazilian adults. But Campelo is part of a historically large chunk of the electorate sitting out this year's presidential race.

Some 33.4 million Brazilian adults did not show up to vote in the first round, resulting in a 21 percent abstention rate, the highest for a general election since 1998.

“It’s my form of protest. I don’t want to dirty my hands with these candidates,” said Campelo, who lives in the Sao Paulo city of Araraquara.

“This isn’t apathy. It’s because I don’t feel there’s anyone qualified enough to earn my vote.”

But appealing to abstaining voters like Campelo may prove to be a path to victory in Sunday's run-off.

World.title: Rybakina readies for title defence at Ningbo Open in final with Fernandez
World.content:
The world number one will face Leylah Fernandez in the final after the unseeded Canadian beat Czech Marie Bouzkova.

Share Rybakina readies for title defence at Ningbo Open in final with Fernandez on social media

Defending Ningbo Open champion Elena Rybakina overcame Russian sixth seed Diana Shnaider 6-3, 7-5 in the semifinal to reach another title clash and remind rivals of her threat before next month’s WTA Finals.

The world number one will face Leylah Fernandez in the final on Sunday after the unseeded Canadian beat Czech Marie Bouzkova by the same 6-3, 7-5 scoreline in the earlier semifinal at the Yinzhou International Tennis Centre in the eastern Chinese city.

Australian and US Open champion Rybakina, who arrived for her title defence after a bruising defeat in Beijing and a foot injury that forced her out of Wuhan, showed flashes of her best form despite a few wobbles against the 13th-ranked Shnaider.

“She [Shnaider] played really well, and it’s always difficult to play against left-handers. We don’t have so many on the tour,” said Rybakina, who faces a similar test against Fernandez.

“I needed some time. The returns were not as bad, but during the rallies, to switch the pattern was a little bit of an issue for me, but I’m happy I managed to win in two sets.”

An aggressive start with powerful winners from deep helped three-time Grand Slam winner Rybakina take full control of the opening frame, which she sealed on her 11th set point after a sudden dip in form.

‘So many opportunities’

“It was an important game, and it was a long one,” added the top-seeded Rybakina.

“It was on my serve, and it was a struggle … I was playing the first balls really well, but I couldn’t close the game … so many opportunities, but I’m glad it went my way. She played some great shots and great rallies.”



The 27-year-old continued to struggle with the accuracy of her first serve in the next set, but won the crucial points and carved out a 4-3 advantage with a break, only to be broken to love in the 10th game.

Rybakina responded strongly to get her nose in front again in the next game with some big hitting, before closing out the victory with a much more assured display on serve to take her place in the final.

She will aim to further sharpen her game in Sunday’s final before turning her attention to the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo next week and then launching her WTA Finals title defence at Indian Wells from November 8.

“It’s never easy,” Rybakina said about winning back-to-back trophies at the Ningbo Open. “Of course I’ll try to do my best. I’m going to fight and give my all tomorrow.”

World.title: Sudan’s soaring fuel prices make getting by harder for workers
World.content:
Azhari Mohamed drives his minibus and eight passengers seven times a day from the Shagar neighbourhood in the Port of Sudan to the city centre and back again.

But despite the long hours – working from 6am to 9pm – fuel shortages in the city have made it difficult for the 60-year-old to make a living.

Azhari’s minibus uses three gallons (11 litres) of petrol a day, costing him about 105,000 Sudanese pounds ($11.30 a day, according to Sudan’s parallel-market exchange rate). With fuel increasingly difficult to obtain, he now spends two days on the road and a third day queuing for fuel.

He can spend more than five hours waiting in line when he needs to fill the tank of his minibus and often finds petrol has run out before his turn comes. When that happens, he goes to the back of the queue at another petrol station hoping to fill up there.

The shortages have led to price rises with a gallon (3.8 litres) of petrol now costing 40,000 Sudanese pounds ($4.30) in Gazira State, south of Khartoum, while in Port Sudan it is 35,000 pounds ($3.80) a gallon.

“We can no longer work because of the fuel shortages. The transport fares are no longer enough to cover the cost of running the vehicle and our household expenses,” Azhari told Al Jazeera.

He says the long hours spent queueing for petrol is time he could spend earning money to support his family.

“I spend long hours of the day waiting to refuel, so I have to work extra hours at night to make up for the time I lose during the day,” he said. “My livelihood depends on what I earn each day.”

After subtracting his vehicle’s operating costs, Azhari has just 50,000 Sudanese pounds ($5.40) left a day, barely enough to cover the needs of his family, which includes his wife and daughter who is at university and needs support for her tuition fees and daily expenses.



“We just need fuel to be available so we can work,” he said. “If fuel is available, we will not face this obstacle.”

Due to the crisis, Sudan’s Transport Chambers Union, which regulates public and private transport services, this month raised intercity bus fares by 40% and minibus fares by 30%.

Aziza Ibrahim from the Umm al-Qura neighbourhood of Port Sudan, works as a cleaner to support her four children. Just getting to work by bus has become a huge financial burden for the 38-year-old, who has cut back her work days to three times a week due to the high travel costs.

Before the war, a journey from her home to the main transport station in the city centre cost 700 Sudanese pounds ($0.08) per passenger. Fares have since risen to 2,500 pounds ($0.27) on some routes, while others charge 2,000 pounds ($0.22).

“I go to work three days a week to reduce transport costs. I need 11,000 pounds ($1.18) a day for the round trip between my home and workplace,” she told Al Jazeera.

Transport costs now consume nearly half of Aziza’s monthly salary of 400,000 pounds ($43), while costly treatment for her diabetes is another financial burden.

“Sometimes I have to borrow money just to be able to go to work. I repay it at the beginning of the month when I receive my salary, which is barely enough to cover my family’s needs,” she told Al Jazeera.

According to the United Nations Development Programme, the war has pushed average incomes in Sudan back to levels last seen in the 1990s.

That is partly due to the effects of the civil war on Sudan’s oil sector. Fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and rival paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) began on April 15, 2023.

Last year, the Ministry of Energy and Petroleum estimated war-related losses at $20 billion. The World Bank has reported that attacks on the Balila oil field disrupted supplies to the Khartoum refinery, which previously met about 60% of the country’s demand for petrol and liquefied petroleum gas.

War damage has seen a sharp decrease in oil production, leaving Sudan reliant on imports amid the global fuel crisis that has pushed up prices of gas, petrol and diesel, among other commodities.

Economic analyst Sidi Ohaj said that the government requirements for petroleum importers have also contributed to the shortages. They include a stipulation that importers must deposit 200kg of gold in the Central Bank and own fuel storage facilities in order to operate in Sudan. Some importers have been unable to meet those requirements, forcing them out of the market which reduces supply.



“One of the causes of the current crisis is the government’s decision to regulate the operations of petroleum import companies,” Sidi told Al Jazeera. “Some companies did not meet the requirements, which led to their exit from the market. This reduced supply relative to demand.”

The government needs to urgently ease import procedures to increase domestic supplies, he said, with shortages affecting the wider economy.



But as the war between the United States and Iran continues to disrupt global energy markets, there is little hope the situation will improve any time soon.

“The continuation of the war [in Sudan], particularly drone attacks that threaten infrastructure across Sudan, is one of the main challenges facing the oil sector,” Sidi told Al Jazeera.

Prices have also risen due to the energy crisis, impacting the purchasing power of citizens and profits of businesses.

Ahmed al-Haj is a local trader in Omdurman market who sells skincare products, such as petroleum jelly, which he packages himself . He said high energy prices are costing almost all areas of his business.

“The raw materials for the products I sell are imported. Higher diesel and petrol prices have increased the cost of transporting a tonne of goods by 30 to 50 percent,” Ahmed told Al Jazeera.

“That increase is then reflected in the price of the products.”

When electricity cuts force him to use a fuel-powered generator for heating or packaging, the additional fuel costs add to his daily bills.

Deliveries within Omdurman, which previously cost 5,000 Sudanese pounds ($0.70) now cost between 10,000 and 12,000 pounds ($1.07 and $1.29). Reaching customers in other states has become impossible due to the high transport costs.

“Transport and distribution workers have also reduced the number of trips they make, leading to goods piling up at traders’ premises,” he added.

World.title: Who was behind the deadly church shooting in Jordan?
World.content:
Authorities are investigating the rare attack on a Christian church; the assailants remain unidentified and at large.

Share Who was behind the deadly church shooting in Jordan? on social media

Security forces in Jordan are searching for three gunmen who opened fire at a church in Karak governorate on Friday, killing eight people and injuring dozens more, according to Jordan’s Ministry of Health.

King Abdullah II said those behind the attack would face the “harshest penalties”, as he offered his condolences to the victims’ families. He has ordered a review of the country’s security procedures for responding to terrorist attacks.

Authorities are calling this rare attack on a Christian place of worship an act of terror, with the perpetrators yet to be identified.

Here’s what we know about how the attack unfolded, and what was behind it.

What happened during the church shooting in Karak?

On Friday afternoon, three masked gunmen opened fire during a funeral in a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hamoud.

Survivors said they heard an explosion just after the start of the service. Two attackers who arrived in a vehicle were joined by a third carrying a semi-automatic rifle. They entered the church and opened fire for several minutes.

One survivor, Nasser al-Burqan, a lawyer, told the Reuters news agency that one of the attackers, standing about two metres (6.5 feet) away, pointed a handgun at him and opened fire.

“When everything finally quietened down, I looked out the window behind me, and I saw two [assailants] – one was masked, the other was not; he was carrying a handgun,” said al-Burqan, a lawyer.

Later, his son, who had also been present, called him to say he had been shot in the leg and was being treated in hospital.



Tarek Ammarin, who was visiting a relative injured in the attack, now in hospital, said: “A massacre, a massacre in every sense of the word.”

Bahjat al-Rushda, mayor of Shihan village in Karak, joined a list of officials condemning what he called a “wicked” attack.

“God willing, this country will remain safe,” he said.

State news channel Al-Mamlaka reported that security forces were deployed to the church and were in pursuit of the two suspects who had arrived in a vehicle.

How many people were killed or injured?

Eight people were killed in the shooting, including seven who died at the scene and one who succumbed to her injuries hours after the attack, Jordan’s Petra news agency reported on Saturday.

Of the 40 people injured, 27 are still in hospital. The Director of Prince Ali Military Hospital in Karak said one person is in critical condition, after undergoing surgery.

Who carried out the attack?

The identity of the three attackers has not been confirmed, with government statements referring to them as “unknown assailants”.

Security camera footage of the attack has been circulating online, however. Video broadcast by Al-Mamlaka shows three people shooting outside the church and running towards its entrance.

Other footage also shows the attackers opening fire on a group of men outside the building trying to flee.

Jordan’s Interior Minister Mazin Al-Farrayeh said a group of “extremists” that have “no relationship to humanity” were responsible for the attack, though no specific groups were mentioned.

Why was the church targeted?

Prime Minister Jafar Hassan said on Friday that the attack was a by-product of terrorist ideology and “blind extremism”, but did not give specifics about the attackers.

The motive remains unclear since the attackers’ identities have yet to be revealed.

Where is Karak, and what do we know about its Christian community?

Karak governorate is about 120km (75 miles) south of Amman and is home to many from Jordan’s Christian minority, which makes up about 300,000 of the country’s population of 11.5 million people.

Taylor Luck, senior Middle East correspondent at the Christian Science Monitor, told Al Jazeera that Jordan’s Christians “pride themselves on [their] interfaith solidarity and coexistence”.

He said that Christians and Muslims have lived side-by-side in Karak for generations and that if the attack had been carried out in an attempt to divide the community, it is more likely that the “community come[s] back even stronger”.



Jordan is also home to many biblical sites that draw visitors from around the world.

What has the response been to this shooting?

Several countries, including Azerbaijan, Iraq, Poland, Palestine and Qatar, have issued statements condemning the attack and expressing their solidarity with Jordan.

Ahmed al-Tayeb, the grand imam of Al-Azhar in Cairo, a leading Sunni religious institution, offered his condolences to the families of the victims, calling the shooting a “heinous terrorist attack”.

“This crime contradicts the teachings of the Abrahamic religions and reveals that its perpetrators are devoid of all compassion, humanity and morality,” he wrote in a social media post.

The United States embassy in Jordan also released a statement on X offering condolences to victims and survivors of the attack.

“On behalf of the American people, we offer our most heartfelt condolences to the victims and survivors of the terror attack today at a church in Karak, Jordan,” it said.

The Jordanian Prime Minister declared three days of mourning following the attack, with flags to be flown at half-mast over government and public buildings.

Has Jordan experienced similar attacks before?

Yes, although they are rare.

In 2016, the ISIL (ISIS) group carried out a series of attacks across Karak, including a deadly siege on a Crusader-era castle in which 10 people were killed, including a Canadian tourist and seven police officers. Dozens of others were injured.

Four attackers were later killed by Jordanian security forces following a long standoff.

World.title: Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits
World.content:
Ukraine now has a "stable connection" to Starlink, its defence minister has said, after its military suffered days of restricted connectivity on the satellite internet network.

Kyiv relies on the Starlink and its military-grade counterpart Starshield for piloting drones and operations within Ukraine, but last week accused US President Donald Trump of telling owner Elon Musk to place limits on it.

This meant drones would lose connection when travelling at 161km/h (100mph) or more, it said. Trump denied doing so before saying Musk had "put it back".

Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said that speeds of more than 400km/h were now possible on the network, indicating that full capability had been restored.

"This result is above all important for our front, for our soldiers, for the operation of drones, for logistics and for communications," he said in a statement on Saturday.

Ukraine's military uses the network of 10,000 low Earth orbit satellites extensively for military operations, particularly in remote areas on the battlefield.

Ukraine uses both the civilian service Starlink and the more secure Starshield, which Musk said was controlled by the US military when he suggested the Pentagon could be behind the recent issues.

Russia is not authorised to use Starlink, so when Ukraine sends long-range missiles or drones deep into Russia to hit oil refineries, the network does not work.

The debacle over Starlink began last week, and emerged during a broader diplomatic row between Trump and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.

Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market - a move criticised by Ukraine and its European allies.

World.title: Arrest made after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
World.content:
Police in the southern German state of Bavaria have detained a 33-year-old German man during a fire at Adolf Hitler's Alpine mountain retreat, the Kehlsteinhaus, also known as the Eagle's Nest.

Dispatchers in Traunstein received a fire alarm from the building at 21:15 local time (19:15 GMT) on Friday and firefighters found it engulfed in flames. No injuries were reported, while difficult terrain hindered efforts to extinguish the blaze.

Police said they apprehended the suspect riding a motorcycle near the scene and told reporters that any possible motive was still being examined.

Some 200 emergency personnel were deployed and a criminal investigation has been launched.

Local police official Gerhart Holzinger told a press conference there was currently no evidence of any further suspects.

The residence, above the town of Berchtesgaden, was one of several buildings in the area used by the Nazi dictator and his entourage during World War Two.

Hitler and top Nazi officials used his nearby Berghof residence to plan the invasion of the USSR in 1941 and the whole complex was considered one of his headquarters.

He also used the area as a backdrop for propaganda films portraying him as a lover of animals and nature.

Local media reported that site had been "largely destroyed", with the public urged to avoid the area.

Bavaria's Interior Minister Joachim Herrmann told reporters that the site would "under no circumstances remain a ruin", broadcaster BR24 reported.

"It is important that we continue our work of remembrance," he said.

World.title: Father who killed Oregon school gunman describes anguish over children he couldn't save
World.content:
A father who fatally shot a gunman at his daughters' school in the US state of Oregon has described his anguish over being unable to save more pupils after "hearing children pleading for their lives".

Three students and a teacher were killed by a 16-year-old former student at Silver Rail Elementary School earlier this month. The attacker was then killed by Kaylub Giamanco.

"I want to apologise for not saving their babies," Giamanco, who has been hailed as a hero, said of his thoughts for the parents of the children killed, in an interview with Oregon Public Broadcasting (OPB) that aired on Friday.

"The gratitude for saving people's children is awesome, but there were ones that I didn't save."

Giamanco, 36, said he wanted to meet the victims' families and "cry with them and hold them".

He credited a teacher who fought the attacker with giving him the chance to intervene without losing his own life.

"I would love to give her a hug because that's a real true hero," he said.

The students who were killed were all boys, aged five, eight and 11. They were among six people in total who were shot in a classroom at the school, police said. Alongside the teacher who was killed, another child and a teacher were wounded.

Giamanco told OPB that the day of the attack began with breakfast and making packed lunches. He and his wife had spent extra time getting their daughters ready because it was school picture day.

The carpenter had taken lunch to work but decided to go home to eat with his wife instead. That decision brought him past the school as the attack began.

He initially wondered whether someone carrying a long gun was playing a prank. Then he saw him fire at a pickup truck and head towards the school.

Giamanco retrieved a handgun from his vehicle and called emergency services.

"I said, 'I'm sorry, I have to go in. People are going to die'," he told the broadcaster.

He followed the attacker, who shot through the school's locked glass doors. Hearing children pleading for their lives and more gunfire, Giamanco crawled towards the building.

"I told myself this is probably the last thing that I'm ever going to do," he said.

World.title: British woman dies after trying to rescue sons swept away at sea in the Bahamas
World.content:
A British mum has died after attempting to rescue her two sons when they were swept away while snorkelling in the Bahamas.

The Royal Bahamas Police Force said officers on the island of Bimini launched an investigation into the sudden death of a 36-year-old British woman on Tuesday.

The force said it believed the woman - thought to be from Stapleford in Nottinghamshire - had been snorkelling with her husband and two sons near the southern point of the island when a strong current reportedly swept both children away.

In an attempt to rescue her sons, "the woman was also swept away", police said. The children were subsequently rescued from the water.

In a statement, posted on social media, the Royal Bahamas Police Force said: "According to the preliminary report, shortly after 10am, officers at the Alice Town police station received information that a female was unresponsive at the North Bimini Ferry Dock.

"Officers responded and, upon arrival, learned that the woman had been transported to the local clinic for medical attention, where she was subsequently pronounced dead by a local doctor despite efforts to save her life.

"Preliminary information indicates that the deceased was snorkelling with her husband and two sons near the southern point of the island when a strong current reportedly swept both children away.

"In an attempt to rescue her sons, the woman was also swept away.

"She was later rescued and transported to the ferry dock, where CPR was reportedly administered.

"Foul play is not suspected at this time.

"An autopsy will be conducted to assist in determining the exact cause of death."

A spokesperson for the Foreign Office added: "Our thoughts are with the family of a British woman who has died in the Bahamas.

"We are in contact with the local authorities and providing support to her family."

World.title: Student movement takes Serbia's Vučić to the wire in neck-and-neck election
World.content:
Ilija SrdanoviÄ may head the list of candidates â but he is not the movement's leader and would not necessarily be first choice prime minister if they won.

SrdanoviÄ insists that the Student List has a clear vision: "We offer to our citizens the core values of civilised society, which this previous regime has taken away from our citizens for the last time."

The other candidates on the Student List range from academics to athletes â and economists to engineers. None of them has a political background. But the students who selected them believe that is a strength, rather than a weakness.

"We've gathered people who are actually the best in their fields, and we really think that they are competent enough to rule the country," says Aleksandra, a student at Novi Sad University who only wants to give her first name.

"All of them are gathered around the same vision of a country where the freedom of speech is ruling, where you can walk to your home in the middle of the night and you will not be beaten up by some hooligans," she adds.

The Student List and its supporters say that Aleksandar VuÄiÄ and the SNS dominate state institutions and media coverage.

At the last parliamentary election in 2023, the International Election Observation Mission noted "overwhelming ruling party advantage" due to "bias in the media" and "misuse of public office and resources".

The BBC approached leading figures in the SNS for an interview but was not offered a response.

World.title: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
World.content:
Kenya has recorded its second death from Ebola as it handles its first ever outbreak of the disease.

A woman, aged 65, who was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo, died after being placed in quarantine, the health ministry said.

Seven other Ebola patients were receiving treatment at two isolation facilities, it added.

All the cases were within "one cluster, with no evidence of community spread", the ministry said.

More than 4,000 people have died in Africa since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease.

Kenya's latest victim had been under quarantine when she developed symptoms on 13 October, the health ministry said.

The first death, on 5 October, was that of a man who fell ill in September and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo before arriving in the Kenyan capital, Nairobi, where he died a few days later.

Those still being treated are three other relatives of the first victim, three health workers and a hospital cleaner.

World.title: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis
World.content:
Vanessa Trump, the former wife of Donald Trump Jr, has announced that she is cancer-free following her breast cancer diagnosis earlier this year.

Trump, 48, who has five children with President Donald Trump's eldest son, shared in a short video on her 19-year-old daughter Kai's Instagram account that her recent tests results "came back clear, so I'm finally cancer-free".

The video, posted on Friday, teases the release of a longer YouTube video to come on Saturday, in which Vanessa and Kai Trump will discuss breast cancer awareness and prevention, Kai wrote in the caption.

Vanessa Trump separated from Trump Jr in 2018 and announced last year that she had begun dating US pro golfer Tiger Woods.

"October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a time to raise awareness about early detection, education, and support for those affected by breast cancer," Kai Trump wrote on Instagram.

"I sat down with my mom and Dr. Nicole Saphier to talk about my mom's journey with breast cancer and learn more about prevention and early detection," she continued.

Kai's post received over 20,000 likes and hundreds of comments from people offering support and well wishes, including from American singer and media personality Mary Millben.

In Friday's video, Trump said she was first diagnosed with breast cancer in April. She publicly announced the diagnosis in May, saying in a social media post that she had undergone surgery and was working on a treatment plan with her medical team.

According to the American Cancer Society, the average risk of a woman in the US developing breast cancer is about 1 in 8, or 13%. The disease also accounts for 30% of all new female cancers every year, according to the group.

Surgery cures most breast cancers, but if some disease remains, chemotherapy, radiotherapy and endocrine therapy can reduce the long-term risk.

Treatments have been advancing, including more targeted therapies for early breast cancer, new types of hormonal therapies, and more precise and effective radiotherapy.

World.title: Three released without charge after fatal arson attack in Ireland
World.content:
Three people, who were arrested in connection with a suspected arson attack which killed four family members in the Republic of Ireland, have been released, gardaÃ­ (Irish police) have said.

Philip and Kim English and two of their children - nine-year-old Jayden and 12-year-old Callum - died after their home in Birch Avenue, on the outskirts of Waterford was set on fire earlier this month.

A man aged in his 20s and a woman in her 30s were previously charged in connection with the attack.

On Saturday, gardaÃ­ said three people - two women in their 30s and a man in his 50s - who were arrested on Tuesday have been released without charge.

A fourth person, a man in his 20s who was arrested on Thursday, remains in custody.

World.title: Jigawa sign $10 million deal with Indian firm to build modern hatchery
World.content:
As part of its agricultural transformation efforts, the Jigawa State Government has signed a $10 million Joint Venture Agreement with India’s Srinivasa Farms Private Limited for the establishment of a modern hatchery in the state.

The agreement provides for Srinivasa Farms to hold 60 percent equity in the venture, while the Jigawa State Government will own the remaining 40 percent, as the proposed facility is expected to be the first modern hatchery of its kind in Northern Nigeria.

Governor Malam Umar Namadi, who presided over the signing ceremony, described the partnership as an important stage in the state’s agricultural transformation efforts and expressed confidence that it would create new opportunities for poultry farmers.

“I am confident that this project will revolutionize the poultry industry, not only in Jigawa State and Northern Nigeria, but across the country. It is also part of our efforts to support the federal government’s agenda on food security,” the governor said.

He stated that the partnership followed engagements with Srinivasa Farms, including a visit to its facilities in India, where the state delegation observed its poultry operations and programmes for supporting smallholder farmers.

“The way the company empowers smallholder farmers, helping them to grow and establish sustainable businesses, greatly impressed us. We believe that Jigawa State has many poultry farmers who have struggled year after year, facing several challenges and making losses.

“With this joint venture, I believe the poultry industry will thrive in Jigawa State, Insha Allah.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The signed agreement contains provisions for training, technical guidance, and other forms of support to help smallholder poultry farmers improve their production and business operations.

The governor said the hatchery agreement was one of five partnerships being pursued following his visit to India as part of the state government’s effort to attract investment, strengthen agricultural value chains, and create opportunities for young people.

Making his remarks, the Srinivasa Farms’ Vice President, Mr. Senthil Kumar Krishnan, said the joint venture would focus on empowering rural communities and improving poultry production efficiency through technical services and quality products.

He said that farmers in Jigawa currently depend on supplies of day-old chicks from distant locations, including Kaduna, with long transportation periods sometimes affecting the quality of the birds upon arrival.

“By producing the chicks locally, we will be able to address these challenges. We will work with the government to provide the best possible support to farmers so that they can obtain quality chicks when they need them.

“Beyond supplying the chicks, we will also extend technical support to farmers, guiding them on how to raise the birds and achieve better results. Better production performance will translate into improved profitability for farmers. That is our main target.”

Furthermore, the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Professor Salim Abdurrahman Lawal, said the investment would address some of the most persistent constraints facing poultry farmers, particularly the high cost and unreliable supply of day-old chicks.

He explained that many chicks supplied to farmers in the northern region are transported from production centers in southern Nigeria, covering distances estimated at between 1,200 and 1,500 kilometers.

“This long journey affects their condition and slows their response to feeding,” he said.

With the proposed hatchery in Jigawa, he said transportation distances within the state would be significantly reduced, with no location expected to be more than approximately 150 kilometers from the facility.

“We have also made plans to establish delivery facilities and involve young people in the distribution of these day-old chicks. The state government has further indicated its commitment to providing a support scheme that will offer relief to farmers in the course of production.”

The agreement was signed on behalf of the Jigawa State Government by the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Professor Salim Abdurrahman Lawal, while Mr. Senthil Kumar Krishnan signed for Srinivasa Farms Private Limited

World.title: Kaduna govt debunks alleged N2.3trn APC campaign funding letter
World.content:
The Kaduna State Government has dismissed as a deliberate fabrication a letter circulating on social media alleging that Governor Uba Sani approved and released N2.3 trillion for the flag-off of the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 presidential campaign in Kaduna, describing the document as fraudulent, misleading and a calculated attempt to undermine the Governor’s reputation for fiscal prudence and responsible governance.

In a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Ahmed Maiyaki, the government described the purported letter, dated 18 October 2026, and titled “Notification for Preparations for the Grand Rally Flag Off,” as a figment of the imagination of its authors, riddled with inconsistencies that raise serious questions about its authenticity.

The letter, purportedly addressed by Governor Uba Sani to Senator Abdulazeez Yari, identified as Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, falsely claims that the Governor budgeted and released N2.3 trillion for the presidential campaign flag-off scheduled for Saturday, 24 October 2026.

Maiyaki pointed out that the entire 2026 Kaduna State budget stands at N985.92 billion, making the alleged N2.3 trillion expenditure more than twice the state’s annual budget. He described the claim as financially implausible and unsupported by any authentic appropriation, approval or expenditure records.

He further identified glaring irregularities in the purported correspondence, including the misspelling of the Governor’s surname as “Uba Sai” and discrepancies in its presentation, which cast further doubt on the document’s credibility. The government also raised serious concerns over the apparent reproduction of the Governor’s signature without authorisation.

“The Kaduna State Government categorically disowns this document. Governor Uba Sani neither authored nor authorised the purported letter, and no N2.3 trillion was budgeted, approved or released for the presidential campaign flag-off. The allegation is entirely fictitious and represents a deliberate attempt to mislead the public,” Maiyaki stated.

The Commissioner emphasised that since assuming office on 29 May 2023, Governor Uba Sani has demonstrated a consistent commitment to fiscal discipline, transparency, accountability and the judicious management of public resources, prioritising investments in security, infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and social protection.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He noted that the administration’s financial management philosophy is reflected in its extensive infrastructure programme, increased agricultural investment, rehabilitation of public institutions, settlement of inherited pension liabilities and expansion of social protection interventions aimed at improving the welfare of Kaduna citizens.

Maiyaki expressed concern over what he described as an emerging pattern of coordinated misinformation intended to discredit the Governor and his administration ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that the deliberate fabrication of official correspondence is criminal and punishable.

“Political competition must be conducted within the bounds of truth, decency and the law. The fabrication of government correspondence and circulation of false financial claims cannot be justified as legitimate political criticism. Those seeking to hold government accountable must do so through credible evidence, not manufactured documents,” he stressed.

The Commissioner disclosed that steps were being taken to establish the origin of the purported letter and called on relevant security and investigative agencies to examine the document, take steps to bring to justice for offences involving forgery or impersonation, and take appropriate action against anyone found culpable in accordance with the law.

He urged members of the public and media organisations to exercise caution in circulating unverified documents, emphasising that allegations concerning public expenditure should be subjected to proper scrutiny and verification before publication.

Maiyaki reaffirmed that Governor Uba Sani remains focused on consolidating peace, strengthening public institutions, accelerating infrastructure development and improving citizens’ welfare, stressing that the administration would not be distracted from its commitment to prudent financial management, transparent governance and sustainable development.

World.title: 10 killed in Taraba attack as residents flee community
World.content:
The police in Taraba State have confirmed that 10 people were killed when gunmen attacked Binnari community in Karim-Lamido Local Government Area, while local sources reported that houses were burnt and food supplies destroyed.

The attack occurred in the early hours of Friday in Amar Ward, Karim II Constituency, according to local sources.

The police spokesperson in the state, Victor Mshelizah, confirmed the killings, saying security personnel had been deployed to the affected community.

“There was an incident that happened yesterday, an attack by unknown gunmen that claimed the lives of ten people. We currently have men deployed there,” Mr Mshelizah said.

The police did not provide further details about the circumstances surrounding the attack or identify the perpetrators.

However, local sources said the assailants, suspected to have crossed into the area from neighbouring Plateau State, stormed the community unexpectedly, killing residents and setting houses ablaze.

The sources also said the attackers destroyed foodstuffs reportedly worth millions of naira, leaving residents to count their losses.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

READ ALSO: Taraba community seeks separate ward over alleged marginalisation

According to the local sources, the attack forced several residents to flee their homes and seek refuge in neighbouring communities. Some people were also reportedly missing after the incident.

The sources further alleged that residents made distress calls during the attack but that security assistance arrived too late to prevent the killings and destruction.

The incident has heightened concerns over insecurity in Karim-Lamido, with residents calling on the Taraba State Government and security agencies to strengthen security and prevent further attacks.

The police have yet to publicly provide further details about the attack, including the reported destruction of property and missing persons.

World.title: Tinubu 2027: RELAX DG Ahmed Bala storms Kaduna for presidential campaign flag-off, rallies support for Tinubu’s re-election
World.content:
The Director General of RELAX, Tinubu Is Fixing Nigeria, Hon Ahmed Bala, has arrived in Kaduna State ahead of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s 2027 presidential campaign flag-off, expressing confidence in the administration’s economic reforms and infrastructure development programmes.

RELAX, Tinubu Is Fixing Nigeria, is described by its leadership as a sister organisation to the City Boy Movement, with both organisations founded by Seyi Tinubu, son of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. The organisations are involved in political mobilisation, public engagement and advocacy for the President’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

Bala, who has remained at the forefront of political advocacy for the administration, said the Kaduna gathering provides an opportunity to highlight the government’s achievements and strengthen public engagement ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He identified the ongoing reconstruction of the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano highway as one of the major infrastructure projects receiving attention under the Tinubu administration.

The highway, which connects the Federal Capital Territory with major commercial centres in Northern Nigeria, remains critical to the movement of goods, agricultural produce and passengers.

Other federal infrastructure projects include the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, the Sokoto-Zamfara-Zaria road corridor, the Kano-Maiduguri highway and road rehabilitation projects across several northern states.

Bala maintained that improved transportation infrastructure would strengthen commerce, reduce logistics challenges and open new economic opportunities for communities across the region.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The RELAX Nigeria DG also highlighted the administration’s educational interventions through the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, agricultural support programmes and the Presidential Compressed Natural Gas Initiative.

He said the Federal Government’s efforts to improve healthcare delivery, increase public revenue and expand infrastructure investment should be considered alongside the economic challenges facing the country.

While acknowledging the difficulties experienced by Nigerians following major economic reforms, Bala expressed optimism that sustained implementation of the administration’s policies could produce long-term benefits.

He further emphasised the importance of grassroots political engagement, describing RELAX Nigeria and the City Boy Movement as platforms through which supporters can communicate the administration’s programmes and priorities.

Bala expressed support for President Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that continuity would provide an opportunity to consolidate ongoing reforms and complete major development projects.

He called for peaceful political participation and urged Nigerians to assess the administration’s performance as the country prepares for the 2027 presidential election.

World.title: INEC risks prosecution for failing to publish voters’ register online – Yiaga Africa
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) risks criminal liability for failing to publish the national voters’ register online as required by the Electoral Act 2022, Samson Itodo, executive director of Yiaga Africa, has said.

Mr Itodo said the commission was bound by Section 19 of the Act to make the register available online for public scrutiny, warning that its failure to do so ahead of the Anambra State governorship election raised questions about compliance with the law.

He spoke on Friday on Channels Television’s Politics Today programme while discussing the absence of the register from INEC’s website less than three weeks before the election.

PREMIUM TIMES had reported that INEC failed to publish the preliminary voters’ register on its website by the 90-day deadline before the 2027 general election, despite a legal requirement for the register to be made available online for public scrutiny.

Mr Itodo said the wording of Section 19 left no room for the commission to decide whether or not to publish the register online.

“The law is very clear. When you say that the commission shall, it means you must,” he said.

He noted that INEC, under its former chairman, Mahmood Yakubu, had published the register online during the previous electoral cycle, making it accessible to Nigerians.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Itodo said the commission’s obligation to publish the register online is separate from displaying copies at polling units, which INEC said it had already done.

“If INEC has not done that and we are just less than three months to the election, it means that it hasn’t complied with that particular section of the law,” he said.

INEC officials face possible penalties

Mr Itodo said Section 19 provides penalties for officials who fail to comply with the requirements for displaying the voters’ register.

He said an INEC official or staff member convicted of failing to display the register as prescribed by law could face a fine of N100,000, a six-month prison term, or both.

He urged INEC to explain publicly why it had not made the register available online, saying its silence could undermine public confidence in the electoral process.

“I think INEC owes it to the Nigerian people, to Nigerian voters and stakeholders to really officially make a statement as to why it has been unable to implement this part of the law. But this silence does not inspire confidence,” he said.

Mr Itodo said the alleged breach could attract criminal proceedings, adding that while prosecution would ordinarily fall to the state, interested stakeholders could approach the courts to compel the commission to comply with the law.

Display of register differs from distribution to parties

The Yiaga Africa director also sought to distinguish the statutory requirement to display the register for claims and objections from INEC’s separate obligation to provide copies to political parties before an election.

He explained that the display process allows registered voters to inspect their details and report errors for correction.

For instance, a voter whose gender was wrongly recorded could request a correction, while relatives could notify the commission that a deceased person remained on the register.

Mr Itodo said this process was different from distributing the register to political parties, which traditionally receive copies 30 days before an election.

He described the voters’ register as a foundation of the electoral process, arguing that its accessibility was essential to public scrutiny and confidence in elections.

Citizens can publish polling unit results

Mr Itodo also defended the right of citizens, journalists and civil society organisations to publish and aggregate election results already announced publicly at polling units, distinguishing that activity from INEC’s exclusive authority to declare winners and return elected candidates.

He explained that results are announced first at polling units before moving through ward, local government and state collation levels, with the national level completing the process where applicable.

After ballots are counted at a polling unit, the presiding officer records the results on the prescribed result sheet and is required to display them publicly, he said.

Once displayed, the results are in the public domain and can be shared by citizens on social media, according to Mr Itodo.

“Under the law, can any Nigerian take the result and post it on their Twitter page or social? Absolutely, because it’s already public,” he said.

He said INEC’s Result Viewing Portal (IReV) was introduced to strengthen transparency by allowing citizens to compare polling unit results uploaded to the platform with figures presented at subsequent collation stages.

That process, he explained, can help expose discrepancies if results are altered during collation.

Aggregating results is not declaring a winner

Mr Itodo said the law distinguishes between announcing results, declaring a winner and returning an elected candidate.

He argued that media organisations and civil society groups do not violate the law by compiling figures from results already announced publicly, provided they do not purport to exercise INEC’s statutory power to declare and return winners.

“What media, civil society can do is they can take results that are already in the public domain, that have been announced by INEC, and aggregate those results. They have not violated the law,” he said.

He said the power to declare a candidate elected and return that candidate rests with INEC, and that publishing or aggregating publicly announced polling unit results does not amount to exercising that power.

Mr Itodo added that independent aggregation could help protect the integrity of the process by making it harder for political actors to pressure election officials to alter results.

He said citizens remained free to share polling unit results they observed, while the formal declaration and return of winners remained the commission’s responsibility.

World.title: New reality show to spotlight affordable African interior design, showcase young talent
World.content:
Retouched By Flair, an interior design organisation, has unveiled a reality television show to promote African interior design, empower young creatives, and show how homes can be transformed without excessive spending.

The 13-week programme, titled The Retoucher, will premiere in the first quarter of 2027 and feature emerging interior designers competing in design challenges as they transform homes and other spaces.

Creator and Executive Producer Debola Majekodunmi said the initiative was designed to make interior design more accessible while giving young African designers a platform to showcase their creativity and gain visibility.

Speaking at the unveiling in Lagos, Majekodunmi said the project would help promote African design identity, indigenous materials and local creativity, adding that good interior design should not be limited to wealthy people.

“I want every home to be decently dressed up. I want to promote that it is not only the wealthy that can have a good interior design,” she said.

Majekodunmi noted that while African culture had gained recognition through food, music, and fashion, interior design still had significant growth potential and needed wider appreciation.

“We want to promote African interior design. We have beauty in Africa. Africa has been promoted through the food, music, and clothing industries. We want to have our own African interior design. So this is the beginning of it,” she said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She added that the initiative was expected to expand beyond Nigeria into other African regions, including East, North and Southern Africa, with the long-term ambition of building a franchise.

How The Retoucher will work

Majekodunmi said the production would begin with auditions across four locations in Nigeria, including Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt, with a fourth location still under consideration.

According to her, about 100 aspiring designers are expected to emerge from the auditions before proceeding to a boot camp for training, mentoring and further assessment.

The process will eventually produce 20 shortlisted contestants who will participate in the 13-week programme.

The organisers also plan to invite homeowners from different backgrounds to submit their homes for transformation. The selection is expected to include people from different economic circumstances and life experiences, giving contestants opportunities to address practical design needs.

Majekodunmi said the show would combine education, creativity and empowerment, with the contestants expected to apply their skills to real-life spaces.

“We are transforming homes and empowering lives. That is it. We have come to empower homes, we have come to transform lives,” she said.

She added that the organisers were pleased with the reception at the unveiling and hoped the programme would grow into a wider movement for African interior design.

Design challenges and home transformations

Veteran Nollywood filmmaker and producer of the show, Tade Ogidan, said The Retoucher would combine competition, audience participation and practical design challenges.

Ogidan explained that contestants would work on different types of spaces, including interiors and exteriors, showing how creative ideas can improve people’s living environments.

He also disclosed that the programme would feature transformations of homes belonging to people who might not ordinarily afford professional interior design services.

“We have part of the concept where we will take people in poor homes. They would all pitch in to say, ‘Come and do up our home, come and do up our home.’

“We will look at it, and then we will go and give them the surprise of their lives, do up the place to become somewhere they would love,” he said.

Ogidan added that viewers would play an active role in the programme, making audience participation an important part of the competition.

At the unveiling, contestants divided into Team Blue and Team Orange were given 25 minutes to transform blank sets using available materials.

Team Orange emerged as the winner after the judges’ assessment and audience voting, which accounted for 40 per cent and 60 per cent of the final scores, respectively.

Team Blue received 16 points from the audience, while Team Orange scored 19 points. The judges’ scores also favoured Team Orange.

The winning team received N200,000, while the runners-up were awarded N50,000.

Stakeholders call for affordable, inclusive design

Strategy Adviser at Retouched By Flair, Hubert Davies, said homeowners could create attractive living spaces without spending too much.

“It doesn’t cost a fortune for you to change your home into your palace,” he said.

Similarly, Jennifer Chukwujekwe, founder of Jenniez School of African Interior Design and former President of the Interior Designers Association of Nigeria, highlighted the sector’s opportunities.

Chukwujekwe also called for greater attention to older people’s needs in interior design, stressing the importance of creating spaces that accommodate their specific requirements.

GDM Group Chief Executive Officer Victor Afolabi said the initiative offered opportunities to improve homes affordably and encouraged partnerships to support the programme and expand its reach.

The Retoucher Project Manager, Jemimah Ododo, said the project would promote designs that reflect African culture and identity while creating opportunities for local talent.

NFVCB added that this would help the Nollywood industry accommodate local, affordable filmmaking budgets beyond Western appeal.

She added that the initiative would demonstrate how indigenous resources and African creativity could produce world-class designs while supporting emerging professionals.

Beyond the television programme, the organisers said they planned to explore training, design exhibitions, partnerships and product development to create further opportunities for young creatives.

They called on brands, broadcasters, building-material manufacturers, retailers, property developers, and investors to support the project through partnerships and sponsorships, aiming to expand its reach and promote African interior design.

World.title: Ebola: Lagos is prepared to respond — Commissioner
World.content:
The Lagos State government says it has stepped up preparedness measures and is prepared to respond following Nigeria’s confirmation of an imported case of Ebola disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

The state’s Commissioner for Health, Akin Abayomi, said Lagos remains on “high alert and preparedness” and is treating the situation as a priority.

“Lagos is a gateway city with constant movement to and from Abuja, and we are treating this as a priority,” Mr Abayomi said in a statement posted on X on Friday.

He said the state’s Emergency Operations Centre (EOC) had been working ahead of the confirmation, with measures being put in place across surveillance, isolation, laboratory testing, infection prevention and control.

‘Lagos is prepared’

Mr Abayomi said response teams are conducting simulation exercises to ensure that responders understand their roles before they are needed.

He said the state’s isolation centre has also been upgraded, while additional capacity is being developed.

He noted that training on infection prevention and control is continuing for health workers across public and private health facilities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The commissioner said Lagos is also establishing a clear laboratory testing pathway, aiming to obtain results within 24 hours.

He noted that screening at airports and other points of entry is being strengthened in collaboration with federal authorities, while disease surveillance is being digitally enhanced on the state’s digital health surveillance platform to support real-time detection, tracing and response.

A “dedicated Ebola Research Committee” is also reviewing the latest evidence on treatment and vaccines to guide the state’s decisions.

Advice to residents

The commissioner urged residents to wash their hands regularly with soap and water and avoid contact with the blood or body fluids of anyone who is ill.

He advised anyone who develops fever, weakness, vomiting, diarrhoea or unexplained bleeding, or believes they may have been exposed, not to self-medicate.

“If you develop fever, weakness, vomiting, diarrhoea or unexplained bleeding, or think you have been exposed, do not self-medicate. Call before visiting a health facility,” he said.

Mr Abayomi also urged health workers to maintain a high index of suspicion, ask about patients’ travel history and use appropriate personal protective equipment.

Residents can report suspected cases or possible exposure through “the Lagos emergency numbers, 112 or 767, or the Directorate of Epidemiology, Biosecurity and Global Health on 0802 316 9485.”

The commissioner urged residents to remain calm, stay alert and rely on official information from the Lagos State Ministry of Health.

Lagos’ 2014 experience

The government’s preparedness comes against the backdrop of Lagos’ experience during Nigeria’s 2014 Ebola outbreak.

Patrick Sawyer, a Liberian diplomat infected with Ebola, arrived in Lagos on 20 July 2014. He was admitted to a private hospital in the city, where the disease was subsequently confirmed.

Nigeria recorded 20 Ebola cases during the outbreak, including eight deaths, before the country was declared free of Ebola transmission on 20 October 2014 after 42 days without a new case.

READ ALSO: Kenya records second Ebola death

Nationwide response

The federal government continues to urge states to strengthen their response systems.

The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, said 21 states have updated their Ebola response plans, while the remaining 15 states are being urged to expedite their preparedness and response mechanisms.

The government has also called on healthcare facilities nationwide to strengthen infection prevention and control, promptly identify and isolate suspected cases and report them to public health authorities.

Nigeria currently has one confirmed imported Ebola case, while 44 contacts of the patient are being monitored.

World.title: Police arrest man who murdered ex-girlfriend, hid body in sack
World.content:
The police in Anambra State have arrested a man, Chima Ofoeke, who allegedly murdered his former girlfriend, Mmesoma Umeorini, in Uga, a community in Aguata Local Government Area of the state.

The police spokesperson in Anambra State, Tochukwu Ikenga, disclosed this in a statement on Saturday.

Mr Ikenga, a superintendent of police, said the arrest followed a report by the victim’s mother to the Divisional Police Officer in Umuchu Division that her daughter had been missing since 16 October.

“Acting on intelligence-led information, police operatives, in collaboration with members of the Agunechemba security outfit in Uga, arrested the suspect, who was identified as the deceased’s alleged former boyfriend,” he said.

The spokesperson said the suspect, from Ebonyi State, confessed during preliminary investigation that he murdered the victim because she broke up with him.

He said the suspect subsequently led police detectives to the location where the remains of the deceased were recovered.

Mr Ikenga said the Commissioner of Police in Anambra, Nnanna Ama, has ordered that the case be transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department Awka, for “a comprehensive and diligent investigation.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Ama, according to the statement, reiterated the commitment of the police in the state to protect lives and property and urged members of the public to promptly report cases of missing persons and other suspicious activities to the appropriate authorities.

“Further developments will be communicated as the investigation progresses,” he assured.

Viral video clip

A video clip obtained by PREMIUM TIMES showed when security operatives arrested the suspect and interrogated him.

In the clip, the suspect was holding a dirty sack which he confessed contained the body of his former girlfriend.

He also confessed that he murdered the victim on a Friday because she ended their romantic relationship

Asked how he murdered the victim, he responded in Igbo language: “I held her neck with her clothes and strangled her until she collapsed.”

Some voices in the background of the clip suggested that the victim’s body must have been cut into pieces to enter the sack.

Prohibited in Nigeria

Murder is outlawed in Section 315 (6) of the Nigeria Criminal Code Act.

Offenders, on conviction, face death sentence, section 319 (1) said.

Several persons have been sentenced to death for murder across the country.

An Aiyetoro High Court in Ogun State, for instance, sentenced a man, Adelake Bara, to death by hanging in June 2022, for shooting and killing one Olaleye Oke.

A high court in Lokoja, Kogi State, in January 2022, also sentenced a man, Muritala Dare to death by hanging for stabbing his colleague to death with a broken bottle.

World.title: Tinubu, Shettima flag off APC 2027 campaign in Kaduna
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu arrived in Kaduna State on Saturday ahead of the flag-off of the All Progressives Congress’ 2027 presidential campaign, with Vice President Kashim Shettima and his wife, Nana, also arriving for the event.

APC National Chairman, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda, the Director-General of the presidential campaign, Abdul’aziz Yari, and Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani were at the airport to welcome the President.

Shettima’s arrival was announced in a statement by his spokesman, Stanley Nkwocha.

Mr Nkwocha said APC governors, party leaders, elected officials, political stakeholders and supporters were gathering at the Kaduna Township Stadium for the commencement of the party’s nationwide presidential campaign.

He described the event as a significant moment for Kaduna, noting that the city would serve as the launching point for the APC’s campaign ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

According to the statement, the campaign would provide the ruling party with an opportunity to present its “Renewed Hope 2.0” agenda and highlight the achievements of the Tinubu administration.

“The stage is set. Kaduna is ready. The 2027 campaign begins!” the statement read in part.

It added, “Asiwaju is here. Northwest for the takeaway!”

Ahead of the President’s arrival, security operatives on Saturday barricaded strategic locations across Kaduna metropolis as authorities stepped up security preparations for the campaign event.

Personnel from the Nigerian Army, Department of State Services, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Nigeria Immigration Service and the Kaduna State Vigilance Service were deployed to different parts of the city.

The security personnel were stationed at major roundabouts and along roads leading to the venue of the campaign flag-off.

Muhammadu Buhari Way, formerly known as WAFF Road, was blocked by security operatives ahead of the expected movement of the President and his entourage through the route.

The Ahmadu Bello Stadium roundabout was also manned by heavily armed soldiers, police officers and plain-clothes security personnel.

The security restrictions affected traffic in several parts of Kaduna, triggering a gridlock that extended from Junction Road to Ahmadu Bello Way.

World.title: French Montana, Jorja Smith to perform at Ballon d’Or 2026
World.content:
Ballon d’Or organisers revealed on Saturday that star US rapper French Montana and English singer Jorja Smith would perform at this year’s ceremony, part of efforts to draw more viewers to the awards event.

Last year saw Canadian singer Charlotte Cardin do her best to lift the somewhat stiff atmosphere at the prize giving in Paris as she performed her hit “Feel Good” in front of a motionless crowd of suited footballers and VIPs at a theatre.

The most prestigious individual award in football will be handed out in London next Monday, with Kylian Mbappe, Spanish pair Lamine Yamal and Ferran Torres, PSG duo Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Harry Kane all seen as frontrunners.

It is the first time the Ballon d’Or ceremony, now in its 70th edition, will be hosted in Britain.

French Montana has over 30 million monthly listeners on Spotify, mixing Moroccan influences, trap, afrobeat and New York hip hop culture.

He has collaborated on hits with Drake, Cardi B and Swae Lee, with whom he made the 2017 track “Unforgettable”, which has racked up 1.9 billion views on YouTube.

English singer-songwriter Jorja Smith mixes RnB, soul and jazz influences, drawing on her Jamaican heritage and her classical music training.

Her career took off 10 years ago with “Blue Lights”, followed by other tracks ranging from intimate to more danceable.

In addition to their “exclusive performances” during the evening, “other surprises are planned”, the Groupe L’Equipe, which organises the ceremony, said in a statement sent to AFP.

The group owns the magazine France Football, which has been awarding the Ballon d’Or since 1956.

It is based on voting by a jury of journalists from the top 100 countries in the FIFA rankings.

In 2025, the top male player prize was awarded to France’s Ousmane Dembele and the women’s to Spain’s Aitana Bonmati.

The ceremony will be broadcast on sports streaming website DAZN, and the L’Equipe TV channel in France.

It will be hosted by former France and Arsenal striker Thierry Henry, and sports journalist Kate Scott.

In 2022, tenor Andrea Bocelli was chosen to open the ceremony.

After last year’s event, Quebec-born Cardin revealed that she had felt uneasy, explaining that she had been through a “moment of great solitude” when she performed alone with limited lighting and stage effects.
