World.title: NDC fixes October 26 for 3rd NEC meeting, campaign council unveiling
World.content:
…Says 80 per cent of its candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms

By Henry Umoru

The national leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has fixed Monday, October 26, for its third National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting, where it will unveil its National Campaign Council and present its candidates with Certificates of Return.

The party has attributed its limited financial resources partly to the economic hardship in the country, just as it claimed that about 80 per cent of its candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms.

According to the NDC, it had to issue the forms to the affected candidates free of charge, contrary to what he described as public speculation about its finances.

In a statement signed on Saturday by NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, he disclosed that the meeting would also feature the presentation of the party’s statement of account by its National Treasurer.

According to him, it is part of the party’s commitment to transparency and accountability in the management of its finances, just as it challenged other political parties, particularly the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to adopt similar measures in disclosing their financial records, adding, “For the NDC, it is no longer politics as usual.”

The statement read, “The leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) wishes to announce that its 3rd National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting will hold on Monday, 26th October, 2026, at JD event centre, Kashim Ibrahim Way, opposite A-class park, Maitama, Abuja. Time is 10 am prompt.

“A major highlight of the meeting will be the release and presentation of the party’s Statement of Account by the National Treasurer. This is in deference to our avowed commitment to the principles of transparency and accountability. In this regard, we challenge other political parties, especially the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), to emulate this level of openness and transparency in the management of their finances.

“For the NDC, it is no longer politics as usual.

“Our finances would have been more robust. However, contrary to speculations in the public domain, and due to the level of poverty, hunger and deprivation in the country occasioned by the rudderless APC and its amorphous economic policies, about 80% of our candidates could not afford the Expression of Interest forms. The party had to issue forms to such candidates free of charge.

“The party will also use the opportunity of the NEC meeting to unveil its National Campaign Council (NCC).

“As a party of innovation, our NCC is all-encompassing. It covers the Presidential, National Assembly, Governorship, and State Houses of Assembly Campaign Councils.

“Our various candidates will be presented with Certificates of Return for their respective offices.

“The NDC is turbo-charged and ready to give Nigerians the altruistic leadership the nation deserves. A New Nigeria is Possible. We can do it!”

World.title: Man City beaten by Aston Villa to end perfect Premier League start
World.content:
Aston Villa’s Senegalese striker #11 Nicolas Jackson scores the team’s second goal during the English Premier League football match between Aston Villa and Manchester City at Villa Park in Birmingham, central England on October 24, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE. No use with unauthorized audio, video, data, fixture lists, club/league logos or ‘live’ services. Online in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No video emulation. Social media in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No use in betting publications, games or single club/league/player publications. /





Manchester City’s perfect Premier League start came to a crashing halt in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa as Nicolas Jackson’s double extended an upturn in form for Unai Emery’s new-look side.

Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City’s struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons.

After Jackson blasted home the opener after just six minutes, Villa relied on a brilliant goalkeeping display from Zion Suzuki to keep City at bay.

Erling Haaland breifly levelled early in the second half only for Villa to respond on the hour mark when Jackson drilled home Ibrahim Mbaye’s cross.

Four years on from Emery’s arrival, which has transformed the club from a sleeping giant into the Champions League, the Spaniard is working more magic despite seeing the spine of his squad in recent seasons decimated.

Six of the side that started Villa’s victory in last season’s Europa League left during the transfer window.

But the recruitment of the likes of Jackson, Suzuki, Mbaye and Johan Manzambi is already paying dividends after a slow start to the campaign.

Until now City have managed to shrug off the cloud hanging over the club’s Premier League future to keep winning on the field.

The 10-time English champions are appealing a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking financial rules between 2009 and 2018 that could lead to swingeing sanctions, including relegation.

There was little sign of that distraction affecting Enzo Maresca’s men, but they were made to pay for two sloppy defensive errors.

A heavy touch by Marc Guehi presented Jackson with possession for the opening goal as he cut inside Elliott Anderson and blasted high past Gianluigi Donnarumma.

City largely dominated the remainder of the first half, but could not find a way past Suzuki.

Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov were all denied before Ndiaye struck the post.

City’s pressure finally told on 52 minutes when Haaland powered in a header from Ndiaye’s cross for his 13th goal in 10 appearances this season.

Josko Gvardiol nearly completed the comeback when Suzuki turned his blistering drive into the crossbar moments later.

Instead, it was Villa to got the decisive third goal.

Mbaye was played in behind the City defence and from his cross, Jackson’s low effort should have been saved by Donnarumma.

The visitors pressed in vain for another equaliser to allow Arsenal the chance to move level on points at the top of the table when they host Everton later on Saturday.

A sixth win in seven games in all competitions for Villa lifts them up to sixth.

World.title: FG’s 90-day cost of living plan is vote-buying – YPP presidential candidate
World.content:
By John Alechenu

Abuja-The presidential candidate of the Young Progressives Party, YPP, Architect Peter Agada, has described the Federal Government’s 90-day action plan to ease cost of living as vote-buying that will not work.

Read Also: Alake’s attack on Atiku won’t cut food prices, ADC campaign fires back

The plan was recently approved by the National Economic Council, NEC, and announced by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Wale Edun.

Agada told Vanguard in Abuja on Saturday that the plan, like previous interventions by the APC-led administration, does not reflect economic reality and is destined to fail.

He said his #LabourDirect ward-to-ward development strategy remains the alternative, with capacity to empower Nigerians with N40 million monthly per ward.

“LabourDirect can capture all Nigerians within 60 days of implementation. We said 60 days; about 20 days are gone before the elections,” he said.

“If they approach me to implement it, Nigerians will have more confidence that they have called one of the candidates to help.”

Agada said government should call people who can fix the micro-economy before January 16, not just roll out macro-economic promises.

The YPP candidate proposed a dashboard powered by the Labour Direct Information Network, LIN System, to monitor projects, employment, production, tax and revenues from a single application.

He recalled that similar measures announced two weeks ago, including subsidy interventions, have shown no results.

Agada said, “I align with those who said the economic team has failed. I have listened to many analysts on TV and radio, none spoke positively about the team. They have lost their bearings.”

He cited past unfulfilled pledges from 2023, including N75 billion for manufacturing, N75 billion for micro SMEs, N50 billion conditional grants, grain distribution, N200 billion to cultivate 500 hectares, N50 billion each for rice farmers and N100 billion for CNG.

According to him, after those announcements, government removed tariffs on food imports, which did not crash food prices.

He said, “If you are fighting food inflation, return food prices to where they were before you took office.

“There are 85 days to the election and you are announcing a 90-day timeline. After election what happens? These guys are playing mind games.”

He urged Nigerians to demand month-by-month job creation data, saying without that, the 90-day plan is just campaign strategy ahead of 2027.

World.title: 2027: Atiku is North’s enemy, says Akume
World.content:
George Akume

….Says, power rotation agreed in Kaduna to keep Nigeria one

By Omeiza Ajayi, Kaduna

As the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) flagged off its presidential campaign on Saturday in Kaduna, Secretary to the Government of the Federation SGF, Senator George Akume, declared that any northerner seeking to contest the 2027 presidential election is an enemy of the region.

Former vice president Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress ADC is the only prominent northern politician seeking to wrestle power from incumbent President Bola Tinubu in the next year’s presidential contest.

This was as he reminded Northerners that the agreement on power rotation between the North and the South was reached in Kaduna State to keep the country together.

His spokesman, Yomi Odunuga, in a statement on Saturday, said the SGF spoke at a pre-campaign meeting with a large crowd of Benue State indigenes residing in Kaduna.

“Remember that it was in this same Kaduna State that we agreed on power rotation between the North and the South. You cannot doubt the credentials of those that reached this agreement at that time, and it was done to keep this country together. We agreed on power shift, and that is what has kept this country going. That is what has retained our territorial integrity,” Akume said.

On that basis, he declared that any Northerner seeking to contest the 2027 presidential election is an enemy of the North, insisting that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu remains the right candidate to lead Nigeria beyond 2027.

“Anybody who is from the North and running for the presidency is an enemy of the North. Don’t allow that pretender to deceive you. It is not yet our turn. The North’s turn is in 2031. Prepare to vote for Tinubu. Do not allow anyone to destroy the country because of a vaunting personal ambition,” he said.

The SGF urged the North to back Tinubu’s re-election bid and wait until 2031 before seeking to return to the presidency. He warned that individual political ambitions should not be allowed to undermine the region’s collective interests.

Akume, a former Governor of Benue State, urged Northerners to remain united and resist political manoeuvres capable of weakening the region’s influence. He cautioned against attempts to divide them along political, religious and personal lines, and recalled past political disagreements among Nigerian leaders, warning against repeating mistakes that could weaken the North in national politics.

He said the North stands to benefit more from supporting Tinubu’s second-term ambition than from allowing individual political interests to create divisions ahead of the next general elections.

Defending the president’s record, the SGF said Tinubu has been fair to all in appointments and does not favour one religion over another.

“Let us remember that the President has been fair to all in terms of appointments and others. He doesn’t favour one religion over the other. Just look at the figures. So be careful about what people tell you,” he said.

Akume also told his audience that the president has shown his love for Benue State through significant projects.

“Let nobody deceive you; Asiwaju loves Benue, and he has displayed that in the number of significant projects the Federal Government is carrying out simultaneously in the state. These projects are diverse in healthcare, roads, education and others. This is being replicated throughout the federation. For example, in the area of education, over 65 per cent of NELFUND has been accessed, and most of them are from the North,” he said.

Apparently taking a swipe at Atiku, he said, “Forget that other one making noise that he was going to remove fuel subsidy. He is always flip-flopping. He says something today and changes gear the next minute.”

The SGF praised Governor Uba Sani and called for his return to office.

“Kaduna State is a historic city that gave us meaning and purpose. So, this is your home too, as Benue State citizens living here. The present governor, Senator Uba Sani, believes in that vision of Saudauna. He is a great man. I want to appeal to you that there is none like Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu in 2027.

“I was the governor of Benue State, and the Fulanis were there. It is about leadership. If Asiwaju was not a good leader, I would not tell you otherwise. I will still come to Kaduna to speak with you. Your governor is a good man, and he has done well for this state. Let us return him to power too,” he said.

The SGF also stressed the need for national unity, peaceful coexistence and cooperation among Nigeria’s diverse ethnic and religious groups and encouraged the preservation of cultural identity and traditions as a means of promoting understanding among communities.

“I believe you are here because you believe in me and because you want to see your son, and that is me in flesh and blood,” he told the gathering.

Those who accompanied Akume included a former governor of Jigawa State, Alhaji Saminu Turaki; Dame Pauline Tallen; Senator Abu Ibrahim; the Minister of Water Resources, Prof. Joseph Utsev; and the Minister of Steel Development, Prince Shuaibu Abubakar Audu.

World.title: Troops neutralise 15 terrorists in Borno
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

The Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), has recorded another operational success with the neutralisation of 15 terrorists in a precision air strike north-west of Pulka in Gwoza LGA of Borno State.

Through these efforts, the Theatre Command continues to maintain pressure on terrorist elements, disrupt their activities and strengthen the security environment across the Northeast.

“Operation HADIN KAI remains resolute in its mission to defeat terrorism and insurgency, protect law-abiding citizens and create the conditions necessary for the restoration of normalcy and socio-economic activities in affected communities.

“The Theatre Command reassures the public that troops will sustain the momentum of ongoing operations with vigilance, determination and professionalism.

“The Theatre Command also calls on members of the public to sustain their cooperation with security agencies by providing timely and credible information on suspicious movements and activities. The continued partnership between the military and the civilian population remains essential to consolidating operational gains and achieving lasting peace and security across the Northeast.” Goni explained. World.title: France protests: Latest developments
World.content:
A protester holds a slogan reading “Tax the rich” during a demonstration in favor of purchasing power, the protection of public services, and fiscal and social justice, in Paris on October 24, 2026 as part of a nationwide call for mobilisation bringing together former members of the Yellow Vest movement, labor unions, high school and university students. Protests by high school students over learning conditions sparked a movement that has since spread nationwide, fuelled by broader anger over the rising cost of living. About 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on October 24, 2026, Interior Minister said at a news conference, warning that calls for violence and looting were circulating on social media. (Photo by Aris MESSINIS / AFP)

Hundreds of protests were held in France Saturday as nationwide anger grows over the cost of living, with security forces massing to prevent a repeat of violence that marred demonstrations last week.

Here are the latest developments:

– ‘Calm’ in Paris –

French police had arrested 135 people nationwide and seized a variety of weapons, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said, adding that, so far, “there has been no major incident”.

Weapons confiscated included metal balls, lead pellets, fireworks, slingshots, steel balls, improvised weapons, a katana and airsoft weapons, he said.

Paris police described the situation as “calm” at midday.

– ‘Scandalous’ –

Hundreds of demonstrators could be seen gathering at Porte d’Italie in Paris, where authorities have said they must begin the only authorised march.

Union representative Murielle Guilbert told reporters it was “scandalous” that President Emmanuel Macron had forbidden protesters from demonstrating “where we wish to demonstrate”.

“We are here today, quite obviously, because there is immense social anger in this country, and because wages have still not been increased to the level they should be,” she added.

Paris police at the last minute ordered the union-organised march be moved from Bastille, in the centre, to the more remote Porte d’Italie on the southeastern rim.

Unions said they reluctantly agreed. But the Yellow Vests — a loosely organised group that staged disruptive street protests against Macron eight years ago — indicated they would not comply.

– Halloween protests called –

One group organising Saturday’s demonstrations — the Yellow Vests — said they would hold another round of protests on October 31.

Organisers called for rallies and a sit-in outside parliament and city halls nationwide, condemning the “authoritarian drift” of President Emmanuel Macron’s government and urging citizens to stand up for “public freedoms”.

– Tear gas in Lyon –

Police fired teargas to disperse some 150 people protesting in the southeastern city of Lyon, in an area banned to all demonstrations, an AFP journalist saw.

Police fired several teargas grenades to clear the group near a university faculty and the city’s police station as part of nationwide rallies against the cost of living. Police moved in as demonstrators tried to block a road.

– ‘Macron resign’ –

Thousands of people yelling anti-fascist slogans marched in the city of Orleans against a congress by far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) party there, AFP journalists saw.

The protest criticised both leading presidential candidate Le Pen and centrist Macron. “Macron resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd yelled.

– Louvre, Orsay closed –

The Louvre, d’Orsay, and Picasso museums, as well as the Grand Palais in Paris, were closed Saturday. The culture ministry had called on institutions to take every measure to ensure the safety of visitors and staff, and the protection of artworks.

World.title: 2027: Plateau Community in Kaduna Pledges Massive Support for Mutfwang
World.content:
The Plateau Community in Kaduna State has pledged massive support for Governor Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang’s re-election in 2027, citing his administration’s development initiatives and commitment to improving the lives of residents.



The pledge was made during an appreciation visit by Mutfwang, his deputy, Ngo Josephine Piyo, and other top government officials to Plateau indigenes residing in Kaduna. The visit coincided with activities surrounding the flag-off of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in the state.

Addressing the gathering, Mutfwang thanked community members for their sacrifices and support during the 2023 governorship election, particularly those who travelled from Kaduna to Plateau to vote for him.



He assured them that his administration would sustain its development agenda, strengthen institutions and improve the quality of life across the state.



“I am here to express my profound appreciation for the support you gave me during the 2023 election that brought me into office. Your sacrifices, your conviction and your unwavering belief in our vision for Plateau State will never be taken for granted,” he said.



The governor urged Plateau indigenes to remain united and committed to the state’s progress. He also called on them to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, arguing that continued cooperation between the state and federal governments would accelerate development.

Highlighting his administration’s achievements, Mutfwang said road construction and rehabilitation projects were ongoing across Plateau’s 17 local government areas, with several already completed and commissioned.



On education, he cited a 50 per cent reduction in tuition fees at Plateau State University, increased scholarship opportunities and efforts to secure accreditation for academic programmes across tertiary institutions. He added that investments in school infrastructure and learning materials were aimed at improving teaching and learning.



In the health sector, the governor said his administration had strengthened healthcare delivery through improved medical infrastructure, modern diagnostic equipment, expanded laboratory capacity and the revitalisation of primary healthcare facilities.



He also reaffirmed his commitment to tackling insecurity through improved intelligence gathering, security operations and community-based initiatives in collaboration with relevant agencies.

Mutfwang highlighted the introduction of the Tin City Metro bus service and other transportation initiatives designed to ease movement and reduce transportation costs for residents.



He commended Tinubu for approving major road projects affecting Plateau, including the Akwanga–Jos–Bauchi–Maiduguri corridor and the Mararaban Jama’a–Mangu–Kanke–Langtang–Shendam–Ibi road, describing them as strategic investments that could boost commerce and open up communities to economic opportunities.



The governor also noted Plateau’s growing political relevance, citing the emergence of Professor Nentawe Yilwatda as APC national chairman and the state’s historical contribution to national party leadership through the late Chief Solomon Lar.



Earlier, Deputy Governor Piyo, Secretary to the State Government Samuel Nanchant Jatau and Director-General of the Mutfwang/Piyo Campaign Council, Joseph Ari, commended the community for maintaining its ties with Plateau and urged members to sustain their support for the administration.

In his remarks, the community’s chairman, John Nanpe, thanked the governor for the visit and pledged the community’s continued solidarity and massive support for his re-election.



A community patron, Peter Dasat, also praised the administration’s development efforts and expressed confidence that voters would reward its performance in 2027.



Traditional rulers, women, youths and elders at the gathering echoed the pledge, reaffirming their support for Mutfwang’s leadership and his second-term ambition.

World.title: Sahara Foundation Launches New Go-Recycling Hub at Air Force Base in Ikeja
World.content:
Peter Uzoho

Sahara Group Foundation has inaugurated its Go Recycling Hub at Sam Ethnan Air Force Base in Ikeja, Lagos, reinforcing its commitment to environmental sustainability, community empowerment and inclusive economic growth.

The new hub advances the Foundation’s efforts to transform recyclable waste from an environmental liability into an economic asset, creating income opportunities for households through targeted waste-to-wealth programmes.

It also marks another step towards strengthening sustainable waste recovery systems and empowering host communities across Nigeria.

Speaking at the inauguration ceremony, Director of Sahara Group Foundation, Chidilim Menakaya, highlighted the Foundation’s continued investment in practical, community-focused solutions that deliver lasting environmental and socio-economic benefits.

“This initiative aligns with our sustainability and development priorities by transforming waste into valuable resources, reducing environmental impact, supporting climate action and creating livelihood opportunities. It demonstrates how communities can advance environmental responsibility while promoting inclusive economic growth,” she said.

Reiterating the Foundation’s broader vision, Menakaya noted that Sahara Go Recycling demonstrates the transformative potential of collective action in building cleaner, more resilient communities.

“Through collaboration, innovation and community participation, we are driving long-term environmental impact while improving livelihoods and strengthening community ownership of sustainable practices,” she added.

The Commander of 651 Base Services Group, Air Commodore M.A. Imam, commended the Foundation’s investment in environmental sustainability and emphasised the importance of collective action in addressing waste management challenges in rapidly growing communities.

Also speaking, the Head of Corporate Communications at Ikeja Electric, Kingsley Okotie, said the company was delighted to join forces with the Sahara Group Foundation to promote responsible environmental stewardship and sustainability at the Air Force base.

He reaffirmed Ikeja Electric’s commitment to building sustainable relationships, enhancing seamless power supply, and supporting the well-being of customers, institutions, businesses and communities.

Since its inception, Sahara Go Recycling has facilitated the recycling of more than 1,000 tonnes of recyclable waste and directly and indirectly supported over 2,000 livelihoods across collection, sorting, logistics and community-based enterprise activities.

Through strategic partnerships and community engagement, the initiative continues to promote recycling, unlock economic value from waste and encourage sustainable lifestyles.

World.title: Gov Ododo’s Policies May Undermine Tinubu’s Re-election in Kogi, Ijele Warns
World.content:
A social activist and politician, Isaiah Davies Ijele, has raised the alarm that the style of governance and policies of Kogi State Governor, Usman Ododo, may be undermining President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election chances in the state in 2027.

In a strong political intervention released on Friday, October 24, 2026, Ijele said it has become imperative for the president and the leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to be made aware of developments in the state.

According to him, “It has become imperative that Mr. President and the leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) are made aware that the style of governance and certain policies of Governor Usman Ododo in Kogi State may be undermining President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s chances of securing re-election in 2027.”

Ijele argued that at a time when the Federal Government allocates substantial resources to states and local governments, Nigerians have been encouraged to hold governors accountable for how public funds are managed.

“The question is simple: What is Kogi State doing with the resources available to it, and why are ordinary citizens still being subjected to unbearable economic pressure?” he queried.

He noted that Kogi State receives allocations running into billions of naira, including funds meant for local government administration and grassroots development, which he said should translate into better roads, affordable education, improved healthcare and stable electricity.

“Unfortunately, rather than feeling the impact of governance, many citizens are confronted with additional financial burdens,” Ijele stated.

The activist cited the reported N6,000 charge imposed on tricycle (Keke) riders for state stickers, describing the riders as ordinary people struggling to feed their families in a difficult economy.

“Why should they be made to pay more when government has access to public funds that should support development and improve living conditions?” he asked.

Ijele said the situation becomes more disturbing with the reported 100 per cent increase in school fees in state-owned institutions.

“At a time when parents are struggling to meet basic needs, doubling school fees places an enormous burden on families and threatens the educational aspirations of thousands of young people. Is this the change the people expected? Is this how a government demonstrates compassion for its citizens?” he asked.

He argued that other states are exploring ways to make education more affordable through scholarships and financial assistance, and Kogi should not be moving in the opposite direction.

“The problem is not simply about money. It is about priorities, accountability and the responsibility of government to its people,” Ijele stressed.

The activist said Kogi East in particular deserves more than political promises, adding that communities continue to demand meaningful infrastructure, good roads, electricity, functional healthcare facilities and economic opportunities.

“The people want to see the impact of public expenditure in their daily lives. If billions of naira are being allocated to government at different levels, citizens have every right to ask what tangible projects have been delivered, what they cost and how communities have benefited. Public resources must produce measurable results, not merely announcements and political publicity,” he said.

Ijele warned that President Tinubu has a political stake in how APC-controlled states perform, noting that while the president cannot be held personally responsible for every state policy, citizens may associate the performance of governors with the broader party.

“President Tinubu has a political stake in how APC-controlled states perform. The conduct of governors and other political officeholders will inevitably influence how voters judge the president and his administration,” he said.

He cautioned Governor Ododo that increasing financial burden on citizens could have political consequences.

“You cannot continuously increase the financial burden on citizens, frustrate students and their parents, and then expect the same people to enthusiastically support your preferred candidate at the polls. The people who pay these fees, the Keke riders who struggle to earn a living, the parents who sacrifice everything to educate their children, and the communities waiting for basic infrastructure are all voters. Their experiences will shape their political decisions in 2027,” Ijele warned.

According to him, “No amount of political mobilisation can permanently replace good governance, and no campaign slogan can erase the daily experiences of suffering citizens.”

Ijele called on the state government to review policies that impose excessive burdens, address concerns around school fees, ensure transparency in the use of public allocations and prioritise projects that directly improve lives.

“The people of Kogi State deserve responsible leadership. They deserve affordable education, accessible healthcare, good roads, reliable electricity and an administration that sees public revenue as a responsibility rather than an opportunity to impose more charges,” he stated.

He added that President Tinubu’s re-election campaign cannot be separated entirely from the performance of those governing under his party.

“If Governor Ododo wants Kogi people to support the president, his government must give them reasons to do so. You cannot make life harder for the people and expect their votes as a reward,” Ijele said.

He concluded that as it stands, there is zero visible impact of the state government in the nine local governments of Kogi East Senatorial District, while questioning how local government funds are being utilized.

“Governor Usman Ododo must act now, not when the political consequences of public dissatisfaction become impossible to reverse. Mr. President, act now before it’s too late!”

World.title: Abuja High Court Rules in Favour of Halkin E&P Over Eunisell
World.content:
The High Court of the Federal Capital Territory in Abuja has delivered judgment in favour of Halkin Exploration and Production Limited (Halkin E&P) in a suit brought by the company against Eunisell Limited over a disputed contractual provision.

The dispute centred on Clause 10.4 of a service agreement between Halkin E&P and Eunisell, which the court ruled was unenforceable, having found it to be a penalty clause designed to terrorise the claimant.

Under Clause 10.4 of the agreement, Halkin E&P was required to pay a late payment charge of 0.5 per cent daily, equivalent to approximately 177 per cent annually on a compound interest basis, on outstanding payments.

The provision resulted in Eunisell claiming millions of dollars in accumulated charges, reportedly exceeding ten times the underlying debt.

In its judgment, delivered by Justice S.B Belgore on October 22, 2026, the court held that “Clause 10.4 of the Service Agreement between Halkin Exploration and Production Limited and Eunisell Limited dated 20th January 2022, which imposes an annual default fee of 177% (equivalent of 0.5% per day), is null, void, and of no legal effect whatsoever.”

In addition, the court ruled that it was “setting aside, quashing, nullifying and invalidating all late payment/default invoices, bills and/or assessments, howsoever described, predicated on Clause 10.4 of the Service Agreement between Halkin Exploration and Production Limited and Eunisell Limited dated 20th January 2022 issued by the Defendant against the Claimant.”

Commenting on the ruling, counsel to Halkin E&P, Chikaosulu Ojukwu, SAN, said “This decision is a victory for the rule of law and vindicates the consistent position maintained by our client, Halkin E&P, that the impugned clause in the agreement was contrary to public policy and therefore unenforceable.

“Our client maintains that Eunisell Limited sought to use that clause to secure an unjustified financial windfall. The defendant Eunisell Limited withdrew from the oil well in the middle of the night, without notice, causing damage to the wellhead, according to our client. Our client will pursue a US$50 million claim against Eunisell Limited through the appropriate legal proceedings. This is a classical case of get rich quick” .

World.title: A Misguided Narrative: The Dangerous Implications Of Punch’s Editorial
World.content:
Biodun Ajiboye

The Punch Editorial Board’s October 16, 2026 piece on the political participation of chief executives of federal parastatals is far worse than merely flawed. It is an ill-fated, ill-informed overreach. It stands as a textbook example of journalism attempting to dictate law without basic comprehension.

The editorial’s central argument collapses under an elementary error in political science: conflating the civil service with the public service. In basic public administration (Public Administration 101), the civil service is recognised strictly as a subset of the larger public service framework. It constitutes the permanent, tenured bureaucracy within ministries and operates under its own distinct civil service rules. By failing to grasp this foundational distinction, the editorial builds its thesis on a fundamentally flawed premise.

The public service spans a far wider scope than the core civil service, incorporating political appointees, commission heads, and leaders of extra-ministerial departments whose offices exist at the president’s pleasure. Federal parastatal chief executives operate as political appointees and public servants rather than career civil servants.

To equate a presidentially appointed director-general, governing under a specific statutory Act, with a career Level 8 civil servant in the Ministry of Works is either profound intellectual laziness or deliberate mischief. If we are to accept Punch’s distorted logic from its, then federal ministers—who are also presidential appointees—must similarly be barred from political engagement. Would Punch ever dare to publish an editorial claiming the Minister of Information cannot campaign for his own government? The absolute absurdity of that premise exposes the emptiness of their entire argument.

The foundation of this debate is not the opinion of Punch. It is Section 40 of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, as amended, which the newspaper conveniently ignored. Section 40 guarantees every person, including public officers, the right to assemble freely and associate with other persons, including forming or belonging to any political party.

This right is not a privilege granted by any media organisation. It is constitutionally guaranteed. Any restriction on that right must be justifiable under Section 45—meaning that it must be reasonably justifiable in a democratic society in the interest of defence, public safety, public order, public morality, or public health. Where is the public danger in a director-general mobilising support for the president who appointed him? There is none.

Punch writes as if the Supreme Court has not spoken on this matter. It has, and authoritatively so. In INEC v. Balarabe Musa & 7 Ors (2003) 10 WRN 1, the apex court demolished the very argument Punch is now recycling.

Justice Emmanuel Ayoola (JSC) delivered a definitive blow to restrictions on civic freedoms, ruling that barring public and civil servants from political party membership is entirely indefensible in a democratic society. The apex court explicitly rejected the argument that public safety, order, morality, or health could justify such a ban, declaring that any attempt to weaponise Section 45(1)(a) to undermine the fundamental political rights guaranteed under Section 40 of the Constitution is fundamentally erroneous.

The Supreme Court explicitly branded it erroneous, yet the newspaper—in a blatant characterisation—upheld it as law. In his landmark concurring judgment, the former Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Mohammed Lawal Uwais, dismantled any ambiguity.

He declared that the provisions of Section 40 of the 1999 Constitution are absolute: every citizen, including civil servants and public office holders, possesses the fundamental right to assemble freely and associate with any political party, trade union, or association to protect their interests. Justice Uwais underscored that the constitution makes zero exceptions and enforces no restrictions on public officers. Where the highest law of the land refuses to draw lines, Punch has arbitrarily invented them.

Even the Head of Service circular, upon which Punch’s argument implicitly relies, was clarified by the Supreme Court judgment. After her office was inundated with requests for clarification on the apex court’s ruling, the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation issued a memo dated May 5, 2022, attempting to enforce the 2008 Public Service Rules regarding partisan politics.

That clarification is exactly what the newspaper missed. The Public Service Rules cannot override the constitution. Because the rules are merely subsidiary legislation, the constitution remains supreme. Where the PSR conflicts with Section 40 (as interpreted by the Supreme Court), it becomes void to the extent of that inconsistency. This is the core principle of constitutional supremacy under Section 1(3)—something paper should well know.

We are arguing for legal precision, not anarchy. The law draws a sharp line between the right to belong to a political party and the act of partisan mobilisation on official duty. This distinction is anchored in explicit terms of appointment, strict codes of conduct, and enabling statutes. It cannot be erased by a blanket editorial lumping everyone into a single category.

A chief executive retains every lawful right to be a committed member, supporter, and mobilizer for the All Progressives Congress (APC), provided these activities are conducted within legal boundaries and outside official functions. The law does not demand political neutrality; it demands structural integrity.

What it strictly forbids is the weaponisation of the office—specifically, the diversion of public funds, the exploitation of official hours, and the use of coercive power to compromise subordinates. By issuing a sweeping, lazy ban, Punch completely bypassed this crucial legal nuance, mistaking legitimate association for institutional abuse.

This editorial is a masterclass in legal illiteracy and political alarmism. It is a transparent attempt to intimidate appointees legitimately driving the re-election campaign of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. Let there be no mistake: momentum is firmly on our side, and the opposition is visibly feeling the heat.

Recent media commentary has drifted into fiction, yet our resolve remains unshaken. We will continue to consolidate our gains and sustain the momentum of our strategic political engagement. Moving forward, our actions will remain strictly within the law, guided exclusively by our official mandates and the constitution—not by outside noise.

The law is settled and the Supreme Court has cleared the air. All Nigerian workers, whether civil or public servants, possess the constitutional right to participate in politics. No media editorial can rewrite the constitution. The Punch is simply late to class.

* Otunba Ajiboye is Chairman, Media & Publicity Committee of FORCEPA, and Executive Secretary/CEO, National Institute for Cultural Orientation (NICO)

World.title: Wahala App, NIIA Forge Alliance to Deploy AI for Security Intelligence, Business Risk Management
World.content:
Nigerian technology company, Wahala App Ltd, has partnered with the General Leo Irabor Early Warning Systems Centre (GLIC) of the Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA) to deploy artificial intelligence (AI) and real-time data analytics for security intelligence, operational risk management and business continuity.

The partnership is expected to strengthen early warning capabilities by integrating citizen-generated incident reports with AI-powered analytics to identify emerging threats, monitor security trends and provide businesses, government institutions and other organisations with information to support timely decision-making.

In a statement issued in Lagos, the company said the collaboration would give the Centre access to its Wahala Network, a digital platform that aggregates incident reports from individuals, businesses and participating organisations to provide insights into security risks and potential operational disruptions. The initiative comes amid growing demand for technology-driven solutions to security challenges, particularly as businesses seek to minimise exposure to threats affecting logistics, supply chains, personnel and other critical operations.

According to the company, the platform’s analytical capabilities enable organisations to identify recurring incidents, detect previously overlooked vulnerabilities and assess the potential impact of security developments on their operations. It explained that AI-powered analysis could also establish connections between seemingly unrelated incidents, providing insights into wider security and socioeconomic risks affecting industries and communities.

The Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Wahala App Ltd, Oriekaose Agholor, said the partnership represented an important step towards integrating citizen participation with institutional early warning systems and expanding the commercial application of real-time security intelligence.

“Safety is a shared responsibility, and timely information can help people make more informed decisions about their surroundings. Our partnership with GLIC is an important step towards connecting citizen participation with wider early warning efforts,” Agholor said.

He added that the company was seeking further partnerships with government agencies, corporate organisations and other institutions to expand the reach of its technology and improve access to actionable security information. Under the arrangement, businesses connected to the Wahala Network would be able to receive information on incidents that could affect their operations, including developments requiring adjustments to transportation routes, logistics planning and personnel safety measures.

The company said its technology could also support preventive risk management by identifying patterns of incidents that might otherwise develop into larger operational or security crises. Agholor noted that wider adoption of the platform could strengthen information sharing across sectors and help organisations respond more effectively to emerging risks.

“We invite Nigerians, businesses and institutions to join us in building a more informed and safety-conscious society,” he said.

Also speaking, Acting Head of the General Leo Irabor Early Warning Systems Centre, Dr Omotola Ilesanmi, said technology and reliable information were increasingly important to effective risk management and institutional preparedness.

“Effective early warning depends on the timely identification of risks and the availability of reliable information to support informed decision-making,” Ilesanmi said. “Technology and citizen participation can contribute to this process by strengthening awareness of emerging risks and supporting preparedness.”

Beyond institutional collaboration, Wahala App said it was expanding public engagement through its Ambassadors Against Wahala programme, which encourages responsible incident reporting and safety awareness across workplaces, educational institutions, religious organisations and communities. The company explained that its digital platform enables users to report incidents, receive location-relevant alerts and send emergency notifications to designated contacts, while its broader technology offerings provide organisations with data-driven insights for security planning and operational resilience.

It emphasised that the platform was intended to complement the responsibilities of government security agencies and emergency response institutions rather than replace existing security structures. Wahala App said the partnership formed part of its broader strategy to deepen collaboration with public institutions and private sector operators, expand the application of AI in risk intelligence and strengthen the role of technology in Nigeria’s security and business environment. The company, which specialises in real-time crisis awareness and management, operates a digital network connecting citizens, businesses and institutions through incident reporting, emergency alerts and AI-powered risk analysis.

World.title: Nigeria Shows Global Tech Giants Are Not Beyond Reach, Says Luminate CEO
World.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of Luminate, Melanie Hui, has praised Nigeria as a leading example of how African countries can shape the global artificial intelligence economy rather than simply consume it. She pointed to the country’s regulators, workers and innovators as proof that the continent is already setting its own terms.

Hui gave the keynote address at the Build 2026 Conference in Abuja on Wednesday. The audience included the Honourable Minister of Communication, Innovation and Digital Economy, heads of government parastatals, members of the diplomatic community and members of the Nigeria AI Collective. She said research Luminate commissioned this year on the continent’s AI landscape “found not only patterns of extraction and inequality. It found imagination and leadership.”

“Here, there are important reasons for optimism,” she said.

Hui cited the action Nigeria’s competition authority took against Meta over data exploitation and discriminatory practices. She said this showed that “global tech companies are not beyond the reach of national institutions.” She also praised app-based drivers in Nigeria for securing government recognition for Africa’s first e-hailing trade union.

She said innovators across Nigeria are “using locally built, practical technology to serve the underserved: from bringing reliable banking for rural communities to tackling massive crop losses.”

Her examples from elsewhere on the continent were litigation in Kenya establishing that global technology companies can be brought before Kenyan courts civil society coalitions in South Africa challenging bulk surveillance at the Constitutional Court AI-assisted learning materials in local languages helping children in Mali drones extending healthcare to remote islands in Uganda

“They are not merely enduring technology,” she said of Africa’s technologists, teachers, climate advocates, feminists, trade unions, youth movements and public interest lawyers. “They are shaping and reshaping it.”

“These examples matter because ownership is also about power: the power to negotiate, regulate, organise and secure remedy,” she added.

Hui’s speech was titled “Africa in the Global AI Order: Towards Equitable Ownership and Shared Prosperity.” She made clear that Luminate stands behind Africa’s ambition to be a full participant in the AI economy.

“My African friends tell me they will not be confined to the role of consumer, supplier of raw data, source of critical minerals or provider of low-paid labour in somebody else’s AI economy,” she said. “And Luminate will stand with them in securing a better digital age.”

She said equitable ownership “means moving beyond participation alone.” It means having “meaningful influence over the infrastructure, the institutions, the partnerships, the choices that will determine Africa’s digital future.”

She also said Africa’s young and growing population, along with its markets, languages and cultures, “will be enormously valuable to the development of future AI systems.”

Hui rejected the argument, made by some in the tech industry, that regulation holds innovation back. She offered a more hopeful view of how growth and fairness can go together.

“Those of us who promote tech justice must not lend credence to some in the tech industry who would paint regulation as a brake on progress. I disagree,” she said. “Safeguards are the allies of progress. Inclusion is the engine of meaningful scale. Sovereignty means being stronger together.”

“Prosperity is not shared automatically,” she added. “It is shared because workers have bargaining power. Because markets can compete. Because regulators and courts have resources and authority. Because people can seek remedy when they are harmed.”

To show what successful AI deployment needs, Hui described how India’s Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare used AI to predict the start of the monsoon for 40 million farmers. She credited African expert Rose Mutiso with the insight that AI “was the last piece of this breakthrough, not the first.”

World.title: Nigeria’s Judiciary and Its Corruption Malady
World.content:
By Mobolaji Sanusi

“An impartial judiciary is essential to the administration of justice and the preservation of liberty.”

— James Madison (1751-1836)

Democracy without a credible judiciary is an invitation to a Hobbesian state of nature, where life is brutish, nasty, poor, and short. Like all human creations, state institutions established by human reasoning are not infallible and are susceptible to sometimes avoidable foibles. But when such imperfections become abysmally alarming, every right-thinking citizen should be deeply perturbed.

That is the shameful state of the Bench in Nigeria today, which is continually acknowledged by very senior stakeholders in the legal profession and beyond. Conflict, which is an essential part of societal coexistence, is becoming increasingly difficult to resolve fairly through the instrumentality of the courts.

This must have informed the country’s uninspiring, dismal ranking of 120th out of 143 countries in the 2025 World Justice Project Rule of Law Index. Given the exposed entrenched corruption on the Bench and in the legal profession generally, coupled with unchecked political interference and inadequate funding, the rating might even be worse by the time the 2026 ranking is released.

Expectedly, the court is a reflection of the society we live in, and the depth of its rot raises a pertinent and fundamental question: Is there any facet of Nigerian life that is immune to the malady of corruption? Yours sincerely acknowledge that there are still honourable judges and other Nigerians who remain above board, but they are so few in number that their feeble voices of reason have been drowned by the tumultuous horde of corrupt plunderers of the public till.

From the days of yore till the present, stakeholders within the legal system and observers outside the noble profession have been concerned and have consistently spoken out against the rot in that increasingly desecrated, fast diminishing profession in the country. Yet, the abysmal state of affairs in the judiciary and legal profession is not improving, and it continues to trouble reputable persons in the polity.

It is therefore unsurprising that retired Justice Amina Adamu Augie has become the latest voice in that regard. She is in a better position to know the extent of endemic corruption in the legal profession as a former teacher of lawyers and a retired Justice of the nation’s apex court. She might not be completely insulated from the rot like other justices/judges and lawyers, but she has raised a justifiable alarm at the recently held 40th anniversary of the Nigerian Law School Class of 1986, where she decried high-level corruption within Nigeria’s judiciary and legal profession.

She declared that corruption in the legal profession, wherever it exists — “on the Bench, at the Bar, or in the Registry — poisons everything by turning the one place where a citizen should find impartiality into one more market stall.”

That damning description of the judiciary as a “market stall” should not be taken lightly, because of the significance of the judiciary and the legal profession towards resolving recurring societal disputes, both human and institutional.

Until now, some Justices of the apex court have curiously deployed their valedictory sessions to expose the rot in the judiciary and the legal profession as a whole. Justice Musa Dattijo Muhammad, who retired as the second most senior Justice of the Supreme Court and Deputy Chairperson of the National Judicial Council, some time earlier noted the “witheringly scornful and monstrously critical” public perception of the judiciary, stemming from “court officials and judges easily being bribed by litigants to obviate delays and/or obtain favourable judgments.”

Similarly, Justice Adefope-Okojie, JCA, at the point of her exit, asked what qualifies any person to bear the exalted title of ‘Honourable Justice’ if not to administer justice without fear or favour. She bemoaned the increasing degeneration of honourable traits in members of the Bench and the Bar.

Justice Ejembi Eko, at his valedictory from the Supreme Court in 2022, expressed concerns about the tepid handling of corruption issues on the Bench by the NJC when he said: “With deference to the NJC, the punishment usually falls short of public expectation… When the punishment for an outstandingly bad and outrageous conduct is far too lenient, it encourages impunity and/or a repeat by others of such errant or atrocious misconduct.”

So far, the effort of the NJC in this regard is work in progress.

Afam Osigwe, the immediate past Nigerian Bar Association President, also earlier this year, during the National Association of Seadogs-organised Ralph Obiora Lecture that held in Enugu State, corroborated the rapacious corruption ravaging especially the Bench when he said: “The judiciary, once revered as the last hope of the common man, is increasingly perceived as a marketplace where justice is auctioned to the highest bidder.”

Osigwe relied on a 2024 survey by the UNODC and the National Bureau of Statistics which revealed that approximately N721 billion in cash bribes was received by public officials in 2023, with judges named as top recipients. An ICPC survey also reportedly showed that N9.4 billion in bribes passed through the justice sector, with lawyers and litigants identified as primary bribe-givers between 2018 and 2020. This is alarmingly condemnable.

Even the revered quintessential jurist of our time, Justice Kayode Eso, who passed on in November 2012, observed the rot in his book The Judiciary: The Shield of Justice, thus: “Corruption in the judiciary is a major problem that needs to be addressed. It is a problem that has been affecting the integrity and effectiveness of the judicial system… We need to take urgent steps to address corruption in the judiciary.”

Again, the question arises: are the necessary steps being taken to address this problem when the judiciary unfortunately relies absolutely on the executive branch for its survival? It made for shameful optics when, not too long ago, the Chief Judge of the nation’s Federal High Court, Honourable Justice John Terhemba Tsoho, led fellow judges cap-in-hand to beg the FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, for landed property and other perquisites.

In my Yoruba culture, there’s a saying that “Ti enu ba je, oju a ti” — He who pays the piper dictates the tune. Following from this, it can be inferred that it will be difficult for the Bench to say a complete NO to the demands of their benefactor called Wike or anyone in the executive arm whenever the need arises. Too bad!

No wonder it is widely believed that corruption in the judiciary will subsist for as long as we have a judiciary that “…must beg the executive for a courtroom roof, vehicles, judges’ entitlements and financial autonomy for the courts” — all of which should ordinarily be constitutional perquisites of office for Justices and Judges.

The 2027 general elections are fast approaching and ours is a country where no politician contesting for positions accedes to defeat at the polls. Election losers in our clime always approach the Election Petition Tribunal on the flimsiest of excuses to contest their loss. Do we rely on “compromisable or tainted judicial officers” to move our democracy forward? This question under the prevailing circumstance is better left unanswered. Too bad!

The country must get its act right if we truly desire a judiciary that is, in words and deeds, largely an impartial referee, not a player in the game. What we have now is largely a courtroom where the calm and neutral administration of the law yields to political interests and pecuniary inducements; a complete reflection of the times we all live in and shamelessly adore for parochial sentiments. On this note, l rest my case for this week.

Ipoola Omisore Relocates ‘Ile-Ife Greats’ To Lagos

“A room without books is like a body without a soul.”

– Marcus Tallius Cicero (January 3, 106 BC—December 7, 43 BC).

The date is October 30, 2026. On that day, Lagos will be agog with a momentous event meant to celebrate recorded reputable sons and daughters of the Yoruba cradle from the Source in Ile-Ife, Osun State.

The convener of the event is none other than the elder statesman, accomplished advertising professional, educationist, author, and two-term former member of the House of Assembly of the Centre of Excellence, Hon. Ahmed Ipoola Omisore, who authored the book titled: “Great Ifes in History,” which will be launched on that day.

The Royal Father of the Day is His Imperial Majesty, Oba Babatunde Enitan Ogunwusi, CFR, while the Principal Guest of Honour is His Excellency, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat—the incoming governor of Lagos state come May 29,2027, insha Allah. The Father-of-the-Day is Chief Oyekunle Alex-Duduyemi, while the book reviewer is the accomplished journalist, President Emeritus of the Nigerian Guild of Editors and Provost of the Nigerian Institute of Journalism, Mr. Gbenga Adefaye.

Definitely, next Friday promises to be an interesting day at the Lagos Airport Hotel, Ikeja, venue for this promising event by Honourable Omisore.

Trust me, yours sincerely will be present at the occasion to celebrate the day with invited guests…..Congratulations in advance Honourable Omisore…

World.title: Two arrested for illegally feeding, exploiting Cape fur seals
World.content:
Two suspects are in custody after allegedly feeding and harassing Cape fur seals at Hout Bay Harbour. Image: Cape of Good Hope SPCA

Two suspects have been arrested for the alleged unlawful feeding and harassment of Cape fur seals in Hout Bay, Cape Town.

The arrests took place on Friday, 23 October 2026, at Hout Bay Harbour.

SPCA SWOOPS IN

According to the Cape of Good Hope SPCA, the arrests were precipitated by “ongoing complaints about activities that bring visitors, including children, into dangerously close contact with wild seals in exchange for paid photographs.”



Additionally, the suspects allegedly displayed “aggression or hostility” when visitors declined to pay a fee after the photographs were taken.

The SPCA worked alongside the City of Cape Town Law Enforcement Animal Control Unit and the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment to take the two suspects into custody.

SEALS: WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW

Cape fur seals reside on South Africa’s western coastline. They live in tight-knit colonies that span hundreds, and they tend to be calm and non-aggressive when encountering humans.

Nevertheless, members of the public are strongly discouraged from feeding or interacting with seals. This is especially if the seals feel threatened or are injured or infected by rabies.

Seals are also protected under the National Environmental Management: Biodiversity Act and the Threatened or Protected Marine Species Regulations. As such, you are prohibited from feeding, physically interacting with or harassing seals. Failure to adhere to these laws constitutes criminal offences.

“Visitors are urged to watch seals from a safe distance, give them space to move freely, and decline encounters that involve food, touching or close posing,” the SPCA says. “Please report concerns to the SPCA or Law Enforcement rather than confronting those involved.



“The SPCA and its enforcement partners will continue spot checks and undercover operations at the harbour to gather evidence and take action where offences are detected. Hout Bay’s seals deserve to remain wild, and everyone visiting the harbour deserves to be safe.”

SEAL FEEDERS CONVICTED

In related news, two men were convicted and sentenced back in May for the unlawful feeding and exploitation of Cape fur seals. They would do so also at Hout Bay Harbour.

They each received a sentence of an R80 000 fine or 24 months’ imprisonment, wholly suspended for five years, provided that they are not convicted of a similar offence during that period.

What are your thoughts about this latest arrest and the ongoing exploitation of Cape fur seals? Let us know in the comments below!

World.title: MK Party condemns IEC over rejection of candidate list corrections
World.content:
The uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party has condemned the Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) for rejecting its request to correct and rectify its candidate lists.

The party said it had submitted a formal request seeking corrections to its candidate nominations, including the placement of ward candidates, omitted candidates and candidates who have since died.

The MK Party said on Tuesday, 20 October, the IEC rejected its requested amendments, maintaining that the ANC versus IEC court case did not reopen the nomination process beyond the limited restoration of nominations that had already been captured on the online system before nominations closed.



The party, led by former president Jacob Zuma, has since demanded that the IEC provide a substantive written report explaining why its requested corrections were rejected, with reasons for each rejection.

It has also called for a clear explanation of the distinction between the relief granted in the ANC proceedings and the corrections sought by the MK Party.

CONCERNS OVER IEC’S TRANSPARENCY

The party has also raised concerns about the IEC’s administration of electoral processes, including the dashboard interruption during the 2024 elections, according to Mahlangu.



“With regard to the party’s candidate list leak in 2024, the IEC confirmed the unauthorised disclosure of candidate lists belonging to the MK Party and ANC, raising serious concerns about the protection of sensitive electoral information,” Mahlangu said.

He also referred to allegations made by Congolese opposition figures against Janet Love, whom they accused of helping to legitimise an allegedly fabricated voter register in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

Mahlangu further cited the charges of theft, fraud and money laundering involving R1.2 million faced by the IEC’s former deputy chairperson Nomsa Masuku, relating to her former employment at Standard Bank.



“The importance of transparency and accountability has not diminished. The current dispute over candidate lists reinforces our distrust in the Commission,” he said.

World.title: Weather: Brace for a wet, stormy Sunday in these provinces
World.content:
Wet and stormy conditions could affect parts of South Africa on Sunday. Image: AI illustration

Here is what the weather has in store for KZN, the Free State, and the North West on Sunday 25 October 2026.

A Yellow Level 2 warning is in place for severe thunderstorms in central and eastern KZN, with heavy rain, hail, damaging winds and possible flooding.

Extremely high fire danger conditions are expected in parts of northern KwaZulu-Natal, increasing the risk of veld fires.



KWAZULU-NATAL

Morning fog over the interior, otherwise partly cloudy and warm to hot with isolated showers and thundershowers except in the extreme north-east.

The wind along the coast will be moderate to fresh northerly to north-easterly but moderate to fresh south- westerly south of Durban, spreading to Richards Bay in the evening

The UVB sunburn will be very high.

DURBAN

Durban is going to be partly cloudy to cloudy with isolated showers and thundershowers



Light to moderate northerly to north-easterly winds will shift to moderate to fresh southerly to south-westerly winds in the afternoon.

Temperatures will range from 19°C to 26°C.

The UVB sunburn index will be very high.

FREE STATE

Free State should be fine fine, windy and warm to hot, becoming partly cloudy with isolated afternoon showers and thundershowers



BLOEMFONTEIN

Bloemfontein is going to be fine and windy, becoming partly cloudy with isolated afternoon showers and thundershowers

Temperatures will range from a minimum of 13°C to a maximum of 31°C.

NORTH WEST

North West is going to be fine, windy and hot, becoming partly cloudy with isolated afternoon showers and thundershowers.



MAHIKENG

Mahikeng is going to be fine and windy, becoming partly cloudy with isolated afternoon showers and thundershowers.
