World.title: Latin America Defense Monitor — October 17–23, 2026
World.content:
The Big Picture: This week’s Latin America Defense Monitor follows a rescue mission in Haiti and a terrorism list in Buenos Aires. Both show how far the US-led security campaign now reaches, from a UN-backed force in Port-au-Prince to the legal registries of South American governments.

On Sunday, 18 October, gunmen attacked an armored vehicle of the Gang Suppression Force, the UN-backed mission in Haiti, and four Salvadoran aviation technicians vanished. On Thursday, 22 October, about 100 Salvadoran special-forces troops landed in Haiti to search for them, with another 100 expected.

The same day, Argentina’s Official Gazette published a joint resolution naming five criminal and insurgent groups as terrorist organisations. Washington already lists three of them, so Buenos Aires is moving closer to the US line, as The Rio Times reported on 22 October.

Bottom Line Up Front: Haiti is the open question. Four men are missing, a second Salvadoran contingent is unconfirmed, and the force they serve is still far below its planned strength.

World.title: Ethiopia Calls for Shared Red Sea Security
World.content:
ETHIOPIA · RED SEA SECURITY

Key Facts — What is happening Ethiopia’s intelligence chief told a regional peace forum in Bahir Dar on Friday, 23 October, that no handful of states can secure the Red Sea alone.

— Why it matters Attacks on ships near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the Red Sea’s southern gate, threaten the trade route between Asia and Europe, and landlocked Ethiopia depends on it.

— The numbers The forum runs three days, 23 to 25 October, and the opening panel had five envoys plus a moderator. No money amounts, ship counts or casualty figures were given.

— Who is who Redwan Huseen heads Ethiopia’s National Intelligence and Security Service. Getachew Reda advises the prime minister on East African affairs and singled out Eritrea, Ethiopia’s northern neighbor, for fomenting crisis.

— What to watch Watch for any communique from the Tana Forum, which ends on Sunday, 25 October, and for a reply from Eritrea’s government to the accusations made in Bahir Dar.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives Eritrean forces entering Ethiopia and taking control of territory a 4.4% chance by October 31 and 14.5% by December 31 (24 October, 10:10 a.m. ET).

— What it means for you For US readers, Red Sea attacks can lift shipping and energy costs, and Washington has already urged restraint over the Ethiopia-Eritrea tensions.

Ethiopia’s intelligence chief says no handful of countries can keep the Red Sea safe alone. He spoke on Friday, 23 October, as a regional security forum opened in Bahir Dar.

Ethiopia called for shared Red Sea security on Friday, 23 October 2026, as a regional diplomacy dialogue opened. Ambassador Redwan Huseen, who runs the National Intelligence and Security Service, warned of militarization and renewed attacks on shipping.

The Red Sea is the sea lane linking Asia, the Suez Canal and Europe, so trouble there can reach US prices. Ethiopia has no coastline, and Redwan said it relies entirely on the Red Sea for maritime trade.

What Happened at the Tana Forum Dialogue

The Special Envoys’ Dialogue opened in Bahir Dar on Friday, part of the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Security in Africa. The forum runs from 23 to 25 October under the theme “Pathways to Peace in Africa: Economic Sovereignty and Geopolitical Transformation”.

The dialogue’s own theme was regional security in the Horn of Africa and the Red Sea. Paul-Simon Handy, listed as regional director for East Africa and African Union representative, moderated the panel.

Fana Media Corporation and the Ethiopian News Agency, both state outlets, covered the opening on Friday. Horn Diplomat and Ethiopia’s foreign ministry blog also reported on the dialogue.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Ethiopia Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Ethiopia’s Spy Chief Said About Red Sea Security

Redwan said militarization, rivalry among foreign powers and renewed attacks on commercial ships in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait strain regional trade routes. The strait is the narrow passage between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.

He argued that Red Sea security cannot be guaranteed by a handful of coastal states acting alone. He called for collective action by regional states and reliable international partners.

Redwan also said he expects the dialogue to produce actionable recommendations. He wants them to align peace initiatives and strengthen cooperation between regional and continental frameworks.

What the Foreign Envoys Said

Guang Cong, the UN secretary-general’s special envoy for the Horn of Africa, called the situation a “polycrisis”. He said wars in Sudan, South Sudan and Somalia and Red Sea shipping threats are deeply linked, the Ethiopian News Agency reports.

Germany’s envoy, Heiko Nitzschke, noted a heightened sense of urgency among European and African policymakers. He cited the impact on trade routes through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and urged region-led peace initiatives and economic integration.

France’s envoy, Frédéric Clavier, said stronger multilateral cooperation is needed to stabilize the Horn of Africa and the Red Sea region. Pekka Haavisto, the UN secretary-general’s personal envoy for Sudan, said diplomatic efforts must line up behind crises that span several states.

In Plain English Tana Forum: a security conference held this year in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, that gathers African and foreign diplomats.

a security conference held this year in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, that gathers African and foreign diplomats. Bab el-Mandeb: the narrow strait at the southern end of the Red Sea, a gateway for ships bound to and from the Suez Canal.

the narrow strait at the southern end of the Red Sea, a gateway for ships bound to and from the Suez Canal. National Intelligence and Security Service: Ethiopia’s main spy and security agency, led by Redwan Huseen.

Ethiopia’s main spy and security agency, led by Redwan Huseen. Horn of Africa: the region of Ethiopia, Eritrea, Djibouti and Somalia on Africa’s eastern tip.

Why Ethiopia Pointed at Eritrea

Getachew Reda, adviser to the prime minister on East African affairs, used the panel to criticize Eritrea. He singled out Eritrea as one of the players showing “recalcitrant behavior” and continuing to “foment crisis”, the Ethiopian News Agency reports.

He said Ethiopia prefers dialogue and multilateral frameworks, citing the Pretoria Agreement on northern Ethiopia. He warned that domestic peace efforts face interference from regional actors and urged the world to confront outside forces fueling instability.

Eritrea’s foreign ministry had already rejected Ethiopian accusations in a statement reported by the Ethiopian news site Borkena on 22 October. It denied that Eritrean troops have crossed into Ethiopia and called generalized calls on both sides legally deficient.

That statement also rejected de-escalation appeals from the UN, the African Union, the United States and Britain. No Eritrean reply to the Bahir Dar remarks has been found.

What It Means for US Readers

The Red Sea route carries trade between Asia and Europe through the Suez Canal. Attacks near Bab el-Mandeb can raise freight and energy costs for US buyers.

Washington is already involved in the Ethiopia-Eritrea dispute. On Sunday, 18 October, Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged restraint over Ethiopia-Eritrea tensions, The Reporter and Capital report.

He warned that troops surging on both sides of the border could spark a wider regional war. He also defended lifting some sanctions on Eritrea as a targeted step to open diplomatic channels.

The panel list published by Fana names no US envoy, and no US statement at the dialogue was found. No new sanctions, shipping rules or aid decisions were announced in Bahir Dar.

US readers should treat the dialogue as diplomatic signaling, not as a change on the water. Shipping costs and the Eritrea dispute are the two things to track.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a real-money prediction platform, lists “Eritrea invades Ethiopia by…?” with about US$115,000 in total volume. The October 31 contract trades at 4.4% (about US$55,000 volume) and the December 31 contract at 14.5% (about US$60,000).

A Yes needs Eritrean forces to enter Ethiopia and take control of territory for 48 hours or more by the date. Prices were read at 10:10 a.m. ET on 24 October 2026, and the dialogue reports mention no such operation.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

No joint statement or recommendations from the dialogue had been published in the sources read. The forum continues until 25 October, so conclusions may still come.

Redwan did not name who carried out the renewed attacks on ships. The reports give no shipping figures, vessel names or dates.

Eritrea’s government has not been found replying to Getachew’s remarks. Claims by both capitals about troops and borders cannot be checked independently from these sources.

Ethiopian state media supplied the envoys’ remarks, and they paraphrase more than they quote. This article therefore attributes each statement and adds no detail the reports do not give.

What Comes Next

Mozambique’s President Daniel Chapo is due to give a keynote at the forum on Saturday, 24 October, the Club of Mozambique reports. The forum closes on Sunday, 25 October.

Watch for a Tana Forum communique and any Eritrean response to Ethiopia’s remarks. A change in shipping attacks near Bab el-Mandeb would matter more to US readers than the speeches.

Earlier coverage: Ethiopia Warns Eritrea of Severe Cost and US Ambassador Urges Ethiopia Talks. Background: Foreign Military Bases in the Horn of Africa Explained.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Tana Forum?

The Tana High-Level Forum on Security in Africa is a gathering on African peace and security. Its 12th edition runs from 23 to 25 October 2026 in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia.

What did Ethiopia say about the Red Sea?

Ethiopia’s intelligence chief said Red Sea security cannot rest with a handful of states. He called for collective action by regional states and reliable international partners.

Why does a landlocked country care about the Red Sea?

Ethiopia has no coastline, and Redwan said it relies entirely on the Red Sea for maritime trade. Attacks on ships therefore threaten its trade routes.

Did the United States take part in the dialogue?

The panel list published by Fana names envoys from the UN, France, Germany and Ethiopia, but no US envoy. The sources do not say whether US officials attended other sessions.

Will this change shipping costs or fuel prices?

No decision was announced in Bahir Dar. The envoys’ warnings are signals rather than measures.

World.title: Morocco Arms Buying Cap Rises to US$19B
World.content:
MOROCCO · DEFENSE

Key Facts — What is happening Morocco’s 2027 budget bill, presented to Parliament on Friday, 23 October, lets the defense minister sign arms and equipment deals worth up to MAD 190.5 billion (about US$19.4 billion) in advance.

— Why it matters The cap is 21% above the 2026 level and 53% above 2024, which gives a country that flies US built jets room for more arms orders.

— The numbers The cap rises from MAD 157.2 billion (about US$16.0 billion) to MAD 190.5 billion (about US$19.4 billion), while the 2027 cash for the equipment account stays near MAD 11.5 billion (about US$1.2 billion).

— Who is who The Royal Armed Forces are Morocco’s military; Abdellatif Loudiyi runs the defense administration, and Fouzi Lekjaa, the finance minister, presented the bill in the government of Fatima Zahra El Mansouri.

— What to watch Parliament now debates the bill, and the next signs are named contracts, including any US ones, plus the final vote, which has no date yet.

— What it means for you For US readers, this is permission to commit money, not a signed order, but it gives room for US jet, vehicle and training orders that US firms and the Pentagon serve.

Morocco wants the legal room to order up to US$19.4 billion of military equipment in advance. The request sits in the 2027 budget bill that the finance minister presented on Friday, 23 October.

Morocco’s government has asked Parliament to lift the Morocco arms buying cap to MAD 190.5 billion (about US$19.4 billion). The request is Article 36 of Finance Bill No. 60.26, presented by Finance Minister Fouzi Lekjaa on Friday, 23 October.

For a US reader, the number matters because Morocco flies US built F-16 jets and C-130 transport planes. It is a ceiling on future orders, not cash spent in 2027, and no contract has been named.

What Article 36 of the Budget Bill Says

The bill’s Arabic text lets the defense minister commit up to MAD 190.5 billion (about US$19.4 billion) in 2027. The finance ministry site publishes the text, and the money comes from credits that Parliament would open in 2028.

The commitments run through a special account for buying and repairing military equipment and for building the defense industry. Such limits let ministries sign multi-year contracts before the money is paid.

The 2026 limit was MAD 157.17 billion (about US$16.0 billion), so the rise is MAD 33.3 billion (about US$3.4 billion), or 21%. Hespress, a Moroccan news site, says this is the largest rise among the advance limits in the bill.

In Plain English: Four Terms to Know

Finance Bill: the government’s draft budget, which Parliament must pass before the year starts.

the government’s draft budget, which Parliament must pass before the year starts. Advance commitment cap: a legal limit on contracts signed now and paid from later budgets.

a legal limit on contracts signed now and paid from later budgets. Royal Armed Forces (FAR): Morocco’s army, air force, navy and royal gendarmerie.

Morocco’s army, air force, navy and royal gendarmerie. Special account: a ring-fenced fund that pays for weapons purchases, heavy repairs and defense industry support.

How the Cap Has Grown Since 2024

Hespress lists the limit as MAD 124.77 billion in 2024 (about US$12.7 billion) and MAD 133.45 billion in 2025 (about US$13.6 billion). The 2026 figure was MAD 157.17 billion (about US$16.0 billion), and the new request is MAD 190.5 billion (about US$19.4 billion).

From 2024 to 2027, the cap would rise by about 53%, based on the Hespress figures. The cap lets the ministry sign contracts in 2027 that are paid from 2028 credits.

Abdelhamid Harifi, an analyst with the FAR-Maroc forum, told Le360 that the cap is room to act over several years. He said it is not a one year bill, and weapons cost far more than five or ten years ago.

Where the Annual Defense Money Goes

The yearly budget moves much less than the cap. Personnel costs rise to MAD 49.34 billion (about US$5.0 billion), up about 5%, which Le360 ties to pay rises.

The bill also creates 5,500 budget posts for the defense administration, which the bill text confirms. Equipment and miscellaneous costs reach MAD 8.37 billion (about US$0.85 billion).

Investment totals MAD 15.2 billion (about US$1.5 billion), split between 2027 payments and commitments for later years. The special equipment account gets MAD 11.49 billion (about US$1.2 billion), against MAD 11.5 billion in 2026.

US Jets, Vehicles and Training in the Picture

Lockheed Martin announced on Tuesday, 6 October, that the first F-16 Block 72 jet for Morocco completed its first flight. The same release says Moroccan forces will receive HIMARS rocket launchers, but gives no delivery date.

The US Army said it will hold its first counter-drone technology event in Tan-Tan, southern Morocco, in spring 2027. Soldier demonstrations are planned for February and March, then an assessment in April and May during the African Lion exercise.

Oshkosh Defense announced on Monday, 5 October, a Moroccan order for 50 heavy equipment tractors and 50 trailers, Hespress reports. The reports give no price for the order, which is a direct commercial sale between the company and Morocco.

On 7 October, at the Marrakech Air Show, Loudiyi said Morocco wants to move from importing defense capacity to building its own. Le360 notes that two defense industrial zones, at Nouaceur and near Kénitra, were created by a June 2024 decree.

What It Means for US Readers

For US defense suppliers and investors, the bill is a sign of future demand rather than a purchase order. Lockheed Martin, which says its Morocco ties go back to 1974, is the main US name in the public record.

For policy watchers, the Tan-Tan event shows US forces testing equipment in Morocco, alongside the arms trade. Conversions here use the market rate of 24 October 2026, which was 9.81 per US dollar.

What Is Not Known

It is not known how much of the US$19.4 billion cap will be signed in 2027, or with which countries and companies. The bill text names no contracts.

Neither the price of the Oshkosh order nor any further US tank purchase has been confirmed. Parliament could also change the bill, and no date for the final vote was found.

What Comes Next

Parliament will now examine the 2027 Finance Bill in committee and in the House of Representatives. No dates for those steps were found.

Approval of the cap would not mean immediate spending or delivery. It would only give the defense administration legal room to sign contracts in 2027.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Morocco’s budget bill change on defense?

It raises the advance commitment limit to MAD 190.5 billion (about US$19.4 billion) from MAD 157.17 billion. The limit lets the defense minister sign multi-year equipment contracts.

Is the US$19.4 billion cap the yearly defense budget?

No, it is a ceiling on commitments paid from 2028 credits. The 2027 cash for the equipment account is MAD 11.49 billion (about US$1.2 billion).

Does this mean Morocco will buy more US weapons?

Not by itself, because the bill names no supplier. Morocco already flies F-16s, and Lockheed announced the first F-16 Block 72 flight on 6 October.

Who presented the bill, and when?

Finance Minister Fouzi Lekjaa presented it at a joint session of both houses of Parliament on Friday, 23 October 2026. The session was set for 3:00 p.m. at the House of Representatives.

When will the bill become law?

Parliament must still debate and vote on it, and no date for the final vote was found. Until then the figures are proposals.

Sources: Morocco Ministry of Economy and Finance, Finance Bill No. 60.26 for 2027, text (Arabic); Hespress (French), 23 October; Hespress (English), 23 October; Le360, breakdown of the defense budget, 23 October; Le360, analyst explainer, 24 October; Hespress (French), parliamentary calendar, 21 October; Hespress (English), US Army test plan, 18 October; Hespress (French), F-16 Block 72 first flight, 6 October; US Army statement, as published by Soldier Systems Daily, 21 October; Lockheed Martin release, 6 October; Hespress (French), Oshkosh order, October; The Defense Post, US Army Tan-Tan event, 21 October (all accessed 24 October 2026).

World.title: Who Runs Tunisia’s Economy, the Key Players in 2026
World.content:
TUNISIA · ECONOMY

Key Facts — The country Tunisia is a North African nation of about 12 million people on the Mediterranean. Its economy is a lower-middle-income one, with roughly 70% of exports going to the European Union.

— Who decides President Kais Saied sets the direction. Prime Minister Sara Zaafrani Zenzri and Finance Minister Michket Slama Khaldi run the budget and the ministries.

— Money Public debt was 82.2% of GDP in 2025. The central bank held its key rate at 7% on 7 October 2026, and inflation was 5.6% in September.

— State firms Tunisia has 111 state-owned enterprises and public bodies, many with monopolies in water, power, rail, ports and staple foods.

— Stock market The Tunis exchange was worth about 48.3 billion dinars (about US$16.1 billion) on 14 August 2026. Five companies hold 48% of that value.

— Biggest listed names BIAT, Poulina Group Holding, Attijari Bank, SFBT and Amen Bank are the five largest listed companies by market value as of August 2026.

— US link The United States imported about US$1.0 billion of goods from Tunisia in 2025 and sold it about US$590 million, a US trade deficit of about US$424 million.

The Tunisia economy is run by a small group: a president who decides, ministers who carry out his line, and state companies with monopolies. For US readers, that matters because American trade, olive oil and investors deal with the same few names.

This guide names the people, state companies, banks and family groups that matter in October 2026, and says how much each is worth.

File photo, January 2022: cargo ships at the port of Sfax, one of Tunisia’s main trading ports. (Photo: Alwaleed369, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

The Tunisia Economy in One Page

The Tunisia economy is a state-led system for about 12 million people. The president sets the direction, while a few banks and family groups hold most private capital.

President Kais Saied chaired a Council of Ministers at Carthage Palace on 13 October 2026, according to the prime minister’s website. Head of Government Sara Zaafrani Zenzri, who appears there in an item dated 23 October 2026, runs the government day to day.

Finance Minister Michket Slama Khaldi was due before parliament’s finance committee on the 2027 budget, La Presse reported on 21 October 2026. Salah Zouari, the equipment and housing minister, is also in charge of the industry, mines and energy ministry, in items dated 9 October 2026.

The numbers behind the names are modest by US standards. The World Bank says growth was 2.5% in 2025 and forecasts 2.3% in 2026, and Tunisia’s statistics office put second-quarter 2026 growth at 2.3%.

Population: about 12 million (World Bank, 2024).

Inflation: 5.6% in the year to September 2026 (national statistics office).

Unemployment: 14.9% in the second quarter of 2026 (national statistics office).

Public debt: 82.2% of GDP in 2025, down from 84.9% in 2024 (World Bank).

The Ministers and the Budget

The government’s economic line is set in short ministerial councils at the Kasbah, the prime minister’s seat. On 4 August 2026 Zenzri chaired one on the 2027 budget, where Khaldi presented the 2026 budget outcome and the 2027 outlook.

The priorities listed were protecting low-income households, reforming health and social protection, restructuring public companies and boosting investment. The 2027 plan sits inside the 2026 to 2030 development plan, which follows Saied’s guidelines.

By 21 October 2026, La Presse said the draft bill rests on three aims: food security, water security and energy security. A 23 October 2026 market digest reported that the draft sets aside 11.846 billion dinars (about US$3.9 billion) for subsidies and plans 32,557 public-sector hires.

Energy and the Private Companies Plan

On 9 October 2026 Zenzri chaired a council on energy. It set a target of 35% of electricity from renewables by 2030, the prime minister’s website says.

The next day another council backed a new model of locally run “private companies”. It said they should be steered towards strategic sectors.

The Central Bank, Debt and Reserves

In the Tunisia economy, the Central Bank of Tunisia, known as the BCT, sets the key rate and manages the dinar. Its board kept the rate at 7% on 7 October 2026 and said risks to inflation lean upward, La Presse reported on 8 October.

Energy is the pressure point. By the end of August 2026 the energy import bill reached 11.3 billion dinars (about US$3.8 billion), up from 8.8 billion dinars (about US$2.9 billion).

The current-account deficit was 4.694 billion dinars (about US$1.6 billion), or 2.5% of GDP, in the first eight months of 2026. Net foreign assets stood at 23.7 billion dinars (about US$7.9 billion) on 6 October, enough for 92 days of imports.

Tunisia repaid a 700 million euro bond (about US$784 million) in July 2026, according to the BCT’s 29 July statement. All dinar conversions here use about 3.0 dinars to the US dollar, the October 2026 rate.

State-Owned Companies and Who Controls Them

The State Department counts 111 state-owned enterprises and public bodies, citing a December 2023 finance ministry report. They compete with private firms in telecoms, banking and insurance, and hold monopolies in rail, water, electricity distribution and port logistics.

They also control imports of staples such as grain, rice, sugar, edible oil and gas. The electricity and gas utility STEG and the flag carrier Tunisair are the two best-known names.

Who Decides on Sales

Privatisation needs a government decision, and the State Department says Tunisia allows foreign bidders. Past sales covered telecoms, banking, insurance, manufacturing and fuel distribution, and sales of confiscated assets need a court order.

Budget transfers to state companies reached 9.1% of GDP in 2023, or about US$4.6 billion in total.

The State Department calls these companies heavily indebted, and lenders price them like the government.

The 2027 budget plan lists the restructuring of public companies as a priority.

File photo, November 2021: a grain silo and loading gear at the port of Sfax at sunset. (Photo: Alwaleed369, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Banks, the Real Gatekeepers of Credit

The central bank counted 29 banks in November 2024: 22 onshore and 7 offshore. Banks provide about 95% of private-sector financing, while the stock exchange supplied about 5% of corporate financing in 2024.

Onshore bank assets were about 160.7 billion dinars (about US$52 billion) in 2023, and non-performing loans were 13.6% of loans. Tourism (33.3%), farming (24.3%) and construction (24.2%) had the worst ratios, the State Department reports.

BIAT, the Biggest Listed Bank

BIAT ended 2025 with net banking income of 1.595 billion dinars (about US$531 million). Its own website shows net loans of 13.045 billion dinars (about US$4.3 billion) and deposits of 22.291 billion dinars (about US$7.4 billion).

Of the twelve listed banks, five earn 64% of the sector’s net banking income, Managers.tn reported. The first-half 2026 total was 3.786 billion dinars (about US$1.3 billion), and Amen Bank grew fastest, at 17.7%.

Attijari Bank, Amen Bank and the Rest

Attijari Bank and Amen Bank rank third and fifth by market value in August 2026. Through September 2026, BH Bank’s net banking income rose 4% and Banque de Tunisie’s rose 10.5%, a 23 October digest reported.

Listed Companies and the Stock Exchange

The stock market is the most visible part of the Tunisia economy, and Tunis has 71 listed securities, according to Managers.tn in August 2026. The main index, the Tunindex, was up 46.41% since the start of 2026 at the close on 14 August.

Total market value was 48.272 billion dinars (about US$16.1 billion) that day, Tunisie Numerique reported. The top five companies together held 23.036 billion dinars (about US$7.7 billion), or 47.72%.

Poulina, the Industrial Giant

Poulina Group Holding began as a poultry business in 1967. It now has about 9,500 employees and 11 sectors, from poultry and appliances to steel processing and packaging.

Its revenue was about 2.118 billion dinars (about US$706 million) in the first half of 2026, nearly three times BIAT’s, Managers.tn said.

On 2 March 2026 it announced a partial sale of its agri-food division on the stock exchange.

BIAT: 6.548 billion dinars (about US$2.2 billion), 13.56% of the market.

Poulina Group Holding: 4.887 billion dinars (about US$1.6 billion), 10.12%.

Attijari Bank: 4.465 billion dinars (about US$1.5 billion), 9.25%.

SFBT: 3.995 billion dinars (about US$1.3 billion), 8.28%.

Amen Bank: 3.142 billion dinars (about US$1.0 billion), 6.51%.

File photo, 2017: the headquarters of the Tunis stock exchange in the Berges du Lac district. (Photo: Ashoola, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Family Groups and Private Owners

Private power sits in a short list of family-led groups. Managers.tn ranked them by 2021 revenue in January 2023.

Poulina came first at 4.4 billion dinars (about US$1.5 billion). The Mabrouk group followed at 3.6 billion dinars (about US$1.2 billion), then the Elloumi group at 3.2 billion dinars (about US$1.1 billion).

Tunisie Telecom, UTIC, the Ben Ayed group, the Bayahi group, Leoni, Delice Holding and SFBT completed the top ten.

One Tech plans to list its cable business on the Tunis exchange in the first half of 2027. Tustex reported this on 23 October 2026.

Exports, Sectors and Foreign Money

About 70% of Tunisian exports go to the European Union, according to the US Commerce Department. The World Bank lists farming (olives, dates, cereals, citrus), component manufacturing, retail and tourism as the main sectors.

In 2025, tourism revenues rose 5.3% and remittances rose 14.9%, while the goods trade deficit widened 13.4%. Offshore firms must generally export at least 70% of output, the State Department says.

Who Invests

Foreign investment totalled US$231.1 million in the first half of 2025, up 26.1%, the investment promotion agency told the US Commerce Department. In 2024 the leading sources were France (US$207 million), Germany (US$109 million), Italy (US$98 million), Qatar (US$41 million) and the United States (US$38 million).

The IMF Gap

The International Monetary Fund projects Tunisian growth of 2.1% in 2026. Its latest full Article IV review on file dates from 2021.

File photo, March 2023: an olive tree in the countryside near Testour, northern Tunisia. (Photo: Smailtn, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons)

What It Means for US Readers

US goods trade with Tunisia is small but visible. In 2025 the United States bought about US$1.014 billion and sold about US$589.6 million, and the deficit reached US$440.7 million in January to July 2026.

Apparel, olive oil, dates, fertilizers and electronics lead US imports from Tunisia, and about 70 US firms operate in the country. The American Chamber of Commerce in Tunis has about 500 members.

Investors in Tunisian stocks or bonds face a thin reserve cushion and an energy bill that is rising. Read this alongside Tunisia’s debt and IMF position, the central bank’s October rate decision and our guide to Tunisia’s geopolitics.

For the wider picture, start at the Tunisia country page, then see Tunisia explained and the story of Tunisair’s restructuring.

What Is Not Known

No public ranking of the wealth of Tunisian families after 2021 revenues has been published, so the order of the private groups may have changed. The ownership split of the five biggest listed firms is not set out in the sources used here.

The 2027 budget figures for the deficit and growth have not been released in the sources reviewed.

Whether the president will allow any sale of a state company remains open.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who runs the Tunisia economy in 2026?

President Kais Saied sets the direction, and Prime Minister Sara Zaafrani Zenzri leads the government. Finance Minister Michket Slama Khaldi handles the budget.

What are the biggest companies in Tunisia?

By stock-market value in August 2026, they are BIAT, Poulina Group Holding, Attijari Bank, SFBT and Amen Bank. Together they hold 47.72% of the market.

How many state-owned companies does Tunisia have?

The State Department counts 111 state-owned enterprises and public bodies, citing a December 2023 finance ministry report. They dominate water, electricity, rail and port logistics.

What is the Tunisian central bank’s interest rate?

The Central Bank of Tunisia held its key rate at 7% on 7 October 2026. Inflation was 5.6% in September.

What does the Tunisia economy export?

About 70% of exports go to the European Union. To the United States, Tunisia sells mainly apparel, olive oil, dates, fertilizers and electronics.

How big is Tunisia’s public debt?

The World Bank puts public debt at 82.2% of GDP in 2025, down from 84.9% in 2024. The fiscal deficit narrowed to 5.2% of GDP in 2025.

Sources: Prime Minister of Tunisia, official website (ministerial councils, September and October 2026), 23 October 2026; La Presse, projet de loi de finances 2027, audition de la ministre des Finances, 21 October 2026; La Presse, Banque centrale de Tunisie board decision, 8 October 2026; Kapitalis, taux directeur de la BCT maintenu à 7%, 29 July 2026; National Institute of Statistics of Tunisia, October 2026; World Bank, Tunisia overview, 2026; IMF, Tunisia country page, October 2026; US State Department, 2025 Investment Climate Statement: Tunisia, 2025; US Commerce Department, Tunisia Country Commercial Guide, 26 February 2026; US Census Bureau, trade in goods with Tunisia, July 2026 data; Tunisie Numerique, Bourse de Tunis, cinq groupes concentrent 48% du marché, 17 August 2026; Managers.tn, Bourse de Tunis, les dominants dominent le marché, 17 August 2026; Managers.tn, ranking of Tunisian groups by 2021 revenue, 28 January 2023; BIAT, official website, October 2026; Poulina Group Holding, official website, 2 March 2026; Tustex, Tunisian financial news digest, 23 October 2026.

World.title: Nigeria’s Currency Ends 2.1% Lower in a Day
World.content:
NIGERIA · ECONOMY AND CURRENCY

Key Facts — What is happening Nigeria’s currency closed 2.1% lower against the US dollar on Thursday, 22 October 2026. It weakened again on Friday, 23 October.

— Why it matters Nigeria is Africa’s most populous country and a major oil producer. Its currency had been steady for weeks, so a sudden break worries investors and importers.

— The numbers The closing rate moved from 1,337 to 1,365 naira per US$1 on Thursday. Dollar trading between banks reached US$1.01 billion on Friday, up from US$316.55 million.

— Who is who The Central Bank of Nigeria regulates banks and runs the official dollar market, called the NFEM. Its official daily rate is the volume weighted average of that day’s trades.

— What to watch Monday, 26 October is the next scheduled trading day. Traders will watch whether heavy demand for dollars fades and whether the central bank comments.

— What it means for you A US dollar now buys more naira, which helps visitors. US investors in Nigerian bonds or shares see dollar returns fall, but analysts say it is too early to call a trend.

Nigeria’s currency closed 2.1% lower on Thursday, but the central bank’s official daily rate moved less. Dollar trading between banks then jumped to US$1.01 billion on Friday.

Nigeria’s currency closed 2.1% lower against the US dollar on Thursday, 22 October 2026. The naira’s closing rate went from 1,337 to 1,365 per US$1.

The naira weakened again on Friday, 23 October, as dollar trading between banks reached US$1.01 billion, central bank data show. For US investors, travellers and firms with Nigerian exposure, the move changes what a dollar buys.

What Happened to Nigeria’s Currency on Thursday and Friday

Central Bank of Nigeria data show the naira closing at 1,365 per US$1 on Thursday, up from 1,337 on Wednesday, 21 October. It traded between 1,336 and 1,369 during the session.

The official daily rate, a volume weighted average, rose less, from 1,334.72 to 1,344.40 naira per US$1, or about 0.7%. The closing rate captures the late jump, while the average blends the whole day.

On Friday the official rate weakened by 17.44 to 1,361.84 naira per US$1, about 1.3%, as BusinessDay also reports. The closing rate was 1,370, which Vanguard reports, and trading ranged from 1,340 to 1,395.

The Friday figures that look different are two measures from the same central bank data. The official rate is the weighted average, and the closing rate is the last trade of the day.

Nairametrics says Thursday’s move of 28 naira per US$1 was the largest closing fall since 9 April 2025, when it was 29. The months in between could not be checked, so the comparison is Nairametrics’ own.

Central bank closing rates stayed between 1,329.50 and 1,337 naira per US$1 from 29 September to 21 October. Thursday’s move therefore broke a band that had held for most of October.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Nigeria economy Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Record Dollar Trading at the Official Market

Central bank data show trading between banks reached US$1.01 billion on Friday, up from US$316.55 million on Thursday. Deals rose from 181 to 315, and BusinessDay and Vanguard put the jump at 219%.

BusinessDay calls the Friday figure a record, but the central bank data opened for this report cover only about four weeks. Nairametrics says total market turnover, a wider measure, also passed US$1 billion on 6 October.

The informal street market weakened too, but outlets disagree on the level. BusinessDay gives 1,385 naira per US$1 and Vanguard gives 1,367, and neither is a central bank figure.

What the Central Bank Did

BusinessDay cites market information that the central bank sold US$150 million on Wednesday and US$300 million on Thursday. No central bank confirmation of these sales or comment on the fall was found.

External reserves, the foreign currency the central bank holds, stood at US$55.16 billion on 22 October, BusinessDay says. That is 28.67% above the US$42.87 billion of a year earlier.

Nairametrics says dealers’ association data showed dollar demand hit a 15 year high of US$18.34 billion in the second quarter of 2026. It adds that the daily data alone does not establish what caused Thursday’s fall.

Why Analysts Say It Is Too Early to Call a Trend

Ayodeji Ebo, chief executive of MDU Capital, said two days of data cannot show that foreign investors are leaving. He pointed to possible one off deals, import payments or profit taking after lower yields.

Ayokunle Olubunmi of Agusto and Co and Muda Yusuf of the Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise also want more data. Vanguard says Cowry Asset Management expects the naira to stay under pressure amid persistent dollar demand.

In Plain English

The naira (about US$0.0007 each) is Nigeria’s currency. The Central Bank of Nigeria regulates banks and runs the official dollar market, called the NFEM.

At 1,361.84 naira per US$1, US$100 buys about 136,184 naira. A higher number means a weaker naira.

The closing rate is the last price of the day, while the official rate is the day’s volume weighted average. Interbank turnover is the value of dollars that banks trade with each other.

What It Means for US Readers

A weaker naira means a US dollar buys more in Nigeria, which helps visitors and anyone sending dollars to relatives. It hurts Nigerians who earn in naira but pay for imports or debts in dollars.

US investors in Nigerian bonds, shares or naira funds see their dollar returns fall when the naira drops. Nothing in the reports says foreign investors have left.

Foreign companies that earn in naira report smaller dollar profits when the currency weakens. None of the reports names a US company affected on Thursday or Friday.

Nigeria is a major oil producer, but none of the reports links this move to oil prices. The naira therefore matters to US readers mainly through investment, remittances and trade.

What Is Not Known

The cause of Thursday’s fall is not established. Analysts quoted by BusinessDay name one off deals, import payments or profit taking, and none confirms that foreign investors are selling.

The largest fall since April 2025 and the record trading label each come from one outlet, Nairametrics and BusinessDay. The central bank data opened for this report cover only about four weeks, so neither could be checked.

The central bank dollar sales are unconfirmed market information. Outlets also give street rates of 1,385 and 1,367 naira per US$1, and no central bank comment was found.

Nairametrics prints Thursday’s interbank turnover as 316.55 million naira, but central bank data show US$316.55 million. The dollar figure is used here.

What Comes Next

The next scheduled trading day at the official market is Monday, 26 October. Traders will watch whether dollar demand stays heavy and whether the central bank comments.

A second heavy day of dollar demand would strengthen the case for a trend. Nobody has yet announced a policy change in response.

Frequently Asked Questions

What happened to Nigeria’s currency this week?

Nigeria’s currency closed 2.1% lower against the US dollar on Thursday, 22 October 2026, at 1,365 naira per US$1. It weakened again on Friday, 23 October.

How weak is the naira against the US dollar?

On Friday the official rate was 1,361.84 naira per US$1, the day’s weighted average, and the close was 1,370. Thursday’s close was 1,365.

What is the official market for dollars in Nigeria?

It is the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, or NFEM, which the Central Bank of Nigeria runs. Banks trade dollars with each other there, and the rate it sets is the official rate.

Did the central bank sell dollars to defend the naira?

BusinessDay cites market information that it sold US$150 million on Wednesday and US$300 million on Thursday. No central bank confirmation was found.

What does a weaker naira mean for US travellers?

Each US dollar buys more naira, so prices in Nigeria look lower in dollar terms. The effect depends on which rate is used, because official and street rates differ.

Sources: Central Bank of Nigeria NFEM exchange rate data, accessed 24 October 2026; BusinessDay, 23 October 2026; Nairametrics, 23 October 2026; Vanguard, 23 October 2026; Nairametrics, 8 October 2026. Rates come from the central bank data feed behind its rates page.

World.title: Pretoria Says City Centre Tap Water Is Safe
World.content:
SOUTH AFRICA · GOVERNMENT

Key Facts — What is happening On Saturday 24 October 2026 the City of Tshwane lifted its boil water advisory for central Pretoria. It says new tests found no E. coli.

— Why it matters Pretoria is South Africa’s administrative capital, home to the presidency and embassies. A separate outbreak in the same metropolitan area is under parliamentary and criminal scrutiny.

— The numbers The advisory covered 22 areas for about two days from Thursday 22 October. In Bronkhorstspruit, 595 people fell ill between 7 and 19 October, including 262 children under five.

— Who is who Executive Mayor Nasiphi Moya leads the City of Tshwane, which runs water in Pretoria. The national Department of Water and Sanitation oversees drinking water quality.

— What to watch The city must repair the Groenkloof sewer pipe and flush the Findlay line. Tshwane voters choose councils in The city must repair the Groenkloof sewer pipe and flush the Findlay line. Tshwane voters choose councils in local elections on Wednesday 4 November

— What it means for you Visitors in central Pretoria can use tap water again, including Arcadia, home to the US Embassy address. Bronkhorstspruit tap water is still unsafe.

Pretoria tap water is safe to drink again in the city centre, the City of Tshwane says. The all clear came on Saturday 24 October, two days after a sewage scare.

The City of Tshwane says Pretoria tap water is safe to drink again in the city centre of South Africa’s administrative capital. It lifted a boil water advisory on Saturday 24 October 2026 after new tests found no E. coli.

The order covered 22 areas around the centre, including Arcadia, the suburb where the United States Embassy has its address. For US readers it matters because the capital hosts American diplomats, and a separate outbreak runs nearby.

Why Pretoria Tap Water Was Under Warning

Tests on Wednesday 21 October found microbial contamination in Findlay Reservoir water, the city said in a statement on Thursday 22 October. The reservoir supplies the city centre and the neighbourhoods around it.

The city blamed a burst sewer pipe that let polluted water enter the network, beyond what chlorine could handle. Chlorine is the disinfectant that utilities add to tap water to kill germs.

It isolated the source, emptied the reservoir and switched the affected areas to the Salvokop Reservoir. Residents were told to boil water for one minute, throw away stored water and ice, and expect tankers.

The city said tanker locations would be announced later. Areas on the list included Pretoria Central, Arcadia, Sunnyside, Marabastad, Prinshof and Trevenna.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How the City Cleared the Water

On Saturday the city said its latest tests found no E. coli and no total coliform bacteria. Total coliforms are a wider group of bacteria that can point to contamination.

Technical teams cleaned the Findlay Reservoir and applied a chlorine shock treatment to the pipe network, the city said. Residents may now use tap water without boiling it.

The city links the contamination to groundwater from the Fountains springs and a damaged sewer pipe in Groenkloof. Repairs on that pipe continue, and groundwater will return to the line only after tests and flushing.

The Mayor’s Apology and the Warning Delay

Mayor Nasiphi Moya apologised on Saturday and said the delay in communicating the first advisory was unacceptable. The reports do not say how long that delay lasted.

She promised an independent investigation into the contamination, any negligence and why residents were not warned on time. Where failures are established, she said, corrective action and consequence management will follow.

A Second Water Crisis in Tshwane

The city says the Pretoria incident is separate from the Bronkhorstspruit crisis in the same metropolitan area. On Friday 23 October, Health Minister Aaron Motsoaledi told Parliament that 595 people there fell ill between 7 and 19 October.

Of those, 262 were children under five, and no deaths were reported. Officials said the Bronkhorstspruit plant ran without chlorine for about three weeks until 14 October.

Deputy Minister David Mahlobo told MPs the Water and Sanitation Department opened a criminal case against the city on 18 October. The department alleges failure to provide information or misleading information, and the mayor says the city will cooperate fully.

Bronkhorstspruit tap water remains unsafe to drink, and about 36 tankers carry water from tested hydrants. The Public Protector is investigating, and the EFF demanded on Saturday that the mayor resign.

In Plain English Boil water advisory: an official warning to boil tap water for one minute before use.

an official warning to boil tap water for one minute before use. E. coli: a bacterium in the gut whose presence in water signals sewage contamination.

a bacterium in the gut whose presence in water signals sewage contamination. Reservoir: a tank that stores treated water before it flows to homes.

a tank that stores treated water before it flows to homes. Chlorine: the disinfectant that kills germs in tap water.

the disinfectant that kills germs in tap water. Public Protector: a state office that investigates maladministration by officials.

a state office that investigates maladministration by officials. EFF: the Economic Freedom Fighters, an opposition party in Parliament.

What It Means for US Readers

The United States Embassy is at 877 Pretorius Street in Arcadia, one of the 22 areas that was under the advisory. No embassy notice about the water had been located by Saturday afternoon.

Visitors to central Pretoria can use tap water again, though some may still choose bottled water. Anyone heading to Bronkhorstspruit and nearby communities should still avoid tap water.

The EFF is demanding the mayor’s resignation days before Tshwane votes in local elections on Wednesday 4 November. The Freedom Front Plus has also asked the Public Protector to investigate the city.

What Is Not Known

The city’s own notice lifting the advisory could not be opened, so this account rests on three outlets that quote it. They agree on the main points.

The city blames a sewer pipe and groundwater. Officials told Parliament that a 21 October inspection found no chlorine disinfection at Findlay Reservoir.

Test dates, sample numbers and the laboratory were not given, and nobody has said whether Findlay water made anyone ill. Illness reports link only to Bronkhorstspruit.

Case counts there were 408 for 7 to 18 October and 595 for 7 to 19 October. No source explains the one day jump.

The Water and Sanitation Department gives 18 October for its criminal case. The EFF says it has opened a separate criminal case against the mayor.

What Comes Next

The city must finish the Groenkloof sewer repairs and flush the pipeline to Findlay Reservoir before groundwater is used again. Routine monitoring of the water will continue.

The Public Protector’s next step on Bronkhorstspruit is to ask the city manager for a formal response. Voters in Tshwane choose their councils on Wednesday 4 November.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Pretoria tap water safe to drink now?

The City of Tshwane says yes for the city centre and nearby areas served by Findlay Reservoir. Its latest tests found no E. coli or total coliform bacteria.

Which areas were under the boil water order?

The advisory covered 22 areas, including Pretoria Central, Arcadia, Sunnyside, Marabastad and Prinshof. The city issued it on Thursday 22 October.

Is this linked to the Bronkhorstspruit outbreak?

The city says no and calls the two incidents separate. Tap water in Bronkhorstspruit remains unsafe, and residents there rely on tanker water.

What caused the contamination?

The city points to a burst or damaged sewer pipe that let polluted groundwater from the Fountains springs into the supply. Officials told Parliament that a 21 October inspection found no chlorine disinfection at the reservoir.

Should visitors to Pretoria worry about the water?

Not in the city centre now, according to the city, though the order lasted two days. Visitors to Bronkhorstspruit and nearby communities should avoid tap water.

World.title: Valterra Platinum Output Falls 6% in Quarter
World.content:
SOUTH AFRICA · MINING

Key Facts — What is happening Valterra Platinum, the JSE-listed South African miner that Anglo American spun off in 2025, said on Friday, 23 October 2026, that third-quarter platinum group metals output fell 6% to 804,300 ounces.

— Why it matters Platinum group metals clean car exhaust and serve hydrogen equipment, so a 6% fall at a major producer matters to buyers, although the company kept its full-year production target unchanged.

— The numbers Own-mined output was 511,900 ounces (down 5%), refined output 576,900 ounces (down 41%), and the average price R38,815 per ounce (US$2,383), up 24% in dollars from a year earlier.

— Who is who Craig Miller is chief executive of Valterra Platinum; Amandelbult and Mogalakwena are its two largest mines this quarter, and Tharisa plc is a platinum and chrome miner that will sell it concentrate.

— What to watch Valterra expects Amandelbult output to step up in the fourth quarter, and its fourth-quarter report will show whether 2026 lands inside the 3.0 to 3.4 million ounce target.

— What it means for you US car and hydrogen industries use these metals, yet no source says this quarter changes US prices or supply, and the company held its 2026 guidance.

South Africa’s Valterra Platinum mined 6% less metal in the third quarter after safety stoppages. It kept its full-year target, and its prices rose.

Valterra Platinum, listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE), said on Friday, 23 October 2026, that output fell 6% in the quarter. Production reached 804,300 ounces in the three months to 30 September, and Business Day puts the year-earlier figure at 855,100 ounces.

Platinum group metals, or PGMs, are rare metals used in car exhaust systems, hydrogen equipment and electronics. The company kept its 2026 target of 3.0 to 3.4 million ounces, so Friday’s report leaves its yearly outlook unchanged.

What Valterra Platinum Reported on Friday

The company published its production report for the quarter ending 30 September 2026 at 08:10 South African time on Friday. The figures cover its own mines and the ore concentrate it buys from other miners.

Own-mined output was 511,900 ounces, down 5%, mainly because of safety stoppages at the Amandelbult mine. Purchases of concentrate from other producers fell 7% to 292,400 ounces.

Business Day carried the same totals on Friday. Mining Weekly added that iridium and ruthenium, two smaller PGMs, kept outperforming the main metals.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on South Africa markets Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Refined Output Fell 41%

Refined output, which excludes metal processed for others under tolling contracts, fell 41% to 576,900 ounces. The company says planned processing maintenance and annual stock counts moved from the first quarter into the third.

Nine-month refined output was broadly in line with last year, which supports that timing explanation. Sales volumes fell 27% to 683,300 ounces, and Business Day says they were partly supported by drawing down refined stock.

Nine-month sales matched the same period of 2025. Nickel output fell 39% to 3,825 tonnes and copper fell 22% to 3,294 tonnes, while chrome concentrate rose 7% to 277,000 tonnes.

In Plain English PGMs are six rare metals led by platinum and palladium, and this report’s total adds gold to five of them. The basket price is the average price Valterra received per ounce across all the metals it sold.

Mine by Mine, Safety Stoppages Weigh Most

Amandelbult produced 137,900 ounces, down 10%, after Section 54 regulatory safety stoppages and the company’s own stoppages across the mine. One worker died in a fall-of-ground incident at Tumela, part of Amandelbult, in July.

Output returned to steady state by quarter end, and the company expects a step-up in the fourth quarter. Mogalakwena, in Limpopo province, made 217,600 ounces, down 4%, after a lease on its Baobab concentrator expired.

Mototolo rose 7% to 70,800 ounces, while Unki in Zimbabwe fell 12% to 50,600 ounces on lower ore grades. Modikwa, where Valterra counts a 50% share, fell 5% to 35,000 ounces.

Prices, Costs and the Tharisa Deal

The average realised price was R38,815 per ounce (US$2,383), up 15% in rand and 24% in dollars from a year earlier. Mining Weekly says prices of the main metals eased from the second quarter amid weaker car sales and economic worries.

Mining Weekly gives Valterra’s realised iridium price at US$7,720 an ounce, against US$4,287 a year earlier, and ruthenium at US$1,583, against US$799. It links the rise to tight iridium supply and demand from green hydrogen, electronics and data centres.

Cash costs are expected near the top of R19,000 to R20,000 per ounce (about US$1,146 to US$1,206). The company blames fuel, chemical and blasting inflation linked to the Middle East conflict, plus the stoppages.

Valterra signed two new concentrate purchase agreements with Tharisa plc, which it says improve margins on third-party processing. Business Day says the binding multiyear deal starts on 1 January 2027, covers half of Tharisa Mine’s PGM concentrate and replaces Sibanye-Stillwater.

What It Means for US Readers

Platinum, palladium and rhodium clean vehicle exhaust, and iridium goes into hydrogen electrolysers that US developers buy. No source says Valterra’s quarter changes prices or supply in the United States.

For US investors, this is an operating update, not a profit result, and guidance was held. Sibanye-Stillwater, which trades in New York and mines in Montana, is the buyer Business Day says Valterra replaces at Tharisa.

Multiplying 683,300 ounces by the US$2,383 basket price gives roughly US$1.6 billion, simple arithmetic and not a company figure. Visitors and residents face no direct effect, since the report concerns mine output and company costs.

What Is Not Known

The production report as read gives no quarterly revenue, profit or dividend figure. It also gives its safety injury rate twice with different values, 1.45 and 1.41 per million hours, so this article uses neither.

The size of the fourth-quarter step-up at Amandelbult is not stated. The start date and share of the Tharisa agreement come from Business Day, not from the company’s report.

Neither the company nor the outlets say what the Tharisa change means for Sibanye-Stillwater’s earnings. No source gives Valterra’s sales to US customers or its exposure to US tariffs.

What Comes Next

Valterra says production remains on track for its 2026 range, and its fourth-quarter report will show whether Amandelbult recovers as promised. No release date for that report appears in the sources read.

The Tharisa agreement is due to start on 1 January 2027, Business Day says. The company says outside safety specialists are reviewing its practices, and Mining Weekly quotes Miller saying recommendations are being implemented.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Valterra Platinum?

It is a South African miner of platinum group metals listed on the JSE, spun off from Anglo American in 2025. Craig Miller is its chief executive.

How much did Valterra Platinum produce in the third quarter?

Total PGM output was 804,300 ounces, down 6%. Own mines made 511,900 ounces and purchased concentrate added 292,400 ounces.

Why did refined output fall 41%?

The company says planned processing maintenance and annual stock counts moved from the first quarter to the third. Nine-month refined output was broadly in line with last year.

Did Valterra Platinum cut its 2026 target?

No, it kept production guidance at 3.0 to 3.4 million ounces. It expects unit costs near the top of its R19,000 to R20,000 range (about US$1,146 to US$1,206).

Why does this matter to US readers?

US carmakers and hydrogen developers use platinum group metals, and New York-listed Sibanye-Stillwater is named in the Tharisa deal. No source says US prices or supply change.

Sources: Valterra Platinum, production report for the third quarter ending 30 September 2026, 23 October 2026; Business Day, 23 October 2026; Mining Weekly, 23 October 2026; Valterra Platinum announcements list (demerger 2 June 2025); Valterra Platinum company profile. Rand conversions use the company’s own US$2,383 for the basket price and open.er-api.com, 24 October 2026, ZAR 16.58 per US$, for the cost range (all accessed 24 October 2026).

World.title: Belize marks United Nations Day, celebrates work of 22 UN agencies
World.content:
Belize marks United Nations Day, celebrates work of 22 UN agencies

By Zoila Palma: Belize joins the international community today in commemorating United Nations Day, marking the 81st anniversary of the global organization.

The occasion highlights the work of 22 United Nations agencies operating in Belize, 12 of which are based in the country, supporting development initiatives in partnership with the Government, civil society and local communities.

United Nations Day commemorates the entry into force of the UN Charter on October 24, 1945, which officially established the organization.

The annual observance provides an opportunity to reaffirm the principles of peace, international cooperation, equality and sustainable development that guide the United Nations in its efforts to address global challenges and promote a better future for all.

In Belize, the work of UN agencies and their partners focuses on creating opportunities for people and building a more inclusive, resilient and sustainable country.

This year’s observance also highlights the importance of collaboration in advancing human dignity and ensuring that no one is left behind.

Special Envoy Rossana Briceno said the day celebrates the power of unity, peace and international cooperation, encouraging renewed commitment to equality and sustainable development.

World.title: International News: France deploys 70,000 police as demonstrations continue over cost of living
World.content:
International News: France deploys 70,000 police as demonstrations continue over cost of living

By Zoila Palma: Thousands of demonstrators gathered in Paris and other French cities today as authorities deployed 70,000 police officers to prevent a repeat of the riots and looting that swept across the country the previous weekend, Reuters report.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 135 people had been arrested nationwide by early afternoon, with some arrests following searches that uncovered fireworks, ball bearings and other items that could be used as weapons.

The heightened security measures included the deployment of 10,000 additional police officers and gendarmes compared with October 17, when protests over the cost of living and deteriorating public services escalated into some of France’s worst unrest in years.

While the main demonstration in Paris began peacefully, police fired tear gas at crowds in Lyon, the country’s third-largest city. Nunez warned that authorities faced significant calls for disruption from political groups and criminals.

Much of central Paris took on the appearance of a city under lockdown, with businesses boarding up storefronts, major cultural institutions closing and more than 20 metro stations shutting down.

World.title: International News: El Salvador’s President on rescue mission in Haiti: “God will grant us victory”
World.content:
International News: El Salvador’s President on rescue mission in Haiti: “God will grant us victory”

By Zoila Palma: President of El Salvador Nayib Bukele says that the Salvadoran army has launched a rescue mission to rescue four Salvadoran members of an international, United Nations-backed security force who are reportedly being held hostage by armed gangs in Haiti.

The four Salvadorans went missing on Sunday after jumping from a burning armored vehicle that was ambushed by armed gangs on the outskirts of Haiti’s capital while they were returning from a market to their base, according to security officials.

Bukele says that there are many messages and analysis claiming that the gangs in Haiti are not like those in El Salvador—”that they are bloodthirsty, heavily armed, and unconquerable; that all previous missions have failed; that we are walking into a trap; that we do not know what we are facing; that this will be our ruin; and that we are heading toward our own Waterloo.”

Bukele says that God will grant victory to the Salvadoran army.

“But when God grants us victory, those same people who are saying all this today will change their tune. They will claim that it was always easy, that anyone could have done it, and that the gangs in Haiti were never as dangerous as people thought.

In any case, we have never listened to them, and we are not going to start now.

Everyone who has enlisted is a believer, and we have entrusted this mission to God—whereas the gangs in Haiti are satanic, and it is common knowledge that they perform human sacrifices,” Bukele asserted.

“The Creator of the Universe is with us,” he said.

World.title: National Evangelical Association of Belize “aggrieved” by charges against Pastor Tzib; pray for justice
World.content:
National Evangelical Association of Belize “aggrieved” by charges against Pastor Tzib; pray for justice

By Zoila Palma: On October 23, 2026, the National Evangelical Association of Belize (NEAB) issued a statement saying that it is aggrieved by the terrible situation resulting in charges against a church Pastor.

“Churches must have structures and guidelines that prevent such occurrences and create a culture in the Church that disallows these areas of abuse.

Abuse situations like this are alarming and shameful to the Church as a whole, going against everything that the Word of God teaches about spiritual leaders and God’s standards of holiness and leadership integrity. The young victims affected are in our prayers, and some of our leaders have already reached out to help with counselling ministry,” NEAB said.

NEAB says that the Court and the Law will process this legally, determining guilt and consequences.

“We pray for justice for the victims in this situation, as well as healing,” NEAB said.

NEAB added that victims have stated that they brought complaints to the leadership as far back as five years ago, and these were dismissed, no action was taken.

“If confirmed, this was a major breach of Kingdom of God and organizational protocols, which then allowed the alleged abuse to continue, affecting more people. We urge all Pastors, Churches and Ministries that when complaints of sexual impropriety are brought to a Leadership Team, they must be taken very seriously and acted on swiftly. When we fail in this area, we fail of that sacred duty of leadership in the Kingdom of God,” the association said.

NEAB urged victims to report to the police because when criminal lines are crossed, it requires a criminal investigation.

The association says that this should provoke discussions and leadership meetings in every church, with sincere hearted analysis and identifying areas of weakness.
